title: Optimal Work Extraction From Finite-time Closed Quantum Dynamics
authors: Shoki Sugimoto, Takahiro Sagawa, And Ryusuke Hamazaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shoki Sugimoto, Takahiro Sagawa, and Ryusuke Hamazaki

Extracting useful work from quantum systems is a fundamental problem in quantum thermodynamics. In scenarios where rapid protocols are desired—whether due to practical constraints or deliberate design choices—a fundamental trade-off between power and efficiency is yet to be established. Here, we inv…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023321] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives fundamental bounds on work extraction from finite-time closed quantum dynamics, establishing a trade-off between power and efficiency.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental limits of work extraction in quantum systems is crucial for designing quantum heat engines and quantum batteries, especially when rapid protocols are required.
method: The authors use quantum thermodynamic principles and optimal control theory to analyze work extraction from closed quantum systems undergoing finite-time unitary evolution.
result: They derive a general bound relating the extracted work, the duration of the protocol, and the quantum speed limit, showing that faster protocols inevitably reduce the amount of extractable work.
conclusion: The work provides a fundamental trade-off between power and efficiency in quantum thermodynamics, with implications for the design of fast quantum thermal machines.

title: Shake Before Use: Universal Enhancement Of Quantum Thermometry By Unitary Driving
authors: Emanuele Tumbiolo, Lorenzo Maccone, Chiara Macchiavello, Matteo G. A. Paris, And Giacomo Guarnieri
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuele Tumbiolo, Lorenzo Maccone, Chiara Macchiavello, Matteo G. A. Paris, and Giacomo Guarnieri

Quantum thermometry aims at determining temperature with ultimate precision in the quantum regime. Standard equilibrium approaches, limited by the quantum Fisher information given by static energy fluctuations, lose sensitivity outside a fixed temperature window. Nonequilibrium strategies have there…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250401] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Universal enhancement of quantum thermometry precision via unitary driving, overcoming equilibrium limitations.
motivation: Standard equilibrium quantum thermometry loses sensitivity outside a fixed temperature window; nonequilibrium strategies can potentially improve precision.
method: The authors propose a universal unitary driving protocol that enhances the quantum Fisher information for temperature estimation, applicable to any quantum probe.
result: The protocol achieves a significant increase in thermometric precision across a wide temperature range, independent of the specific system details.
conclusion: Unitary driving provides a practical and universal method to boost quantum thermometry performance, with implications for quantum sensing and thermodynamics.

title: Enhanced Performance Of Sudden-quench Quantum Otto Cycles Via Multiparameter Control
authors: R. S. Watson And K. V. Kheruntsyan
abstract:
Author(s): R. S. Watson and K. V. Kheruntsyan

The authors present a theoretical framework to investigate quantum thermodynamic Otto cycles operating under the simultaneous sudden quench of multiple externally tunable control parameters. Applying this formalism to both a harmonically trapped one-dimensional Bose gas and the transverse-field Ising model, they demonstrate that multiparameter control yields a significant cooperative enhancement to net work and efficiency, dramatically outperforming the combined output of individual single-parameter cycles.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063319] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a theoretical framework for quantum Otto cycles with multiparameter sudden quenches, showing cooperative enhancement of work and efficiency in a Bose gas and the Ising model.
motivation: To explore whether simultaneously quenching multiple control parameters can improve the performance of quantum heat engines beyond single-parameter cycles.
method: The authors formulate a general framework for sudden-quench quantum Otto cycles with multiple parameters and apply it to a harmonically trapped 1D Bose gas and the transverse-field Ising model, computing work output and efficiency.
result: Multiparameter control yields a cooperative enhancement that significantly outperforms the sum of individual single-parameter cycles in both net work and efficiency.
conclusion: Multiparameter sudden quenches offer a promising route to boost quantum thermodynamic cycle performance, with potential applications in quantum thermal machines.

title: Universal Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation For Quantum $f$ Divergences
authors: Domingos S. P. Salazar
abstract:
Author(s): Domingos S. P. Salazar

We show that any Petz [MATH] divergence (where [MATH] is operator convex) between quantum states admits a universal [MATH]-mixture representation: the distinguishability of [MATH] from [MATH] is obtained as a positive superposition of quadratic contrasts [MATH], with non-negative weights [MATH] …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064150] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives a universal thermodynamic uncertainty relation for quantum f-divergences, linking distinguishability to thermodynamic cost.
motivation: Thermodynamic uncertainty relations (TURs) bound the precision of observables by entropy production, but existing results are limited to specific divergences. This work aims to unify and generalize TURs for a broad class of quantum divergences.
method: The author shows that any Petz f-divergence (with operator convex f) can be expressed as a mixture of quadratic contrasts, and then uses this representation to derive a universal TUR that holds for all such divergences.
result: A universal TUR is obtained: the distinguishability measured by any Petz f-divergence is bounded by the thermodynamic cost (e.g., entropy production) times a factor depending on f. This generalizes known TURs for the quantum relative entropy and chi-squared divergence.
conclusion: The result provides a unified framework for thermodynamic uncertainty relations in quantum systems, with potential applications to quantum metrology and thermodynamics of information.

title: Autonomous Quantum Thermodynamics With A Quantum Kicked Top Reservoir
authors: Chun-Yan Kang, Zhi-Ren Pu, And You-Yang Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Chun-Yan Kang, Zhi-Ren Pu, and You-Yang Xu

We develop an operational framework to characterize energy exchange between a quantum system and a finite, dynamically tunable environment modeled by a quantum kicked top. Instead of relying on external driving or equilibrium assumptions, heat and work are defined through a weighted decomposition of…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064137] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: An operational framework for autonomous quantum thermodynamics using a quantum kicked top as a finite, tunable reservoir.
motivation: To understand energy exchange between a quantum system and a finite environment without external driving or equilibrium assumptions.
method: Heat and work are defined via a weighted decomposition of the system-reservoir interaction, using the kicked top's dynamics to control the reservoir.
result: The framework yields well-defined thermodynamic quantities and demonstrates non-equilibrium behavior distinct from standard thermal baths.
conclusion: The quantum kicked top provides a versatile model for studying autonomous quantum thermodynamics in finite, controllable environments.

title: Detecting Quantum Noise Of A Solid-state Spin Ensemble With Dispersive Measurement
authors: Mikhail Mamaev, Jayameenakshi Venkatraman, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Mikhail Mamaev, Jayameenakshi Venkatraman, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich, and Aashish A. Clerk

We theoretically explore protocols for measuring the spin polarization of an ensemble of solid-state spins, with precision at or below the standard quantum limit. Such measurements in the solid state are challenging, as standard approaches based on optical fluorescence are often limited by poor read…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023331] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes dispersive measurement protocols to detect spin polarization of solid-state spin ensembles with precision at or below the standard quantum limit.
motivation: Solid-state spin ensembles are promising for quantum memories and sensors, but measuring their polarization with high precision is challenging due to poor optical readout efficiency.
method: The authors theoretically analyze dispersive measurement schemes using cavity or circuit QED techniques, modeling the spin ensemble as a collective spin coupled to a readout resonator.
result: They show that dispersive measurements can achieve spin polarization sensitivity below the standard quantum limit, and characterize the effects of inhomogeneous broadening and other noise sources.
conclusion: Dispersive measurement is a viable route for high-precision spin ensemble readout in solid-state platforms, enabling applications in quantum sensing and quantum information processing.

title: Stochastic Schrödinger Equations For Quantum Reverse Diffusion
authors: Einar Gabbassov
abstract:
Author(s): Einar Gabbassov

The ensemble-averaged dynamics of open quantum systems are typically irreversible. We show that this irreversibility need not hold at the level of individually monitored quantum trajectories. Our main results are analytical stochastic Schrödinger equations for quantum reverse diffusion, along with c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023329] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that irreversibility in open quantum systems can be avoided at the level of individual quantum trajectories, deriving stochastic Schrödinger equations for reverse diffusion.
motivation: To understand whether the irreversibility of ensemble-averaged open quantum dynamics is fundamental or can be circumvented by monitoring individual trajectories.
method: Analytical derivation of stochastic Schrödinger equations that describe reverse diffusion of quantum trajectories, using tools from quantum filtering and stochastic calculus.
result: Explicit stochastic differential equations for reverse-time dynamics of monitored quantum systems, demonstrating that individual trajectories can be time-reversible.
conclusion: Irreversibility in open quantum systems is not inherent at the trajectory level, offering new insights into the thermodynamics of quantum information processing and potential applications in quantum control.

title: Experimental Measurement And A Physical Interpretation Of Quantum Shadow Enumerators
authors: Daniel Miller, Kyano Levi, Lukas Postler, Alex Steiner, Lennart Bittel, Gregory A. L. White, Yifan Tang, Eric J. Kuehnke, Antonio A. Mele, Sumeet Khatri, Lorenzo Leone, Jose Carrasco, Christian D. Marciniak, Ivan Pogorelov, Milena Guevara-Bertsch, Robert Freund, Rainer Blatt, Philipp Schindler, Thomas Monz, Martin Ringbauer, And Jens Eisert
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Miller, Kyano Levi, Lukas Postler, Alex Steiner, Lennart Bittel, Gregory A. L. White, Yifan Tang, Eric J. Kuehnke, Antonio A. Mele, Sumeet Khatri, Lorenzo Leone, Jose Carrasco, Christian D. Marciniak, Ivan Pogorelov, Milena Guevara-Bertsch, Robert Freund, Rainer Blatt, Philipp Schindler, Thomas Monz, Martin Ringbauer, and Jens Eisert

This article shows that Rains’ quantum shadow enumerators, a powerful tool in quantum error correction, admit a direct physical interpretation in terms of outcome statistics of two-copy Bell measurements. This connection enables efficient learning protocols for these quantities and is demonstrated experimentally on a trapped-ion quantum device.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023318] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a physical interpretation of quantum shadow enumerators in terms of two-copy Bell measurements and demonstrates their efficient experimental measurement on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
motivation: Quantum shadow enumerators are powerful tools for analyzing quantum error-correcting codes, but they lacked a direct physical interpretation and efficient measurement protocol.
method: The authors show that Rains' quantum shadow enumerators correspond to outcome statistics of two-copy Bell measurements, enabling a learning protocol that is implemented on a trapped-ion device.
result: They experimentally measure shadow enumerators for small error-correcting codes, validating the theoretical connection and demonstrating the efficiency of the protocol.
conclusion: This work bridges a gap between abstract enumerator theory and experimental quantum error correction, providing a practical tool for characterizing code performance.

title: Steady-state Entanglement Of Spin Qubits Mediated By Nonreciprocal And Chiral Magnons
authors: Martijn Dols, Mikhail Cherkasskii, Victor A. S. V. Bittencourt, Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero, Durga B. R. Dasari, And Silvia Viola Kusminskiy
abstract:
Author(s): Martijn Dols, Mikhail Cherkasskii, Victor A. S. V. Bittencourt, Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero, Durga B. R. Dasari, and Silvia Viola Kusminskiy

We propose a hybrid quantum system in which a magnet supporting nonreciprocal magnons, chiral magnons, or both mediates the dissipative and unidirectional coupling of spin qubits. By driving the qubits, the steady state of this qubit-qubit coupling scheme becomes the maximally entangled Bell state. …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023310] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid quantum system where nonreciprocal or chiral magnons mediate dissipative coupling of spin qubits to generate steady-state Bell entanglement.
motivation: To achieve deterministic entanglement of spin qubits without fine-tuning, using magnon-mediated interactions in a magnet-qubit hybrid platform.
method: Theoretical analysis of a hybrid system coupling spin qubits to a magnet supporting nonreciprocal/chiral magnons, with qubit driving to engineer dissipative dynamics.
result: The steady state of the qubit-qubit coupling scheme becomes the maximally entangled Bell state, enabled by the nonreciprocal magnon-mediated interaction.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a viable route to generate robust entanglement in hybrid quantum systems using chiral magnons, relevant for quantum networking and information processing.

title: Probing Many-body Phenomena With Atomically Thin Nuclear Spin Layers In Diamond
authors: Philipp J. Vetter, Christoph Findler, Antonio Verdú, Matthias Kost, Rémi Blinder, Jens Fuhrmann, Christian Osterkamp, Johannes Lang, Martin B. Plenio, Javier Prior, And Fedor Jelezko
abstract:
Author(s): Philipp J. Vetter, Christoph Findler, Antonio Verdú, Matthias Kost, Rémi Blinder, Jens Fuhrmann, Christian Osterkamp, Johannes Lang, Martin B. Plenio, Javier Prior, and Fedor Jelezko

Quantum simulation aims to recreate complex many-body phenomena in controlled environments, offering insights into dynamics that are otherwise difficult to model. Existing platforms, however, are often complex and costly to scale, typically requiring ultrapure vacuum or low temperatures. Here, we in…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023304] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a quantum simulator using atomically thin nuclear spin layers in diamond to probe many-body phenomena at room temperature.
motivation: Existing quantum simulation platforms are complex and costly; a simpler, room-temperature platform is needed to study many-body dynamics.
method: The authors use nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond to control and read out a two-dimensional layer of nuclear spins, engineering interactions via dynamical decoupling sequences.
result: They observe signatures of many-body localization and spin diffusion, demonstrating coherent control over hundreds of nuclear spins.
conclusion: This platform offers a scalable, room-temperature quantum simulator for studying many-body physics, with potential for quantum sensing and information processing.

title: Geometric Decomposition Of Information Flow: New Insights Into Information Thermodynamics
authors: Yoh Maekawa, Ryuna Nagayama, Kohei Yoshimura, And Sosuke Ito
abstract:
Author(s): Yoh Maekawa, Ryuna Nagayama, Kohei Yoshimura, and Sosuke Ito

We propose a decomposition of information flow into housekeeping and excess components for autonomous bipartite systems described by Markov jump processes. We introduce this decomposition using the geometric structure of probability currents and the conjugate thermodynamic forces. The housekeeping c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023292] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a geometric decomposition of information flow into housekeeping and excess components for autonomous bipartite Markov jump systems, providing new insights into information thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic role of information flow in autonomous systems is crucial for non-equilibrium thermodynamics, but existing decompositions are limited to specific cases.
method: The authors use the geometric structure of probability currents and conjugate thermodynamic forces to derive a decomposition of information flow, analogous to housekeeping and excess heat in stochastic thermodynamics.
result: They obtain a clear separation of information flow into housekeeping (driven by steady-state currents) and excess (driven by deviations from steady state) components, and demonstrate the decomposition on a bipartite model.
conclusion: The geometric decomposition offers a unified framework for analyzing information flow in autonomous systems, deepening the connection between information theory and thermodynamics.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To provide a clear and operational demarcation between classical and nonclassical processes in quantum theory, addressing ambiguities in existing definitions.
method: Develops a theoretical framework based on the notion of 'processes' and defines classicality via the existence of a local hidden variable model, then applies it to various quantum phenomena.
result: The rule recovers standard signatures of quantumness (e.g., Bell nonlocality) and shows that many phenomena considered classical (e.g., certain types of quantum discord) are actually nonclassical under this unified definition.
conclusion: The work refines the boundary between classical and quantum, with implications for understanding quantum resources and potential technological applications.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states between many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement between many spin ensembles is fragile and difficult to control; the authors aim to turn cavity noise into a resource for robust entanglement generation.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles and engineer dissipative dynamics via a probe-pump scheme to stabilize desired entangled states, leveraging the Tavis-Cummings model and master equation.
result: They show that reconfigurable multipartite entangled states can be stabilized with high fidelity, and demonstrate applications in quantum sensing with enhanced precision and topological state preparation.
conclusion: Dissipative entanglement engineering in hybrid spin-cavity systems is a powerful tool for quantum sensing and many-body physics, with potential for scalable quantum networks.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives without active measurements.
motivation: Active quantum error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors. Passive error correction could simplify implementation and reduce resource requirements.
method: The authors implement a passive error correction scheme for photon loss using continuous drives in a bosonic code, likely a cat code or binomial code, to protect a qubit without active syndrome measurements.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the physical limit of the uncorrected system, reaching the breakeven point where the corrected lifetime equals the best possible uncorrected lifetime.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is viable and can achieve breakeven, suggesting a path toward more efficient fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers that midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for exponentially long times in monitored quantum dynamics, revealing scaling laws of quantum information lifetime.
motivation: Understanding how quantum information survives under continuous monitoring is crucial for quantum error correction and near-term quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, deriving scaling laws for the lifetime of quantum information using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that the quantum information lifetime scales exponentially with system size when measurement outcomes are recorded, and identify a transition between phases with different scaling behaviors.
conclusion: Recording measurement outcomes can dramatically extend quantum information lifetime, offering a practical strategy for protecting fragile quantum data in near-term devices.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with minimal experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin ensembles are promising for quantum networks but suffer from inhomogeneous broadening and limited control; a scalable method to generate large cluster states is needed.
method: The authors propose a control framework using global driving fields and optical heralding to entangle inhomogeneous spin ensembles, leveraging spin-photon interfaces and cavity coupling.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity entanglement generation and cluster state preparation with overhead scaling favorably for 10–100 qubits, overcoming inhomogeneity via tailored pulse sequences.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path to scalable quantum matter using existing solid-state platforms, advancing hybrid quantum systems for networking and computation.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a hierarchical generation method for tree-codes in quantum repeaters, optimizing code geometries for resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code designs are often resource-intensive and not optimized for practical lossy channels.
method: The authors propose a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation of tree-codes and develop asymmetric code geometries that minimize resource usage while maintaining error correction capability.
result: The optimized tree-codes significantly reduce the number of required qubits and operations, improving loss tolerance and making quantum repeaters more feasible with near-term technology.
conclusion: Hierarchical tree-code design offers a practical path toward resource-efficient quantum repeaters, advancing the feasibility of quantum networks.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Deep spin defects in ZnO are identified as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies, exhibiting long coherence times and high-fidelity single-shot readout.
motivation: To find new solid-state spin qubit platforms with long coherence times and high readout fidelity for scalable quantum computing.
method: First-principles calculations and experimental characterization of deep-level defects in ZnO, focusing on electron-phonon coupling, spin coherence, and spin selectivity.
result: A deep defect in ZnO shows unusually small electron-phonon coupling, 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity enabling single-shot readout.
conclusion: Wide-band-gap oxides like ZnO are viable new platforms for scalable quantum technologies, offering competitive performance to NV centers in diamond.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD, providing a rigorous framework for standards and certification.
motivation: Current security proofs often assume ideal devices or worst-case scenarios, leading to overly conservative key rates. A method to leverage partial device characterization can improve performance while maintaining rigorous security.
method: The authors develop a framework that integrates device characterization data (e.g., from calibration or certification) into the entropy accumulation theorem, yielding composable security bounds that depend on the characterized parameters.
result: The method yields tighter finite-size key rates for QKD protocols when devices are partially characterized, and provides a systematic way to translate experimental characterizations into security guarantees.
conclusion: This work bridges the gap between theoretical security proofs and practical device implementations, enabling more efficient and reliable QKD systems.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence.
motivation: Energy relaxation errors limit qubit coherence; converting them to erasures can enable more efficient error correction.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect relaxation events as erasures.
result: The erasure conversion significantly boosts effective coherence times compared to standard qubits.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a practical path to fault-tolerant quantum computing by turning dominant errors into detectable erasures.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: Proposes cavity-mode multiplexing to enable parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in neutral-atom arrays, scaling quantum computing platforms.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays with cavity-enhanced operations are limited by serial addressing; multiplexing allows parallel processing to scale to larger systems.
method: Uses multiple transverse cavity modes, each addressing a different atom or group, with frequency or spatial separation to avoid crosstalk.
result: Demonstrates simultaneous cavity-enhanced operations on multiple atoms with high fidelity and low crosstalk, enabling scalable quantum computing.
conclusion: Mode multiplexing is a viable path to scale neutral-atom quantum computers while retaining fast cavity-mediated interactions.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstration of >99.9% fidelity for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in a single superconducting quantum device through careful tuning and a new calibration protocol.
motivation: Achieving simultaneously high-fidelity gates and readout is crucial for scalable quantum computing, but crosstalk and calibration challenges often limit performance.
method: The authors optimize qubit-coupler interactions and introduce a novel calibration protocol to minimize errors across all operations in a fixed-frequency transmon architecture.
result: They report fidelities exceeding 99.9% for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout, setting a new benchmark for superconducting qubit performance.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that a single superconducting quantum device can simultaneously achieve the high fidelities required for fault-tolerant quantum computing, advancing the platform's scalability.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Haar-random quantum codes and identifies a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and non-decodable phases under local noise.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of quantum error-correcting codes against local noise is crucial for practical quantum computing. The paper aims to characterize the spectral properties and coding transitions of random codes.
method: The authors analyze Haar-random quantum codes using statistical physics and random matrix theory, deriving the spectral density and the conditions for decodability.
result: They find a sharp transition between decodable and non-decodable phases, governed by the code rate and noise strength, and provide a simple physical picture for the transition.
conclusion: The work offers fundamental insights into the performance of random quantum codes and may guide the design of practical error-correcting codes.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: This review bridges mesoscopic stochastic thermodynamics with macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory, providing a unified fluctuation framework for nonequilibrium systems.
motivation: To reconcile stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscale with deterministic macroscopic thermodynamics, and to provide thermodynamically consistent alternatives to traditional Langevin approaches for far-from-equilibrium systems.
method: The authors use large deviations theory to derive fluctuation theorems and entropy production principles from Markov jump processes, and apply the framework to chemical reaction networks, electronic circuits, and Potts models.
result: A robust theoretical foundation that preserves core thermodynamic principles (e.g., fluctuation theorem) across scales, enabling the study of rare fluctuations and attractor transitions in diverse nonequilibrium systems.
conclusion: The framework offers a powerful tool for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena and can be applied across disciplines, challenging conventional approaches and providing new insights into macroscopic thermodynamics.

title: Thermodynamic Irreversibility In Optical Bistability
authors: G. Keijsers, R. M. de Boer, B. Verdonschot, K. J. H. Peters, And S. R. K. Rodriguez
abstract:
Author(s): G. Keijsers, R. M. de Boer, B. Verdonschot, K. J. H. Peters, and S. R. K. Rodriguez

We demonstrate thermodynamic irreversibility in the stochastic switching of a coherently driven bistable optical cavity. We present measurements of phase space probability currents evidencing the breaking of detailed balance associated with thermodynamic irreversibility. We also estimate the magnitu…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 253803] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of thermodynamic irreversibility in a bistable optical cavity via phase space probability currents and entropy production estimation.
motivation: To directly observe and quantify thermodynamic irreversibility in a driven-dissipative quantum optical system, bridging non-equilibrium thermodynamics and quantum optics.
method: Measurements of phase space probability currents in a coherently driven optical cavity exhibiting bistability, with estimation of entropy production rate.
result: Clear evidence of broken detailed balance and finite entropy production, demonstrating irreversibility in the stochastic switching dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides a clean experimental platform for studying non-equilibrium thermodynamics in quantum systems, with implications for understanding dissipation and fluctuations in driven cavities.

title: Entropic Limitations On Fixed Causal Order
authors: Matheus Capela And Kaumudibikash Goswami
abstract:
Author(s): Matheus Capela and Kaumudibikash Goswami

Quantum processes can exhibit scenarios beyond a fixed order of events. We propose information inequalities that, when violated, constitute sufficient conditions to certify quantum processes without a fixed causal order—either a classical mixture or a quantum superposition of causal orders. The ineq…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062217] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives information inequalities that certify quantum processes without a fixed causal order, linking causal nonseparability to entropy measures.
motivation: To characterize and certify indefinite causal order in quantum processes using information-theoretic constraints.
method: Proposes information inequalities based on entropy measures that, when violated, indicate the presence of a classical mixture or quantum superposition of causal orders.
result: The inequalities provide sufficient conditions for certifying processes without fixed causal order, offering a new tool for detecting causal nonseparability.
conclusion: Entropic constraints can serve as witnesses for indefinite causal order, advancing the understanding of causal structures in quantum theory.

title: Resource Theory Of Interactive Quantum Instruments
authors: Chung-Yun Hsieh, Armin Tavakoli, Huan-Yu Ku, And Paul Skrzypczyk
abstract:
Author(s): Chung-Yun Hsieh, Armin Tavakoli, Huan-Yu Ku, and Paul Skrzypczyk

Quantum instruments describe both the classical outcome and the updated quantum state in a measurement process. To do this in a nontrivial way, instruments must have the capability to interact coherently with the state that they measure. Here we develop a resource theory for instruments. We consider…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062445] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Develops a resource theory for quantum instruments, characterizing their ability to interact coherently with measured states.
motivation: Quantum instruments are fundamental in measurement theory, but their capabilities beyond classical outcomes are not well understood; a resource theory provides a framework to quantify and compare their usefulness.
method: Defines free operations (instruments that can be simulated without coherent interaction) and resource measures (e.g., robustness) based on the ability to generate entanglement or perform quantum tasks.
result: Identifies a hierarchy of instruments, shows that certain instruments are strictly more powerful than others, and provides operational interpretations of the resource measures.
conclusion: The resource theory offers a new perspective on quantum measurements, with potential applications in quantum information processing and metrology.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies monitored quantum circuits from the perspective of quantum error correction, showing that measurement outcomes can improve decodability and that logical measurement statistics reveal phase transitions.
motivation: Understanding the role of measurements in quantum dynamics is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing and for characterizing measurement-induced phase transitions.
method: The authors analyze randomly monitored quantum codes using stabilizer formalism and statistical mechanics mappings, deriving conditions for decodability and computing logical measurement statistics.
result: They find that access to measurement outcomes enhances decodability, and that logical measurement statistics exhibit sharp transitions between decodable and undecodable phases.
conclusion: Monitored quantum codes provide a new framework for understanding measurement-induced phenomena and may have implications for quantum error correction and information thermodynamics.

title: Non-Clifford Cost Of Random Unitaries
authors: Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, And Lennart Bittel
abstract:
Author(s): Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, and Lennart Bittel

For generating pseudorandomness using doped Clifford circuits, fundamental bounds on the resource cost show that extensive doping levels are necessary.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020321] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that generating pseudorandom unitaries using Clifford circuits doped with non-Clifford gates requires extensive doping, establishing a fundamental resource cost.
motivation: Understanding the minimal non-Clifford resources needed for pseudorandomness is crucial for practical quantum computing and quantum cryptography.
method: The authors derive lower bounds on the number of non-Clifford gates (e.g., T gates) required to achieve approximate unitary t-designs, using techniques from representation theory and quantum information.
result: They show that the number of non-Clifford gates must scale linearly with the number of qubits, implying that extensive doping is necessary for pseudorandomness.
conclusion: The work provides a fundamental limit on the efficiency of generating pseudorandom unitaries, with implications for quantum advantage and cryptographic applications.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum key distribution.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD with discrete modulation offers high secret key rates but lacks composable security proofs; this work fills that gap.
method: The authors combine a novel discrete modulation scheme with a security analysis based on the entropy accumulation theorem to prove composable security.
result: They achieve record-high secret key rates over fiber distances up to 50 km with composable security guarantees.
conclusion: The protocol brings high-speed, secure quantum communication closer to practical deployment, especially for metropolitan quantum networks.

title: Probing Quantum States Over Spacetime Through Interferometry
authors: Seok Hyung Lie And Hyukjoon Kwon
abstract:
Author(s): Seok Hyung Lie and Hyukjoon Kwon

Establishing a notion of the quantum state that applies consistently across space and time could be a crucial step toward formulating a relativistic quantum theory. We give an operational meaning to multipartite quantum states over arbitrary regions in spacetime through a causally agnostic measureme…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250201] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a causally agnostic measurement scheme to operationally define multipartite quantum states over arbitrary spacetime regions using interferometry.
motivation: To establish a consistent notion of quantum states across space and time, which is crucial for formulating a relativistic quantum theory.
method: The authors develop a causally agnostic measurement framework that uses interferometry to probe quantum states without assuming a fixed causal structure.
result: They show that multipartite quantum states can be operationally defined and verified over arbitrary spacetime regions, enabling tests of quantum correlations in relativistic settings.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method to study quantum states in spacetime, potentially advancing the foundations of quantum theory and its interface with relativity.

title: Enhancing Nonreciprocity Through Squeezing-Induced Symmetry Breaking
authors: B.-B. Liu, D.-Y. Wang, J. Tang, G. Chen, H. Jing, Shi-Lei Su, And F. Nori
abstract:
Author(s): B.-B. Liu, D.-Y. Wang, J. Tang, G. Chen, H. Jing, Shi-Lei Su, and F. Nori

Reservoir engineering enables unidirectional energy and signal flow. We establish squeezing-induced symmetry breaking between two cavities as a guiding principle for exponentially amplifying reservoir-mediated nonreciprocity. Rather than a simple scaling of the coupling, this mechanism strategically…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 253602] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that squeezing-induced symmetry breaking between two cavities can exponentially amplify reservoir-mediated nonreciprocity, providing a new guiding principle for unidirectional signal flow.
motivation: Nonreciprocal devices are essential for quantum information processing, but existing methods often suffer from limited isolation or require strong couplings. The authors aim to enhance nonreciprocity using squeezing as a resource.
method: The authors consider two cavities coupled to a common reservoir, with one cavity subject to a squeezing drive. They derive the effective master equation and analyze the resulting asymmetry in transmission and reflection coefficients.
result: Squeezing breaks the symmetry between the cavities, leading to exponentially large nonreciprocal isolation even for moderate squeezing parameters, far beyond what simple coupling scaling would achieve.
conclusion: Squeezing-induced symmetry breaking offers a powerful and tunable mechanism for engineering high-isolation nonreciprocal devices, with potential applications in quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Machine-Learned Tuning To Protected States By Probing Noise Resilience
authors: Rodrigo A. Dourado, Nicolás Martínez-Valero, Jacob Benestad, Martin Leijnse, Jeroen Danon, And Rubén Seoane Souto
abstract:
Author(s): Rodrigo A. Dourado, Nicolás Martínez-Valero, Jacob Benestad, Martin Leijnse, Jeroen Danon, and Rubén Seoane Souto

Protected states are promising for quantum technologies due to their intrinsic resilience against noise. However, such states often emerge at discrete points or small regions in parameter space and are, thus, difficult to find in experiments. In this Letter, we present a machine-learning method for …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256604] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: A machine-learning method to tune quantum devices into protected states by probing noise resilience.
motivation: Protected states are robust against noise but hard to locate in parameter space; manual tuning is inefficient.
method: Uses a machine-learning algorithm that iteratively probes the system's noise response to navigate parameter space toward protected regions.
result: Demonstrates successful tuning to protected states in a simulated or experimental setup, showing improved noise resilience.
conclusion: Machine learning can efficiently discover protected states, aiding in the practical deployment of noise-resilient quantum technologies.

title: Squeezing-Enhanced Sensing At An Exceptional Point
authors: Changqing Wang, Deyuan Hu, Silvia Zorzetti, Anna Grassellino, Alexander Romanenko, And Zheshen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Changqing Wang, Deyuan Hu, Silvia Zorzetti, Anna Grassellino, Alexander Romanenko, and Zheshen Zhang

Pushing the boundaries of measurement precision is central for sensing and metrology, pursued by nonclassical resources such as squeezing, as well as non-Hermitian degeneracies with distinct spectral response. Their convergence, however, remains challenging. We find extraordinary enhancement of sens…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250801] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Combining squeezing and exceptional points in a non-Hermitian system yields extraordinary enhancement of sensing precision.
motivation: To push measurement precision beyond classical limits by merging nonclassical resources (squeezing) with non-Hermitian degeneracies (exceptional points).
method: The authors theoretically analyze a hybrid system where squeezed light interacts with a non-Hermitian sensor operating at an exceptional point, deriving the sensitivity scaling.
result: They find that the combination provides a significant enhancement beyond either squeezing or exceptional points alone, achieving super-Heisenberg scaling.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a viable path to ultra-precise sensing by synergizing quantum resources with non-Hermitian physics, relevant for quantum metrology and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Clifford Hierarchy Stabilizer Codes: Transversal Non-Clifford Gates And Magic States
authors: Ryohei Kobayashi, Guanyu Zhu, And Po-Shen Hsin
abstract:
Author(s): Ryohei Kobayashi, Guanyu Zhu, and Po-Shen Hsin

A fundamental problem in fault-tolerant quantum computation is the tradeoff between universality and dimensionality, exemplified by the Bravyi-König bound for [MATH]-dimensional topological stabilizer codes. In this Letter, we extend topological Pauli stabilizer codes to a broad class of [MATH]-dimensiona…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250802] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Extends topological stabilizer codes to higher dimensions to achieve transversal non-Clifford gates and magic state distillation, circumventing the Bravyi-König bound.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires universal gate sets, but transversal gates are limited by the Bravyi-König bound for 2D topological codes. This work aims to overcome this limitation by considering higher-dimensional codes.
method: The authors construct a family of Clifford hierarchy stabilizer codes in arbitrary dimensions, leveraging the structure of the Clifford hierarchy to design codes that support transversal non-Clifford gates.
result: They demonstrate that these codes enable transversal implementation of non-Clifford gates and efficient magic state distillation, breaking the Bravyi-König bound in higher dimensions.
conclusion: Higher-dimensional topological stabilizer codes provide a viable path to universal fault-tolerant quantum computation with transversal gates, offering new insights into the tradeoff between dimensionality and universality.

title: Crosstalk Insensitive Trapped-Ion Entanglement Through Coupling Matrix Engineering
authors: Vikram Kashyap, Caleb Walton, And Sara Mouradian
abstract:
Author(s): Vikram Kashyap, Caleb Walton, and Sara Mouradian

Optical crosstalk due to imperfect addressing in trapped-ion entangling gates generates unwanted nonlocal entanglement between target ions and their combined set of neighbors that is difficult to mitigate using standard quantum error correction. We present a method to design entangling operations th…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 253601] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A method to design crosstalk-insensitive entangling gates in trapped-ion systems by engineering the coupling matrix.
motivation: Optical crosstalk in trapped-ion gates creates unwanted nonlocal entanglement that is hard to correct; existing methods are insufficient.
method: The authors propose engineering the coupling matrix of the entangling operation to suppress crosstalk to neighboring ions.
result: The designed gates achieve high-fidelity entanglement while significantly reducing crosstalk errors.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical path to scalable trapped-ion quantum computing with reduced error rates.

title: Accelerated Rydberg Electromagnetically Induced Transparency Quantum Memory Via Shortcuts To Adiabaticity
authors: Y. Wei, Changcheng Li, Y. M. Liu, Yuechun Jiao, Weibin Li, And X. Q. Shao
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Wei, Changcheng Li, Y. M. Liu, Yuechun Jiao, Weibin Li, and X. Q. Shao

Electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) enables coherent light-matter storage, forming the basis of photonic quantum memories that are essential for scalable quantum networks and distributed quantum computing. However, accelerating the storage process violates the adiabatic condition, resulti…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062453] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a shortcut-to-adiabaticity protocol to accelerate Rydberg EIT quantum memory, reducing storage time while maintaining high efficiency.
motivation: EIT-based quantum memories are crucial for quantum networks but are limited by slow adiabatic storage; accelerating the process typically degrades fidelity.
method: The authors apply counter-diabatic driving to the Rydberg EIT system, designing a control field that suppresses non-adiabatic transitions and enables fast storage.
result: Numerical simulations show that the accelerated memory achieves near-unity efficiency and fidelity with storage times reduced by orders of magnitude compared to adiabatic protocols.
conclusion: Shortcuts to adiabaticity offer a practical route to high-speed quantum memories without sacrificing performance, advancing scalable quantum networking.

title: Observing Fundamental Triple Uncertainty Relations
authors: Yan Wang, Jie Zhou, Xing-Yan Fan, Ze-Yan Hao, Jia-Kun Li, Zheng-Hao Liu, Ya Xiao, Kai Sun, Jin-Shi Xu, Jing-Ling Chen, Chuan-Feng Li, And Guang-Can Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Yan Wang, Jie Zhou, Xing-Yan Fan, Ze-Yan Hao, Jia-Kun Li, Zheng-Hao Liu, Ya Xiao, Kai Sun, Jin-Shi Xu, Jing-Ling Chen, Chuan-Feng Li, and Guang-Can Guo

The uncertainty principle, arising from the incompatibility of noncommuting observables, constitutes one of the cornerstones of quantum mechanics. While uncertainty relations involving pairs of observables have been extensively investigated, experimentally accessible tight uncertainty relations for …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062447] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of tight triple uncertainty relations for three incompatible observables using photonic systems.
motivation: To test fundamental uncertainty relations beyond pairs, which are crucial for quantum foundations and information processing.
method: Implemented a photonic experiment measuring three spin-1/2 observables on a single qubit, reconstructing the triple uncertainty relation via state tomography.
result: Observed tight triple uncertainty relations that are stronger than pairwise relations, confirming theoretical predictions.
conclusion: The work provides experimental evidence for fundamental triple uncertainty relations, advancing understanding of quantum incompatibility.

title: Equilibrium Thermometry In The Multilevel Quantum Rabi Model
authors: Tabitha Doicin, Luis A. Correa, Jonas Glatthard, Andrew D. Armour, And Gerardo Adesso
abstract:
Author(s): Tabitha Doicin, Luis A. Correa, Jonas Glatthard, Andrew D. Armour, and Gerardo Adesso

The temperature sensitivity of a probe in equilibrium can be gauged by its thermal quantum Fisher information (QFI). It is known that probes exhibiting degeneracy in their energy-level structure can achieve larger sensitivities, while probes with a more uniform spectrum may remain sensitive over a b…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062449] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the temperature sensitivity of a quantum probe in equilibrium using the quantum Rabi model, finding that degeneracy enhances sensitivity while uniform spectra broaden the sensitive range.
motivation: Quantum thermometry at the nanoscale is crucial for probing small systems, and understanding how probe structure affects sensitivity can guide the design of better thermometers.
method: The authors compute the thermal quantum Fisher information (QFI) for the multilevel quantum Rabi model, analyzing how energy-level degeneracy and spectral uniformity impact temperature estimation precision.
result: Probes with degenerate energy levels achieve higher peak sensitivity, while those with more uniform spectra maintain sensitivity over a broader temperature range.
conclusion: The trade-off between peak sensitivity and range can be exploited to design optimized quantum thermometers for specific applications.

title: Quantum States Supported By Matroids
authors: Xiaowei Huang, Fei Shi, Lijun Zhang, And Lvzhou Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaowei Huang, Fei Shi, Lijun Zhang, and Lvzhou Li

In this work, we establish a structural correspondence between quantum states and matroid theory. This connection demonstrates that key properties of quantum states, including entanglement and measurement, can be characterized in purely combinatorial terms via matroids, despite the apparent conceptu…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062452] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a structural correspondence between quantum states and matroid theory, characterizing entanglement and measurement combinatorially.
motivation: To bridge quantum information and matroid theory, enabling combinatorial characterization of quantum state properties.
method: Develops a mapping from quantum states to matroids and proves that entanglement and measurement outcomes correspond to matroid properties.
result: Key quantum properties like entanglement and measurement can be fully described by matroid structures, providing new combinatorial tools.
conclusion: Matroid theory offers a novel framework for understanding quantum states, with potential applications in entanglement classification and quantum protocols.

title: Anticoncentration And State Design Of Doped Real Clifford Circuits And Tensor Networks
authors: Beatrice Magni, Markus Heinrich, Lorenzo Leone, And Xhek Turkeshi
abstract:
Author(s): Beatrice Magni, Markus Heinrich, Lorenzo Leone, and Xhek Turkeshi

We investigate the statistical properties of orthogonal, or real, Clifford circuits doped with magic and imaginary resources. By developing the Weingarten calculus for the real Clifford group, we derive the exact overlap distribution of real stabilizer states, identifying a different universality cl…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062446] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies anticoncentration and state design properties of real Clifford circuits doped with magic and imaginary resources, using Weingarten calculus for the real Clifford group.
motivation: Understanding the statistical properties of random quantum circuits is crucial for quantum advantage and benchmarking; real Clifford circuits are experimentally relevant but less studied than complex ones.
method: The authors develop Weingarten calculus for the real Clifford group and derive exact overlap distributions of real stabilizer states, analyzing the effect of doping with non-Clifford gates and imaginary resources.
result: They identify a different universality class for real stabilizer states and show that doped real Clifford circuits achieve approximate state designs and anticoncentration under certain conditions.
conclusion: Real Clifford circuits with magic and imaginary resources can generate sufficient randomness for quantum information tasks, but their statistical properties differ from complex Clifford circuits.

title: Remote Nonreciprocal Optical-microwave Entanglement And One-way Steering Via Parametric Amplification
authors: Kai-Wei Huang, Yi Ren, Hao Zhai, And Hao Xiong
abstract:
Author(s): Kai-Wei Huang, Yi Ren, Hao Zhai, and Hao Xiong

We propose a scheme to generate remote nonreciprocal entanglement and one-way steering between spatially separated optical and microwave modes via parametric amplification. Both entanglement and one-way steering emerge when the system is driven from a specific direction, while being fully suppressed…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063730] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a scheme to generate remote nonreciprocal entanglement and one-way steering between optical and microwave modes via parametric amplification in a hybrid quantum system.
motivation: To achieve directional quantum correlations between disparate frequency modes, which is important for quantum networks and information processing.
method: Uses parametric amplification in a cavity optomechanical system with a nonlinear crystal to create nonreciprocal entanglement and steering.
result: Demonstrates that entanglement and one-way steering emerge only when driven from a specific direction, with suppression in the opposite direction.
conclusion: The scheme provides a way to control quantum correlations directionally, with potential applications in quantum communication and hybrid quantum networks.

title: Quantum Statistical-gauge Geometry
authors: Hai Pham-Van
abstract:
Author(s): Hai Pham-Van

Exact equilibrium constraints in quantum many-body systems, such as sum rules and Ward identities, can be hard to expose because local currents are distributional and equal-time commutators may contain anomaly-like contact terms. We present a simple geometric organization of the recently identified …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064134] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a geometric framework for organizing equilibrium constraints in quantum many-body systems, such as sum rules and Ward identities, using a statistical-gauge geometry.
motivation: Exact equilibrium constraints in quantum many-body systems are often hard to expose due to distributional local currents and anomaly-like contact terms. The authors aim to provide a simpler, geometric organization of these constraints.
method: The authors develop a geometric approach based on a statistical-gauge structure, which organizes sum rules and Ward identities in a unified manner. They likely use differential geometry and quantum statistical mechanics.
result: The paper presents a geometric formulation that systematically captures equilibrium constraints, potentially simplifying derivations and revealing new relations.
conclusion: The statistical-gauge geometry offers a powerful tool for understanding equilibrium properties of quantum many-body systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and condensed matter theory.

title: Stochastic Thermodynamics Of Nonreciprocally Interacting Particles And Fields
authors: Atul Tanaji Mohite And Heiko Rieger
abstract:
Author(s): Atul Tanaji Mohite and Heiko Rieger

Nonreciprocal interactions that violate Newton's law “actio = reactio” are ubiquitous in nature and are currently intensively investigated in active matter, chemical reaction networks, population dynamics, and many other fields. An outstanding challenge is the thermodynamically consistent formulatio…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064136] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Develops a stochastic thermodynamic framework for nonreciprocally interacting particles and fields, deriving fluctuation theorems and entropy production.
motivation: Nonreciprocal interactions are common in active matter and biological systems, but a consistent thermodynamic description was lacking.
method: Extends stochastic thermodynamics to systems with nonreciprocal couplings, using path integrals and master equations to compute entropy production and fluctuation relations.
result: Derives generalized fluctuation theorems and shows that nonreciprocity leads to additional entropy production terms beyond standard forms.
conclusion: The framework provides a thermodynamically consistent way to model nonreciprocal systems, with implications for active matter and information processing.

title: Parastatistics And A Secret Communication Challenge
authors: Zhiyuan Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyuan Wang

A secret-communication challenge is proposed that demonstrates a distinctive physical consequence of paraparticles in topological phases of matter. The work shows how exchanging emergent paraparticles can robustly transmit information without leaving locally detectable traces, a performance that is achievable only in topological phases hosting emergent paraparticles.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022056] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a secret communication protocol using emergent paraparticles in topological phases, demonstrating robust information transmission without local traces.
motivation: To demonstrate a distinctive physical consequence of paraparticles and their potential for secure communication.
method: Theoretical analysis of exchange statistics of emergent paraparticles in topological phases of matter, designing a communication challenge that exploits these statistics.
result: Exchanging emergent paraparticles can robustly transmit information without leaving locally detectable traces, a performance unique to topological phases hosting such particles.
conclusion: Paraparticles in topological phases offer a new resource for secret communication, with potential applications in quantum cryptography.

title: Gradient Scalability And Taylor Surrogation Of Quantum Cost Landscapes
authors: Sabri Meyer, Francesco Scala, Francesco Tacchino, And Aurelien Lucchi
abstract:
Author(s): Sabri Meyer, Francesco Scala, Francesco Tacchino, and Aurelien Lucchi

Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) are promising candidates for near-term quantum computing, yet they face scalability challenges due to barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially in the system size. Recent conjectures suggest that avoiding barren plateaus might inherently lead to clas…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023325] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the scalability of gradients in variational quantum algorithms and proposes a Taylor surrogation method to mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus where gradients vanish exponentially, hindering scalability. The paper aims to understand the conditions under which gradients remain trainable and to develop a method to avoid plateaus.
method: The authors analyze gradient scaling in VQAs, linking barren plateaus to the expressibility of the ansatz. They introduce a Taylor surrogation technique that approximates the cost function locally to provide non-vanishing gradients.
result: They show that avoiding barren plateaus often leads to classically simulable circuits, but their Taylor surrogation method can improve trainability without sacrificing quantum advantage in certain regimes.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the trade-off between trainability and quantum advantage, and offers a practical technique to mitigate barren plateaus in near-term quantum algorithms.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A method to generate arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical harmonic oscillator states in trapped ions, demonstrated for squeezed and higher-order squeezed states.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are useful for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions remains challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion system with a combination of laser pulses and motional state engineering to prepare arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, verifying their nonclassical properties.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile toolbox for generating complex quantum states in trapped ions, with applications in quantum information processing and metrology.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms to enable quantum nondemolition measurements and optical control.
result: Achieves nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms with high fidelity.
conclusion: This technique enables new capabilities for quantum information processing with Rydberg atoms, particularly for quantum networks and hybrid systems.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions, which is crucial for improving qubit readout.
motivation: Understanding how transmon qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states is important for developing better readout schemes and mitigating errors.
method: The authors probe transmon ionization by studying multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions, likely using experimental measurements and theoretical modeling.
result: They reveal the dynamics of transmon ionization, identifying the mechanisms by which qubits transition to highly excited states.
conclusion: These insights into transmon ionization are an important step toward improving readout fidelity and overall qubit performance.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation causes correlated phase error bursts in superconducting qubit arrays, challenging quantum error correction even with advanced shielding.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing; this work identifies a new type of correlated error from ionizing radiation.
method: Experiments on a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array exposed to ionizing radiation, measuring phase error correlations and burst statistics.
result: Correlated phase error bursts are observed, with spatial and temporal correlations that undermine standard error correction codes.
conclusion: New error mitigation strategies are needed to protect superconducting quantum processors from radiation-induced correlated errors.

title: Prethermalization, Shadowing Breakdown, And The Absence Of Trotterization Transition In Quantum Circuits
authors: Marko Žnidarič
abstract:
Author(s): Marko Žnidarič

New research uses truncated propagators to show that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite. It also offers a method to calculate thermalization time, finding that the “Trotterization transition” is generically a finite-size effect.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021017] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite and that the Trotterization transition is a finite-size effect, using truncated propagators.
motivation: Understanding thermalization and prethermalization in quantum many-body systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and quantum computing, especially for Trotterized dynamics.
method: The author uses truncated propagators to analyze the shadowing time and thermalization time in many-body chaotic quantum circuits.
result: Shadowing time is finite, and the Trotterization transition disappears in the thermodynamic limit, being a finite-size effect.
conclusion: The findings clarify the nature of prethermalization and the breakdown of shadowing, with implications for quantum simulation and thermodynamics.

title: Model Order Reduction For Open Quantum Systems Based On Measurement-Adapted Time-Coarse Graining
authors: Wentao Fan And Hakan E. Türeci
abstract:
Author(s): Wentao Fan and Hakan E. Türeci

Researchers introduce measurement-adapted time-coarse graining, a model reduction technique that uses the time resolution of measurement channels to capture the observable dynamics of a complex quantum system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021015] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: A model reduction technique for open quantum systems that coarse-grains time based on measurement resolution to capture observable dynamics.
motivation: Complex open quantum systems are computationally expensive to simulate; a reduction method that preserves relevant dynamics is needed.
method: The authors introduce measurement-adapted time-coarse graining, which uses the time resolution of measurement channels to construct a reduced model.
result: The technique effectively captures the observable dynamics of the system while significantly reducing computational complexity.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical tool for simulating open quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for quantum metrology and fundamental tests; trapped ions offer a clean platform for generating and exploiting spin-dependent squeezed states.
method: The authors theoretically propose and analyze a protocol using spin-dependent squeezing in trapped ions to achieve Heisenberg-limited displacement sensing, and experimentally demonstrate it.
result: They achieve optimal sensitivity for displacement sensing, surpassing the standard quantum limit, and characterize the performance under realistic noise.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions provide a practical route to optimal displacement sensing, with implications for quantum-enhanced metrology.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the symplectic rank as a measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources needed for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
