motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable systems, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. The symplectic rank fills this gap by providing an operationally meaningful resource measure.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian unitaries required to decompose a state, and derive its properties using symplectic geometry and phase-space representations.
result: The symplectic rank is shown to be a faithful, additive, and convex measure of non-Gaussianity, and it directly relates to the minimal number of non-Gaussian operations needed for state preparation and the optimal compression rate.
conclusion: The symplectic rank provides a unified framework for quantifying non-Gaussian resources, with implications for quantum information processing and continuous-variable quantum computing.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying sources of decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters with narrow linewidths are crucial for quantum networks, but spectral diffusion and decoherence limit their performance. Understanding the origins of instability is key to improving emitter coherence.
method: The authors study single erbium ions coupled to silicon nanophotonic cavities, performing spectroscopy to characterize spectral diffusion and decoherence mechanisms.
result: They identify specific sources of spectral instability, such as charge fluctuations and phonon interactions, and quantify their impact on emitter linewidth and coherence.
conclusion: The findings provide a pathway to stabilize cavity-coupled erbium emitters, advancing their use in quantum networking and computation.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are computationally expensive and not scalable.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference approach that approximates posterior distributions over models and parameters, enabling fast and scalable estimation.
result: The method accurately identifies spin environments and supports real-time adaptive measurement strategies, validated on experimental NV center data.
conclusion: Variational Bayesian inference provides an efficient tool for quantum estimation and model learning, with potential applications in quantum sensing and control.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity QED model with Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions leading to blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: To understand how kinetic constraints and long-range interactions in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays give rise to exotic non-equilibrium phenomena.
method: The authors study a minimal model of cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, analyzing the interplay of cavity-mediated interactions and Rydberg blockade using analytical and numerical techniques.
result: They find blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating that kinetic constraints stabilize these exotic phases.
conclusion: Cavity QED with Rydberg atoms provides a platform for realizing kinetically constrained many-body physics and long-range quantum scars.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: An open-source pulse optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates for quantum error correction in neutral-atom platforms.
motivation: Neutral-atom quantum computing requires high-fidelity multiqubit gates to implement quantum error correction codes efficiently.
method: The authors develop an open-source pulse optimization framework that designs and optimizes multiqubit Rydberg gates, leveraging the Rydberg blockade mechanism.
result: The framework achieves high-fidelity multiqubit gates suitable for quantum error correction, demonstrated on neutral-atom platforms.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for implementing error correction in neutral-atom quantum computers, advancing the platform's viability.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a fully integrated silicon photonic chip for self-testing quantum random number generation, advancing practical quantum security devices.
motivation: To miniaturize and scale quantum random number generators for real-world security applications using self-testing protocols that require minimal trust in the hardware.
method: Implements a self-testing quantum random number expansion protocol on a silicon photonic chip, using integrated photonic components to generate and measure quantum states.
result: Achieves high-speed random number generation with provable security based on Bell inequality violations, all on a compact chip platform.
conclusion: The work paves the way for production-scale, miniaturized quantum security devices by integrating self-testing randomness expansion onto a photonic chip.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enhance photon blockade, yielding stronger antibunching and high transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter coupling, which is experimentally challenging. This work explores collective effects to overcome this limitation.
method: The authors study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, analyzing the system's quantum dynamics and photon statistics using master equations.
result: They find that photon blockade is collectively enhanced with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission even when individual emitters are weakly coupled.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a scalable route to photon blockade, relevant for quantum nonlinear optics and quantum information processing.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can suppress nonadiabatic errors in quantum control, but exact implementation is challenging; variational approaches offer approximations but may lack accuracy.
method: The authors introduce a weighted action formalism combined with computer algebra to systematically optimize variational counterdiabatic protocols, enabling efficient computation of high-order corrections.
result: The method yields significantly higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving in test systems, with reduced computational overhead.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and quantum computing applications requiring fast, high-fidelity operations.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Large-scale quantum processors require simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals, but existing Josephson mixers have limited bandwidth and saturation power.
method: The authors design and fabricate impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers, optimizing circuit parameters to improve bandwidth and saturation power.
result: The mixers achieve significantly enhanced bandwidth and higher saturation power compared to conventional designs, enabling simultaneous amplification of multiple quantum signals.
conclusion: These improved Josephson mixers are promising components for quantum signal processing and transduction in large-scale quantum processors.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
Author(s): William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, and Viktor Svensson

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments motivate a need for clear criteria to identify Majorana bound states in interacting systems, which is crucial for topological quantum computing.
method: The authors develop theoretical definitions and measures of robustness and locality for Majorana bound states in the presence of interactions, using numerical simulations and analytical models.
result: They provide quantitative criteria to distinguish true Majorana bound states from trivial Andreev bound states, and show how interactions affect their protection.
conclusion: The work establishes a framework to assess the feasibility of Majorana-based qubits in realistic interacting systems, guiding future experiments.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique using classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling sequences for multi-qubit systems often scale poorly with qubit number when targeting correlated noise; this work aims to design efficient, device-tailored sequences.
method: The authors map the problem of designing k-local dynamical decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, leveraging error correction principles to cancel spatially correlated errors.
result: They produce sequences whose length depends only on the code parameters and not on the total number of qubits, enabling efficient decoupling for large systems.
conclusion: This approach bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, offering practical sequences for noise mitigation in quantum devices.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is central to quantum algorithm design, and its state version extends applicability to learning stabilizer groups and other symmetries.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that leverages Fourier sampling over Abelian groups to solve the state hidden subgroup problem efficiently.
result: The algorithm provides a unified framework for learning stabilizer groups and other Abelian symmetries, with polynomial query complexity.
conclusion: This work advances quantum algorithm theory by generalizing the hidden subgroup problem to quantum states, with implications for quantum learning and complexity.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without adding noise is a key challenge.
method: The authors engineer an effective negative-mass oscillator using tailored optical interactions in a fully optical setup, creating a coherent cancellation mechanism.
result: They demonstrate cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the sensitivity of the optomechanical sensor.
conclusion: This work provides a new method for quantum noise cancellation, with potential applications in quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Phase Estimation With Partially Randomized Time Evolution
authors: Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, And Aram W. Harrow
abstract:
Author(s): Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, and Aram W. Harrow

Partially randomized product formulas slash the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020332] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Partially randomized product formulas reduce Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, enabling significant resource savings for quantum chemistry.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is a key subroutine but requires expensive Hamiltonian simulation; reducing this cost is crucial for practical quantum advantage.
method: The authors introduce partially randomized product formulas that mix deterministic and random Trotter steps, analyzed using a combination of Hamiltonian simulation theory and phase estimation error analysis.
result: The approach yields orders-of-magnitude reduction in the simulation overhead for quantum chemistry benchmarks, with rigorous error bounds.
conclusion: Partially randomized time evolution offers a practical and provably efficient way to accelerate phase estimation, making it more feasible for near-term quantum devices.

title: Maximizing The Nondemolition Nature Of A Quantum Measurement Via An Adaptive Readout Protocol
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’Neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, and Andrea Morello

Adaptive subspace-switching readout improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, boosting qudit readout fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020330] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: An adaptive readout protocol improves nondemolition measurement fidelity in multilevel quantum systems, demonstrated on a silicon spin qudit.
motivation: Quantum measurements in multilevel systems often cause backaction that destroys quantum information; a nondemolition readout is crucial for quantum error correction and state preparation.
method: The authors implement an adaptive subspace-switching readout that dynamically adjusts the measurement basis based on prior outcomes, reducing measurement-induced errors.
result: They achieve a readout fidelity of 99.61% on a silicon spin qudit, significantly outperforming standard readout schemes while reducing measurement time.
conclusion: Adaptive readout protocols are a practical tool for high-fidelity, nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, applicable across various qubit platforms.

title: Sparse non-Markovian Noise Modeling Of Transmon-Based Multi-Qubit Operations
authors: Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, And Gregory Quiroz
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, and Gregory Quiroz

A comprehensive noise modeling approach for transmon-based quantum processors captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors, achieving a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020327] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: A sparse non-Markovian noise model for transmon-based multi-qubit operations achieves sevenfold improvement in accuracy for variational algorithm simulation.
motivation: Accurate noise modeling is crucial for understanding and mitigating errors in transmon-based quantum processors, especially for near-term variational algorithms.
method: The authors develop a sparse non-Markovian noise model that captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors in transmon qubits, and use it as a hardware proxy simulator.
result: The model achieves a sevenfold improvement in accuracy compared to standard noise models when simulating variational algorithms.
conclusion: Sparse non-Markovian noise modeling significantly enhances the fidelity of simulations for transmon-based quantum processors, enabling better error mitigation and algorithm performance prediction.

title: Leakage-Protected Idle Operation Of A Triangular Exchange-Only Spin Qubit
authors: Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, And Jason R. Petta
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, and Jason R. Petta

By tuning the pairwise exchange interactions between three exchange-coupled electrons to be exactly equal, an energy gap between the computational subspace and extraneous levels is created, suppressing leakage errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020324] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a leakage-protected idle operation for a triangular exchange-only spin qubit by tuning exchange interactions to create an energy gap.
motivation: Leakage errors in exchange-only spin qubits degrade gate fidelity; protecting idle operation is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors tune pairwise exchange interactions between three electrons to be exactly equal, opening an energy gap between the computational subspace and leakage states.
result: They experimentally observe suppressed leakage errors during idle operation, demonstrating a protected idle regime.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method to mitigate leakage in exchange-only qubits, advancing their viability for quantum information processing.

title: Diagnosing Chaos With Projected Ensembles Of Process Tensors
authors: Peter O’donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, And Mark T. Mitchison
abstract:
Author(s): Peter O’Donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, and Mark T. Mitchison

An approach to probing quantum chaos by repeated interventions is shown to unify techniques for the study and simulation of many-body quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020322] Published Tue May 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a method to diagnose quantum chaos using projected ensembles of process tensors, unifying techniques for studying many-body quantum dynamics.
motivation: Understanding quantum chaos is crucial for characterizing thermalization and the thermodynamic behavior of quantum systems, but existing probes often require full state tomography or are limited to specific models.
method: The authors define a process tensor that captures the effect of repeated interventions on a quantum system, and then construct projected ensembles from this tensor to extract signatures of chaos, such as spectral form factors and out-of-time-order correlators.
result: The projected ensemble approach reproduces known chaos indicators and reveals new features, such as the emergence of random matrix statistics in the process tensor's eigenstates.
conclusion: The method provides a unified framework for probing chaos in many-body systems, with potential applications to quantum thermodynamics and the study of thermalization.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and practical implementations.
motivation: Continuous-variable (CV) approaches offer advantages in quantum communication, such as compatibility with existing telecom infrastructure and high-rate key distribution, motivating a systematic review of the field.
method: The paper surveys CV quantum communication protocols, including CV-QKD, entanglement-based schemes, and network architectures, discussing theoretical security proofs and experimental realizations.
result: CV quantum communication is shown to be a mature and competitive technology, with demonstrated long-distance QKD and potential for integration into quantum networks.
conclusion: Continuous-variable techniques are a viable and promising path for practical quantum communication, with ongoing challenges in loss and noise mitigation.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: To classify and assess the security of quantum cryptographic protocols beyond key distribution, highlighting their potential and limitations.
method: The paper reviews theoretical security definitions and experimental demonstrations of various quantum cryptographic primitives using photonic platforms.
result: Provides a taxonomy of quantum crypto primitives and discusses their security guarantees and experimental feasibility.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers enhanced security for many tasks beyond QKD, but practical implementations face significant challenges.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classifying nonequilibrium stationary states using quantum field theory.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors employ nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify universal behavior based on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: They identify distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking to known critical phenomena and topological phases.
conclusion: The review provides a systematic classification that can guide future experiments and theory in nonequilibrium quantum thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: A review of computational methods for predicting decoherence of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques.
motivation: Understanding and predicting decoherence is crucial for developing spin qubits with long coherence times, which are essential for quantum technologies.
method: The paper reviews ab initio and cluster expansion methods to compute spin-spin relaxation times for various spin qubit platforms.
result: Cluster expansion techniques provide reliable predictions for spin-spin relaxation times, but challenges remain for higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational approaches are maturing and can guide the design of spin qubits with improved coherence, though further development is needed for complex environments.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to testing whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, using quantum information methods to design experiments that can distinguish between classical and quantum theories of gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks based on entanglement and information theory, and analyzes proposed tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement between quantum probes.
result: It provides a status update on theoretical approaches and concrete experimental proposals for detecting gravitationally induced entanglement, which would indicate a quantum nature of gravity.
conclusion: Information-theoretic methods offer a promising path to test quantum gravity at low energies, with several feasible experiments on the horizon.

title: Black Hole Thermodynamics Without Black Hole Solutions
authors: Meng-Nan Yang, Guan-Yi Lu, And H. Lü
abstract:
Author(s): Meng-Nan Yang, Guan-Yi Lu, and H. Lü

We consider the string-theory-inspired Einstein-Maxwell-Maxwell-dilaton theory and show that we can derive the complete set of thermodynamic quantities of charged black holes without having to construct the black hole solutions. We argue that the technique can be applied more broadly to string theor…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251403] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Derives black hole thermodynamics from string-inspired theory without explicit black hole solutions.
motivation: To show that thermodynamic properties of black holes can be obtained from the theory's structure alone, bypassing the need for constructing solutions.
method: Uses the Einstein-Maxwell-Maxwell-dilaton theory and applies thermodynamic relations directly to the Lagrangian or field equations.
result: Complete set of thermodynamic quantities (mass, charge, temperature, entropy) are derived without solving the field equations.
conclusion: The technique is broadly applicable to string theory and other gravitational theories, simplifying the study of black hole thermodynamics.

title: Dissipation Due To Bulk Localized Low-Energy Modes In Strongly Disordered Superconductors
authors: Anton V. Khvalyuk And Mikhail V. Feigel’man
abstract:
Author(s): Anton V. Khvalyuk and Mikhail V. Feigel’man

Microwave dissipation in strongly disordered superconductors is driven by localized collective modes within rare weak spots, a theoretical insight which provides a fresh strategy to enhance coherence times in quantum devices.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256001] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper identifies localized collective modes in rare weak spots as the dominant source of microwave dissipation in strongly disordered superconductors, offering a path to improve coherence times in quantum devices.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating microwave dissipation is crucial for enhancing coherence times in superconducting qubits, a key challenge in quantum computing.
method: The authors theoretically analyze dissipation due to bulk localized low-energy modes in strongly disordered superconductors, focusing on rare weak spots.
result: They find that localized collective modes within rare weak spots drive microwave dissipation, providing a fresh strategy to reduce loss.
conclusion: The insights can guide material engineering to improve coherence times in superconducting quantum devices.

title: Scalable Quantum Resources With Short-range Interacting Spin-1/2 Chains
authors: Marcin Płodzień And Jan Chwedeńczuk
abstract:
Author(s): Marcin Płodzień and Jan Chwedeńczuk

The dynamical generation of quantum resources, such as many-body entanglement, Bell correlations, or spin squeezing, can be achieved via one-axis twisting (OAT) dynamics, which require all-to-all couplings. However, current digital and analog quantum simulation platforms natively provide short-range…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062220] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that short-range interacting spin-1/2 chains can generate scalable quantum resources like entanglement and Bell correlations via one-axis twisting dynamics, overcoming the need for all-to-all couplings.
motivation: One-axis twisting (OAT) dynamics generate useful quantum resources but require all-to-all couplings, which are not available in many quantum simulation platforms. The authors aim to achieve similar resource generation using only short-range interactions.
method: The authors study spin-1/2 chains with nearest-neighbor interactions and show that OAT-like dynamics emerge from the interplay of interactions and a global drive, using analytical and numerical methods to characterize the generated quantum correlations.
result: They demonstrate that scalable many-body entanglement, Bell correlations, and spin squeezing can be generated in short-range interacting chains, with the amount of resources scaling with system size.
conclusion: Short-range interacting spin chains can serve as a scalable source of quantum resources, making them promising for quantum metrology and information processing without requiring all-to-all connectivity.

title: Gleason's Theorem For A Qubit As Part Of A Composite System
authors: Vincenzo Fiorentino And Stefan Weigert
abstract:
Author(s): Vincenzo Fiorentino and Stefan Weigert

We extend Gleason's theorem to the two-dimensional Hilbert space of a qubit by invoking the standard axiom that describes composite quantum systems. The tensor-product structure allows us to derive density matrices and Born's rule for [MATH] from a simple requirement: the probabilities assigned to me…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062221] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Extends Gleason's theorem to qubits using the composite system axiom, deriving density matrices and Born's rule from probability assignments.
motivation: Gleason's theorem does not apply to two-dimensional Hilbert spaces; the authors aim to fill this gap by leveraging the tensor-product structure of composite systems.
method: They impose that probability assignments on a qubit must be consistent with those on a larger composite system, using the standard quantum axiom for composite systems.
result: They derive that the only possible probability measures are given by density matrices and Born's rule, thus extending Gleason's theorem to qubits.
conclusion: The work provides a foundational justification for the quantum formalism in the simplest non-trivial case, reinforcing the role of composite systems in quantum theory.

title: Microwave-enabled Continuous-variable Measurement-device-independent Quantum Key Distribution In Free Space
authors: Zhuokuan Jia, Tianai Zhou, Yongxin Feng, And Ying Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Zhuokuan Jia, Tianai Zhou, Yongxin Feng, and Ying Guo

Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) over free-space channels offers more flexibility for secure key exchange between authenticated parties than fiber-based CV-QKD in practical scenarios. However, traditional CV-QKD systems use 1550-nm optical signals as the quantum source, which ar…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062450] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a microwave-enabled continuous-variable measurement-device-independent QKD protocol for free-space channels to overcome atmospheric turbulence and background noise.
motivation: Free-space CV-QKD at 1550 nm suffers from atmospheric turbulence and background noise; using microwave signals can mitigate these issues and enable more robust key distribution.
method: The protocol uses microwave signals as the quantum source, employs continuous-variable encoding, and implements measurement-device-independent detection to eliminate detector side-channel attacks.
result: Simulations show that the microwave-based protocol achieves higher secret key rates over longer distances compared to optical CV-QKD under realistic atmospheric conditions.
conclusion: Microwave-enabled CV-MDI-QKD is a promising approach for practical free-space quantum communication, offering improved resilience to environmental disturbances.

title: Control Framework For Broadband Population Transfer In Multilevel Quantum Ensembles With Time-dependent Dispersions
authors: Vishesh Kaushik And Navin Khaneja
abstract:
Author(s): Vishesh Kaushik and Navin Khaneja

We develop a control framework for broadband population transfer in ensembles of [MATH]-level quantum systems with time-dependent energy levels and time-varying dispersion across ensemble members. Ensemble inhomogeneity is modeled through time-varying dispersion functions that capture Hamiltonian varia…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062620] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Develops a control framework for broadband population transfer in multilevel quantum ensembles with time-dependent dispersions.
motivation: Ensemble inhomogeneities, such as time-dependent energy level dispersions, hinder precise quantum control; a robust framework is needed to achieve high-fidelity population transfer across the ensemble.
method: The authors model ensemble inhomogeneity via time-varying dispersion functions and design control pulses using optimal control theory to achieve broadband population transfer.
result: The framework enables efficient population transfer in multilevel systems despite time-dependent dispersions, demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: The control approach is promising for quantum information processing with inhomogeneous ensembles, such as those used in quantum memories and transducers.

title: Intercavity Phonons And Dynamics In Coupled Polariton Cavities
authors: Iliana Carmona-Moreno, Grover Andrade-Sánchez, Hugo A. Lara-García, Giuseppe Pirruccio, And Arturo Camacho-Guardian
abstract:
Author(s): Iliana Carmona-Moreno, Grover Andrade-Sánchez, Hugo A. Lara-García, Giuseppe Pirruccio, and Arturo Camacho-Guardian

Intercavity polaritons, hybrid quasiparticles with spatially separated photonic and excitonic components, provide a platform to engineer structured light-matter states. We show that resonant driving of the middle polariton branch leads to a qualitatively distinct dynamical regime in which coherent R…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062814] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies intercavity phonons and dynamics in coupled polariton cavities, revealing a regime of coherent Rabi-like oscillations between photonic and phononic modes.
motivation: To understand the role of phonons in coupled polariton cavities and explore new dynamical regimes for engineering light-matter states.
method: The authors use a theoretical model of coupled polariton cavities with resonant driving, analyzing the dynamics of intercavity phonons and polariton branches.
result: They find that resonant driving of the middle polariton branch leads to coherent Rabi-like oscillations between photonic and phononic modes, mediated by intercavity phonons.
conclusion: Intercavity phonons play a crucial role in the dynamics of coupled polariton cavities, offering a platform for coherent control of hybrid light-matter states.

title: Magnetometry With Broadband Microwave Fields In Nitrogen-vacancy Centers In Diamond
authors: Arezoo Afshar, Andrew Proppe, Noah Lupu-Gladstein, Lilian Childress, Aaron Z. Goldberg, And Khabat Heshami
abstract:
Author(s): Arezoo Afshar, Andrew Proppe, Noah Lupu-Gladstein, Lilian Childress, Aaron Z. Goldberg, and Khabat Heshami

Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond are optically addressable and versatile light-matter interfaces with practical application in magnetic-field sensing, offering the ability to operate at room temperature and reach sensitivities below pT/[MATH]. We propose an approach to simultan…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063113] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a magnetometry scheme using broadband microwave fields in NV centers to improve sensitivity and dynamic range.
motivation: NV centers are promising for magnetic field sensing but conventional narrowband methods limit sensitivity and dynamic range.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a protocol using broadband microwave fields to simultaneously address multiple NV resonances, enhancing signal-to-noise ratio.
result: The broadband approach achieves higher sensitivity and wider dynamic range compared to standard narrowband techniques.
conclusion: Broadband microwave excitation is a viable strategy to improve NV-based magnetometry performance.

title: Phonon Scattering From Spatial Relaxation Of One-dimensional Bose Gases
authors: Bilal Alilou, Clément Duval, Frederick Del Pozo, And Nicolas Cherroret
abstract:
Author(s): Bilal Alilou, Clément Duval, Frederick Del Pozo, and Nicolas Cherroret

We theoretically investigate the nonequilibrium relaxation of a spatial density modulation in a one-dimensional nonintegrable Bose gas and its connection to the equilibrium scattering rate [MATH] of the system's phononic excitations. We show that the density relaxation is generically go…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063321] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies nonequilibrium relaxation of density modulations in 1D Bose gases, linking it to phonon scattering rates.
motivation: Understanding relaxation in nonintegrable quantum systems is fundamental to nonequilibrium thermodynamics and transport.
method: Theoretical analysis using hydrodynamic and kinetic approaches to connect density relaxation to equilibrium phonon scattering rates.
result: The density relaxation is generically governed by the phonon scattering rate, with explicit expressions derived.
conclusion: The work provides a direct link between equilibrium scattering and nonequilibrium relaxation, relevant for quantum thermodynamics.

title: Non-Hermitian Cavity Magnomechanics With $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetry-related Asymmetric Transparency
authors: Cham Oumie, Wu-Ming Liu, And Kashif Ammar Yasir
abstract:
Author(s): Cham Oumie, Wu-Ming Liu, and Kashif Ammar Yasir

We investigate magnomechanically induced transparency in a cavity magnomechanical system with traveling-field-induced non-Hermitian coupling. The setup consists of a microwave cavity mode coupled to magnons in a single-crystal yttrium iron garnet sphere, where the magnon mode is further hybridized w…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063522] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Investigates non-Hermitian cavity magnomechanics with PT-symmetry-related asymmetric transparency.
motivation: To explore magnomechanically induced transparency in a cavity magnomechanical system with non-Hermitian coupling, which is relevant for quantum information processing and sensing.
method: Theoretical analysis of a cavity magnomechanical system with traveling-field-induced non-Hermitian coupling, involving a microwave cavity mode coupled to magnons in a YIG sphere.
result: Observes PT-symmetry-related asymmetric transparency and related phenomena.
conclusion: Provides insights into non-Hermitian physics in hybrid quantum systems, potentially useful for quantum transducers and signal processing.

title: Nonreciprocal Universal Photon Blockade In An Asymmetrical Cavity
authors: Xiuwen Xia, Xinqin Zhang, Xiaobing Luo, Chaofei Liu, Haozhen Li, Jabir Hakami, Jingping Xu, And Yaping Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Xiuwen Xia, Xinqin Zhang, Xiaobing Luo, Chaofei Liu, Haozhen Li, Jabir Hakami, Jingping Xu, and Yaping Yang

Inspired by the distinctive properties of universal photon blockade (UPB), we propose a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings model in an asymmetric cavity to achieve quantum nonreciprocity. Through theoretical analysis, we establish direction-dependent optimal conditions for perfect UPB in weak-driving limita…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063729] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical proposal for achieving nonreciprocal universal photon blockade in an asymmetric cavity using a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings model.
motivation: To realize quantum nonreciprocity and photon blockade simultaneously, which is important for quantum information processing and networking.
method: The authors analyze a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings model in an asymmetric cavity, deriving direction-dependent optimal conditions for perfect universal photon blockade under weak driving.
result: They establish that nonreciprocal photon blockade can be achieved with high contrast, enabling directional control of single-photon transmission.
conclusion: The proposed system provides a platform for integrated quantum devices that combine nonreciprocity and photon blockade, useful for quantum networks.

title: Universality Of Dissipative Discrete Time Crystal Formation
authors: Jr. And Jayson G. Cosme Roy D. Jara
abstract:
Author(s): Roy D. Jara, Jr. and Jayson G. Cosme

We demonstrate that the Kibble-Zurek mechanism holds for open systems transitioning from a disordered phase to a discrete time crystal (DTC). Specifically, we observe the characteristic power-law scaling with quench time of the number of spatial defects and the transition delay measured from the tim…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214323] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates that the Kibble-Zurek mechanism applies to open systems forming discrete time crystals, showing universal scaling of defects and transition delay.
motivation: Understanding defect formation in time crystals is important for characterizing non-equilibrium phases in open quantum systems.
method: The authors study a driven-dissipative model of a discrete time crystal and analyze the scaling of spatial defects and transition delay as a function of quench time using numerical simulations.
result: They observe power-law scaling consistent with the Kibble-Zurek mechanism, indicating universality in the formation of discrete time crystals.
conclusion: The Kibble-Zurek mechanism holds for open systems transitioning to a discrete time crystal phase, providing insights into non-equilibrium critical dynamics.

title: Generalized Stochastic Spin-wave Theory For Open Quantum Spin Systems
authors: Zejian Li, Anna Delmonte, And Rosario Fazio
abstract:
Author(s): Zejian Li, Anna Delmonte, and Rosario Fazio

We propose a semiclassical framework for solving open quantum dynamics in driven-dissipative spin systems. Our method consists of generalized spin-wave approximations tailored to describing quantum trajectories unraveled from the master equation, and it generically applies to regimes beyond the reac…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214324] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: A semiclassical framework for solving open quantum dynamics in driven-dissipative spin systems using generalized spin-wave theory.
motivation: Open quantum spin systems are important for quantum thermodynamics and quantum information, but exact solutions are often intractable; a semiclassical method can capture essential physics in regimes beyond the reaction coordinate approach.
method: The authors propose generalized spin-wave approximations tailored to quantum trajectories unraveled from the master equation, extending spin-wave theory to open systems.
result: The framework is shown to apply generically to driven-dissipative spin systems, providing a tractable semiclassical description.
conclusion: This work offers a new tool for studying non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics in spin systems, relevant to quantum thermal machines and open quantum systems.

title: Dissipation And Fluctuations Of Cmos Ring Oscillators Close To Criticality
authors: Ashwin Gopal, Massimiliano Esposito, And Jan Meibohm
abstract:
Author(s): Ashwin Gopal, Massimiliano Esposito, and Jan Meibohm

We analyze a thermodynamically consistent model of Complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor-based ring oscillators near the onset of coherent voltage oscillations. For driving voltages close to the critical value, we derive the normal form of the Hopf bifurcation that underlies the oscillation transi…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245308] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the thermodynamics of CMOS ring oscillators near a Hopf bifurcation, deriving fluctuation theorems and dissipation bounds for coherent oscillations.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost and fluctuations of classical computing elements near criticality is important for designing energy-efficient devices.
method: The authors develop a thermodynamically consistent model of CMOS ring oscillators and use stochastic thermodynamics to derive the normal form of the Hopf bifurcation and associated fluctuation relations.
result: They obtain analytical expressions for work, heat, and entropy production near the oscillation onset, and show that fluctuations obey a detailed fluctuation theorem.
conclusion: The work provides a thermodynamic framework for classical oscillators near criticality, linking dissipation to information processing in CMOS circuits.

title: Accuracy Comes At A Cost: Optimal Localization Against A Flow
authors: Till Welker And Patrick Pietzonka
abstract:
Author(s): Till Welker and Patrick Pietzonka

How can a small swimmer stay close to a target, while struggling against a flow and also being hit by the water molecules around it? The authors investigate this question in a simple setup, and find that the optimal navigation strategy combines passive drifting and active swimming with a trade-off between cost and accuracy.


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064142] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Optimal navigation strategy for a small swimmer in a flow trades off accuracy and cost, revealing thermodynamic constraints on information processing.
motivation: Understand how a microscopic swimmer can localize near a target despite flow and thermal noise, balancing energy expenditure and positional accuracy.
method: Theoretical analysis using stochastic thermodynamics and optimal control theory to derive the trade-off between cost (work) and accuracy (mean squared displacement).
result: The optimal strategy combines passive drifting and active swimming, with a fundamental bound linking accuracy and thermodynamic cost.
conclusion: Accuracy in localization comes at a thermodynamic cost, illustrating a general principle for information processing in noisy environments.

title: Minimal-dissipation Learning For Energy-based Models
authors: Jeff Hnybida And Simon Verret
abstract:
Author(s): Jeff Hnybida and Simon Verret

We show that the bias of the approximate maximum-likelihood estimation (MLE) objective of a persistent chain energy-based model (EBM) is precisely equal to the thermodynamic excess work of an overdamped Langevin dynamical system. We then answer the question of whether such a model can be trained wit…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065306] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Shows that the bias in maximum-likelihood training of energy-based models equals thermodynamic excess work, and explores minimal-dissipation learning.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamic cost of training energy-based models and whether they can be trained with minimal dissipation.
method: Connects the bias of persistent chain EBM training to excess work in overdamped Langevin dynamics, then analyzes minimal-dissipation protocols.
result: The bias is exactly the thermodynamic excess work; minimal-dissipation learning is possible under certain conditions.
conclusion: Energy-based model training has a thermodynamic interpretation, and dissipation can be minimized, linking machine learning to thermodynamics.

title: Dynamical Typicality In Classical Lattice Systems
authors: Nicolas Nessi And Peter Reimann
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolas Nessi and Peter Reimann

Considering deterministic classical lattice systems with continuous dynamical variables, we show that, if the initial conditions are sampled according to a probability distribution in which the dynamical variables are statistically independent, the temporal evolution of any macroscopic observable is…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064138] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that for deterministic classical lattice systems with independent initial conditions, the time evolution of macroscopic observables is typically well-described by the microcanonical ensemble, establishing a form of dynamical typicality.
motivation: Understanding how macroscopic irreversibility emerges from deterministic microscopic dynamics is a fundamental question in statistical mechanics. The paper aims to provide a rigorous justification for the typicality of equilibrium behavior in classical lattice systems.
method: The authors consider deterministic classical lattice systems with continuous variables and show that if initial conditions are sampled from a product distribution, the time evolution of any macroscopic observable is close to its microcanonical average for most times, using concentration of measure and dynamical systems arguments.
result: They prove that for large systems, the fraction of time a macroscopic observable deviates from its microcanonical average is exponentially small in system size, with explicit bounds that depend on the observable's sensitivity and system parameters.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous foundation for dynamical typicality in classical lattice systems, supporting the idea that equilibrium statistical mechanics emerges from deterministic dynamics under typical initial conditions.

title: Rotation Sensor Based On An Atom-cavity System
authors: Jim Skulte, Jayson G. Cosme, And Ludwig Mathey
abstract:
Author(s): Jim Skulte, Jayson G. Cosme, and Ludwig Mathey

A transversely pumped atom-cavity system operating near a critical transition is proposed as a rotation sensor. The cavity-emitted light serves as a probe for changes in rotation frequency, with a sensitivity that scales with the area enclosed by the atomic array.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022057] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes an atom-cavity system as a rotation sensor with sensitivity scaling with the enclosed area.
motivation: To develop a quantum-enhanced rotation sensor using a transversely pumped atom-cavity system operating near a critical transition.
method: The system uses cavity-emitted light as a probe; sensitivity is analyzed via the critical behavior of the atom-cavity system.
result: The rotation sensitivity scales with the area enclosed by the atomic array, offering potential advantages over classical sensors.
conclusion: The atom-cavity system provides a promising platform for rotation sensing with quantum-enhanced performance.

title: Quantum Dynamical Signatures Of Topological Flow Transitions In Limit Cycle Phases
authors: Alejandro S. Gómez And Javier Del Pino
abstract:
Author(s): Alejandro S. Gómez and Javier del Pino

Quantum self-oscillatory phases are ubiquitous in driven-dissipative systems. Classically, each phase is defined by its flow pattern and how stationary sets organize phase space (e.g., fixed points and limit cycles), with transitions triggered by local bifurcations or global basin rearrangements. In…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023319] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum signatures of topological flow transitions in limit cycle phases of driven-dissipative systems, linking classical bifurcations to quantum observables.
motivation: Understanding how classical topological transitions in phase space manifest in quantum systems is crucial for characterizing driven-dissipative phases and their stability.
method: The authors analyze a quantum van der Pol oscillator model using phase-space methods and quantum trajectory simulations to identify signatures of limit cycle transitions.
result: They find that topological flow transitions are accompanied by changes in quantum fluctuations, entanglement, and spectral properties, providing observable quantum markers.
conclusion: Quantum dynamical signatures can detect classical flow transitions, offering a way to probe non-equilibrium phase structure in quantum systems.

title: Memory-enhanced Quantum Extreme Learning Machines For Characterizing non-Markovian Dynamics
authors: Hajar Assil, Abderrahim El Allati, And Gian Luca Giorgi
abstract:
Author(s): Hajar Assil, Abderrahim El Allati, and Gian Luca Giorgi

We use a quantum extreme learning machine (QELM) for characterizing and estimating parameters of quantum dynamics generated by a tunable collision model. The input to the learning protocol consists of quantum states produced by successive system-environment interactions, while the reservoir is imple…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023306] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses a quantum extreme learning machine (QELM) with memory to characterize non-Markovian dynamics in a collision model, demonstrating parameter estimation and detection of memory effects.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are important in quantum systems but challenging to characterize; machine learning offers a data-driven approach to extract parameters and detect memory effects without full tomography.
method: A QELM is implemented with a reservoir of qubits that interact sequentially with system states via a collision model; the reservoir's output is used to train a linear readout for parameter estimation and non-Markovianity detection.
result: The QELM successfully estimates system-environment coupling strengths and detects non-Markovianity, with memory-enhanced reservoirs improving performance over memoryless ones.
conclusion: Quantum extreme learning machines with memory are effective tools for characterizing non-Markovian quantum dynamics, offering a practical approach for quantum system identification.

title: Indefinite Causal Order In Cavity Quantum Electrodynamics
authors: Luis Octavio Castaños-Cervantes, Lorenzo M. Procopio, And Tim J. Bartley
abstract:
Author(s): Luis Octavio Castaños-Cervantes, Lorenzo M. Procopio, and Tim J. Bartley

Indefinite causal order (ICO) has the potential to be a new resource for quantum information processing. In most of its experiments, ICO has been investigated in a photonic platform. Here, we investigate ICO in a cavity quantum electrodynamics system composed of two cavities. Our results show that I…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023295] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates indefinite causal order (ICO) in a cavity quantum electrodynamics system, showing that ICO can be realized in this platform and may serve as a resource for quantum information processing.
motivation: ICO is a potential resource for quantum information tasks, but most experiments have been photonic; exploring ICO in cavity QED could enable new applications.
method: The authors model two cavities coupled via a quantum switch, analyzing the dynamics and the emergence of ICO using master equations and numerical simulations.
result: They demonstrate that ICO can be achieved in cavity QED, with the degree of causal order controllable by system parameters.
conclusion: Cavity QED provides a viable platform for ICO, opening up possibilities for quantum information protocols exploiting indefinite causal order.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, and David R. Reichman

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020502] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: A review of the process tensor framework for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics using tensor networks.
motivation: Non-Markovian effects are crucial in many quantum systems but computationally challenging; efficient methods are needed.
method: The paper reviews the process tensor formalism and demonstrates how tensor-network representations enable practical simulation of complex non-Markovian dynamics.
result: The framework is shown to be applicable across diverse physical fields, providing a unified approach to non-Markovian dynamics.
conclusion: Process tensor methods with tensor networks offer a powerful tool for simulating non-Markovian quantum systems, relevant to open quantum systems and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Lieb-Mattis entangled states enable robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing with intrinsic common-mode noise rejection.
motivation: Differential phase sensing is crucial for quantum sensor networks but suffers from common-mode noise; existing entangled states are fragile to such noise.
method: The authors propose using Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states of spin ensembles that are naturally insensitive to common-mode phase shifts, and analyze their performance for differential phase estimation.
result: Lieb-Mattis states achieve Heisenberg-limited sensitivity for differential phase while being robust against common-mode noise, outperforming conventional entangled states in noisy environments.
conclusion: Lieb-Mattis states provide a practical and scalable approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing, enabling robust quantum sensor networks.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics in the continuum limit.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, which are central to non-equilibrium thermodynamics and fluctuation theorems.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise identities and establishing connections to diffusion processes via continuum limits.
result: Achieves a unification of previously disjoint theories, enabling consistent treatment of observables across jump and diffusion regimes.
conclusion: The framework enhances the theoretical toolkit for studying stochastic thermodynamics and may facilitate new results in fluctuation theorems and thermodynamic bounds.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne

This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective proposes that biomolecular condensates can process information through phase transitions, linking physical chemistry to cellular computation.
motivation: Cells must process high-dimensional environmental signals, but traditional molecular signaling may be insufficient; phase transitions offer a collective, nonlinear mechanism for information processing.
method: The authors present a conceptual framework drawing on phase separation, multivalent interactions, and condensate formation, discussing how these physical phenomena can implement computational operations like sensing, classification, and response.
result: They argue that phase transitions enable cells to perform complex computations, such as threshold detection and multi-input integration, with minimal molecular components.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation provides a powerful, physically-grounded paradigm for cellular information processing, with implications for synthetic biology and understanding of living systems.

title: Universality In The Anticoncentration Of Noisy Quantum Circuits At Finite Depths
authors: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo de Nardis, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo De Nardis, and Andrea De Luca

A universal description of noisy random circuits reveals depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent anticoncentration.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020365] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a universal description of anticoncentration in noisy random quantum circuits at finite depths, revealing depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent behavior.
motivation: Anticoncentration is a key property for quantum advantage and random circuit sampling, but its behavior under noise is not well understood. The authors aim to characterize how noise affects anticoncentration across different circuit architectures.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework using statistical mechanics mappings and replica methods to analyze the output distribution of noisy random circuits. They consider various noise models and circuit topologies.
result: They find that anticoncentration persists up to a depth-dependent noise threshold, with a universal scaling that is independent of circuit architecture. The transition between anticoncentrated and concentrated regimes is described by a universal function.
conclusion: The results provide a unified understanding of anticoncentration in noisy quantum circuits, which is important for assessing the feasibility of quantum advantage experiments and for designing error mitigation strategies.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing and simulation, but loading and imaging them with high fidelity and low atom loss remains challenging. EIT offers a way to perform nondestructive imaging and continuous loading.
method: The authors apply electromagnetically induced transparency to achieve nondestructive imaging of atom arrays, and use it to enable continuous loading of atoms into optical tweezers. They work in finite magnetic fields to control atomic states.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity imaging with low atom loss and efficient loading of atom arrays, showing that EIT can be a practical tool for neutral-atom quantum information processing.
conclusion: EIT-based imaging and loading is a viable technique for improving the performance of neutral-atom arrays, with potential applications in quantum computing and simulation.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubits is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise cross-correlations.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readout data to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in the previously inaccessible frequency range.
result: They successfully demonstrate the method on a qubit platform, extracting noise cross-correlations and revealing new insights into noise sources.
conclusion: This technique provides a powerful tool for noise characterization in qubit systems, aiding in the development of more coherent quantum devices.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate codes to reduce logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at the megaquop scale requires fault-tolerant architectures that minimize space and time overhead, especially for neutral-atom platforms where native gates and error correction are still developing.
method: The authors design a transversal architecture that combines small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate quantum error-correcting codes, optimized for neutral-atom hardware constraints such as long-range interactions and parallel gate operations.
result: The architecture achieves significant savings in logical qubit count, physical qubit count, and runtime compared to conventional approaches, enabling megaquop-scale simulations with realistic hardware parameters.
conclusion: Neutral-atom quantum computers can feasibly reach megaquop-scale quantum simulation with the proposed transversal architecture, bridging the gap between current hardware and practical quantum advantage.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes a theoretical link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing bounds on loss function concentration to mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus where gradients vanish, hindering trainability. Understanding how noise affects loss landscapes is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors derive analytical bounds on the variance of loss functions under noise, relating expressivity (via the dimension of the dynamical Lie algebra) to concentration rates.
result: They show that noise can actually help by reducing the effective expressivity, leading to less concentrated loss functions and improved trainability, quantified by explicit concentration estimates.
conclusion: Noise in parametrized quantum circuits can be beneficial for training by counteracting barren plateaus, offering a principled guide for designing noise-resilient variational algorithms.

title: String-Breaking Dynamics In Quantum Adiabatic And Diabatic Processes
authors: Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, de Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, And Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract:
Author(s): Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, De Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, and Alexey V. Gorshkov

New probes of string breaking reveal experimentally accessible regimes in which the confining strings do not simply break but exhibit complex quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020331] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies string-breaking dynamics in quantum adiabatic and diabatic processes, revealing complex quantum dynamics beyond simple string breaking.
motivation: Understanding string breaking in confining gauge theories is important for quantum simulation and non-equilibrium dynamics, with potential implications for quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors use a combination of analytical models and numerical simulations, likely including tensor networks or exact diagonalization, to study the dynamics of string breaking in a quantum spin chain or lattice gauge theory.
result: They identify experimentally accessible regimes where string breaking exhibits rich quantum dynamics, including diabatic effects and non-adiabatic transitions.
conclusion: The work provides new probes for string breaking in quantum simulators, highlighting the interplay between confinement and quantum dynamics.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold
