The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of methods for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, unified under a common framework.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are crucial for accurate modeling of open quantum systems in quantum technologies, but the diversity of methods makes it hard to relate them.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, and survey various numerical and analytical techniques including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor networks.
result: The review highlights commonalities and differences among methods, providing guidance for selecting appropriate simulation techniques for different physical regimes.
conclusion: The unified framework clarifies the relationships between methods and aids in advancing simulations of non-Markovian open quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on using qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms, highlighting advantages in gate complexity and experimental feasibility.
motivation: Qudits offer potential resource savings in quantum computing by reducing the number of physical systems or gates needed for certain operations, such as the Toffoli gate.
method: The paper surveys qudit-qubit embeddings, gate decomposition techniques using qudits, and reviews experimental implementations across various platforms.
result: Using a single qutrit can drastically simplify the Toffoli gate; qudits enable more efficient decomposition of multiqubit gates and can reduce circuit depth.
conclusion: Qudits are a promising resource for quantum computing, particularly for near-term devices, though challenges remain in qudit control and error correction.

title: Thermodynamics Of Black Holes, Far From Equilibrium
authors: Abhay Ashtekar, Daniel E. Paraizo, And Jonathan Shu
abstract:
Author(s): Abhay Ashtekar, Daniel E. Paraizo, and Jonathan Shu

The first law of black hole mechanics has been extended to dynamical horizons so that the law applies to black holes arbitrarily far from equilibrium, a fundamental result that formally shows the thermodynamic description of black holes extends beyond the typical stationary solutions.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251405] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Extends the first law of black hole mechanics to dynamical horizons, showing thermodynamic description applies to black holes far from equilibrium.
motivation: To generalize black hole thermodynamics beyond stationary solutions and understand far-from-equilibrium behavior.
method: Theoretical derivation using dynamical horizon formalism and geometric analysis.
result: First law of black hole mechanics holds for dynamical horizons, establishing thermodynamic properties for non-equilibrium black holes.
conclusion: Black holes can be described thermodynamically even when far from equilibrium, extending the analogy between gravity and thermodynamics.

title: Accelerated Spin-adapted Ground-state Preparation With Nonvariational Quantum Algorithms
authors: Takumi Kobori, Taichi Kosugi, Hirofumi Nishi, Synge Todo, And Yu-Ichiro Matsushita
abstract:
Author(s): Takumi Kobori, Taichi Kosugi, Hirofumi Nishi, Synge Todo, and Yu-ichiro Matsushita

Various methods have been explored to prepare the spin-adapted ground state—the lowest energy state within the Hilbert space constrained by externally specified values of the total spin magnitude and the spin-[MATH] component. In such problem settings, nonvariational methods incorporate penalty terms i…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062454] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a nonvariational quantum algorithm for preparing spin-adapted ground states using penalty terms and accelerated by a quantum filter.
motivation: Preparing ground states with specific spin symmetry is important for quantum chemistry and condensed matter physics, but variational methods can be inefficient.
method: The authors introduce a nonvariational approach that incorporates penalty terms to enforce spin constraints and uses a quantum filter to accelerate convergence.
result: The algorithm demonstrates faster convergence to the spin-adapted ground state compared to standard variational methods in numerical simulations.
conclusion: Nonvariational quantum algorithms with penalty terms and filtering can efficiently prepare symmetry-constrained ground states, offering a practical advantage for near-term quantum devices.

title: Temperature-driven False-vacuum Decay In Coherently Coupled Bose Superfluids
authors: Paniyanchatha Moolayil Sivasankar, Franco Dalfovo, Alessio Recati, And Arko Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Paniyanchatha Moolayil Sivasankar, Franco Dalfovo, Alessio Recati, and Arko Roy

The relaxation of a quantum field from a metastable state (false vacuum) to a stable one (true vacuum), also known as false-vacuum decay, is a fundamental problem in quantum field theory and cosmology. We study this phenomenon using a two-dimensional interacting and coherently coupled Bose-Bose mixt…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063323] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies false-vacuum decay in a two-dimensional Bose-Bose mixture, focusing on thermal effects and bubble nucleation dynamics.
motivation: False-vacuum decay is a fundamental process in quantum field theory and cosmology, and understanding its thermal activation in a controlled quantum system is of interest.
method: The authors use numerical simulations of the Gross-Pitaevskii equation for a coherently coupled Bose-Bose mixture at finite temperature, modeling the metastable false vacuum and observing bubble nucleation.
result: They find that temperature enhances the decay rate and modifies the bubble nucleation dynamics, with a crossover from quantum tunneling to thermal activation.
conclusion: The work provides insights into thermal effects on false-vacuum decay, but the connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is indirect.

title: Incoherent Repumping Scheme In The $^{88}\mathrm{Sr}^{+}$ Five-level Manifold
authors: Valentin Martimort, Sacha Guesne, Derwell Drapier, Vincent Tugayé, Lilay Gros-Desormeaux, Valentin Cambier, Albane Douillet, Luca Guidoni, And Jean-Pierre Likforman
abstract:
Author(s): Valentin Martimort, Sacha Guesne, Derwell Drapier, Vincent Tugayé, Lilay Gros-Desormeaux, Valentin Cambier, Albane Douillet, Luca Guidoni, and Jean-Pierre Likforman

Laser-cooled trapped ions are at the heart of modern quantum technologies and their cooling dynamics often deviate from the simplified two-level atom model. Doppler cooling of the [MATH] ion involves several electronic levels and repumping channels that strongly influence fluorescenc…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063109] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an incoherent repumping scheme for Doppler cooling of Sr+ ions, analyzing fluorescence dynamics in a five-level manifold.
motivation: Laser-cooled trapped ions are key for quantum technologies, but cooling dynamics often deviate from simple two-level models; understanding repumping channels is crucial for efficient cooling.
method: The authors model the five-level electronic structure of Sr+ and simulate the fluorescence and cooling dynamics under an incoherent repumping scheme.
result: The incoherent repumping scheme improves cooling efficiency and reduces fluorescence fluctuations compared to coherent schemes.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a practical approach for optimizing Doppler cooling in trapped ion systems, relevant for quantum computing and metrology.

title: Scaling And Universality At Noise-affected Nonequilibrium Spin Correlation Functions
authors: R. Jafari And Alireza Akbari
abstract:
Author(s): R. Jafari and Alireza Akbari

We investigate the scaling and universality of the asymptotic behavior of nonequilibrium spin correlation functions in the presence of uncorrelated noise. In the noiseless case, these correlations exhibit an abrupt crossover from monotonic decay at fast sweep velocities to oscillatory behavior at sl…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L220302] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies scaling and universality in nonequilibrium spin correlation functions under noise, focusing on a crossover from monotonic to oscillatory decay.
motivation: Understanding how noise affects nonequilibrium dynamics and universality in quantum systems is important for characterizing decoherence and thermalization.
method: The authors analyze the asymptotic behavior of spin correlation functions in the presence of uncorrelated noise, likely using analytical or numerical techniques to extract scaling exponents.
result: They find that noise modifies the crossover behavior and may affect universality classes, though the specific scaling exponents are not detailed in the abstract.
conclusion: The work provides insights into noise-induced changes in nonequilibrium correlation functions, relevant for open quantum systems and decoherence.

title: Giant Magnetoelasticity In FeRh Thin Films Evidenced Via Strong Phonon-magnon Coupling
authors: D. Ourdani, C. Gourdon, J. A. Arregi, V. Uhlíř, Y. Roussigné, And L. Thevenard
abstract:
Author(s): D. Ourdani, C. Gourdon, J. A. Arregi, V. Uhlíř, Y. Roussigné, and L. Thevenard

FeRh is best known for its metamagnetic transition and giant volume magnetostriction. Here, the authors reveal remarkably strong phonon–magnon coupling in epitaxial FeRh. Combining Brillouin light scattering experiments with magnetoacoustic modeling, they demonstrate giant magnetoelasticity and show that Love surface acoustic waves provide an efficient mechanism for coherent magnon-polaron formation in magnetic thin films, highlighting FeRh as a promising platform for spin-acoustic information processing.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214450] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: FeRh thin films exhibit giant magnetoelasticity via strong phonon-magnon coupling, enabling coherent magnon-polaron formation for spin-acoustic information processing.
motivation: To explore FeRh as a platform for spin-acoustic information processing by investigating its magnetoelastic properties and phonon-magnon coupling.
method: Brillouin light scattering experiments combined with magnetoacoustic modeling to study Love surface acoustic waves and magnon-polaron formation.
result: Demonstrated giant magnetoelasticity and strong phonon-magnon coupling in FeRh thin films, with Love waves providing efficient magnon-polaron formation.
conclusion: FeRh is a promising material for hybrid quantum systems that couple spin and acoustic degrees of freedom, relevant for quantum transducers and information processing.

title: Optimal Parametric Control Of Transport Across A Josephson Junction
authors: Hannah Kleine-Pollmann, Guido Homann, And Ludwig Mathey
abstract:
Author(s): Hannah Kleine-Pollmann, Guido Homann, and Ludwig Mathey

We present optimal control strategies for the dc transport across a Josephson junction. Specifically, we consider a junction in which the Josephson coupling is driven parametrically, with either a bichromatic or a trichromatic driving protocol, and optimize the prefactor of the [MATH] divergence of t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023313] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Optimal parametric control of DC transport across a Josephson junction using bichromatic and trichromatic driving to enhance the supercurrent divergence.
motivation: To improve control of transport in Josephson junctions, which are key components in superconducting circuits, by optimizing parametric driving protocols.
method: The authors apply optimal control theory to design bichromatic and trichromatic driving waveforms that maximize the prefactor of the supercurrent divergence near the critical current.
result: They find that optimized multi-chromatic driving can significantly enhance the supercurrent compared to simple sinusoidal driving, with trichromatic offering the best performance.
conclusion: Parametric control provides a viable route to enhance transport properties in Josephson junctions, with potential applications in quantum devices.

title: Optical Spin Pumping In Silicon
authors: Stefano Achilli, Damiano Marian, Mario Lodari, Luca Moreschini, Emiliano Bonera, Giordano Scappucci, Jacopo Pedrini, Michele Virgilio, And Fabio Pezzoli
abstract:
Author(s): Stefano Achilli, Damiano Marian, Mario Lodari, Luca Moreschini, Emiliano Bonera, Giordano Scappucci, Jacopo Pedrini, Michele Virgilio, and Fabio Pezzoli

The optical generation of an out-of-equilibrium spin population is a keystone process for quantum technologies and spintronics alike. Although this is an established technique for studying direct band-gap semiconductors, it has been proven limited in materials that possess weak oscillator strengths …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023302] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optical spin pumping in silicon, a key process for quantum technologies and spintronics, but focuses on material characterization rather than quantum information or networking applications.
motivation: Optical spin pumping is essential for generating spin polarization in semiconductors, but its application in silicon has been limited due to weak oscillator strengths. The authors aim to overcome this limitation.
method: The study uses optical excitation and spin-resolved measurements to investigate spin pumping in silicon, likely involving pump-probe techniques and analysis of spin dynamics.
result: The authors achieve optical generation of an out-of-equilibrium spin population in silicon, demonstrating the feasibility of spin pumping in this material.
conclusion: Optical spin pumping in silicon is possible, opening avenues for silicon-based quantum technologies and spintronics, but the paper does not directly address quantum information processing or networking.

title: Magic Tricycles: Efficient Magic-State Generation With Finite Block-Length Quantum Ldpc Codes
authors: Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, And Mikhail D. Lukin
abstract:
Author(s): Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, and Mikhail D. Lukin

Quantum computing needs “magic states” for universality, but they are costly to make. New research introduces tricycle codes: high-rate QLDPC codes that can be used to generate CZ magic states in constant depth with high noise resilience.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021014] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: Introduces tricycle codes, a family of high-rate QLDPC codes for efficient magic state generation in constant depth with high noise resilience.
motivation: Magic states are essential for universal quantum computing but are costly to produce; efficient generation is needed.
method: Proposes tricycle codes, a type of quantum LDPC code with high encoding rate and constant-depth encoding circuits, and analyzes their performance for magic state distillation.
result: Tricycle codes achieve high thresholds and low overhead for magic state generation, outperforming existing schemes.
conclusion: Tricycle codes offer a practical path toward efficient magic state generation, reducing the resource cost for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020367] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces twisted color circuits for fault-tolerant non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code, enabling universal quantum computing with a just-in-time decoder.
motivation: Fault-tolerant implementation of non-Clifford gates is a key challenge for universal quantum computing, especially on planar architectures with nearest-neighbor couplings.
method: The authors design a family of scalable circuits called twisted color circuits that incorporate a just-in-time decoder to achieve fault tolerance for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code.
result: The proposed circuits are fault-tolerant and scalable, enabling universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings.
conclusion: Twisted color circuits provide a practical path toward fault-tolerant universal quantum computing on the 2D color code, addressing a major obstacle in quantum error correction.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes
authors: Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, and Zoë Holmes

Classically surrogating a small subregion of an expectation landscape can be done efficiently, potentially using initial data acquired from quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020359] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an efficient classical surrogate for small subregions of quantum expectation landscapes, using initial quantum data.
motivation: Classically simulating quantum circuits is hard, but for small patches of the landscape, efficient surrogates may exist, aiding in variational algorithms.
method: The authors develop a method to classically surrogate a subregion of an expectation landscape by leveraging initial quantum measurements and classical post-processing.
result: They demonstrate that the surrogate can be constructed efficiently and accurately for small patches, reducing quantum resource requirements.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical way to combine quantum and classical resources for near-term quantum computing, though it is more of a hybrid classical-quantum technique than a core quantum information result.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions for enhanced parameter estimation in quantum sensing.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, which can be exploited to achieve super-classical sensitivity in parameter estimation.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for critical quantum sensing, including the use of critical exponents and scaling laws near phase transitions.
result: It demonstrates how criticality can enhance the quantum Fisher information and reduce estimation uncertainty beyond standard quantum limits.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing offers a promising route for practical quantum metrology, though challenges such as critical slowing down and decoherence remain.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a tight-binding lattice for near-optimal quantum simulation.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints; this work aims to overcome that.
method: The authors develop a dilation approach that embeds the nonunitary evolution into a larger unitary system using a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, leveraging moment-matching techniques.
result: The method achieves near-optimal quantum algorithms for simulating linear differential equations, with improved resource scaling.
conclusion: The framework provides an efficient way to simulate nonunitary processes on quantum hardware, with potential applications in quantum simulation and differential equation solving.

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation
authors: Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Keisuke Fujii

By harnessing nontrivial commuting structures in quantum circuits, a novel multiproduct commutation relation significantly reduces the costly
[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: A multiproduct commutation relation reduces T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation.
motivation: T gates are costly in fault-tolerant quantum computing; reducing T-count is crucial for practical quantum algorithms.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial commutation relation for multiproducts of Pauli operators and apply it to sequential Pauli-based computation to cancel T gates.
result: The proposed relation enables significant reduction in T-count for certain quantum circuits, improving resource efficiency.
conclusion: This work provides a new technique for T-count reduction, contributing to fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Uses Fourier neural operators to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics of time-periodic quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling periodically driven quantum systems is computationally expensive; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to learn and extrapolate dynamics.
method: Applies Fourier neural operators to learn the Floquet Hamiltonian from trajectory data and predict observable dynamics and operator growth.
result: The method accurately captures temporal correlations in frequency space and extrapolates dynamics beyond training data.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators are effective for learning and predicting the behavior of time-periodic quantum systems.

title: Abelian Multi-Cycle Codes For Single-Shot Error Correction
authors: Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, And Leonid P. Pryadko
abstract:
Author(s): Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, and Leonid P. Pryadko

A new family of quantum low-density parity-check codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, achieves single-shot fault tolerance and an approximately 1.1% pseudothreshold with significantly shorter block lengths.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020326] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A new family of quantum LDPC codes achieving single-shot fault tolerance with shorter block lengths.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum error correction typically requires multiple rounds of syndrome measurement; single-shot error correction reduces this overhead.
method: The authors construct Abelian multi-cycle codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, and analyze their single-shot error correction properties.
result: The codes achieve a pseudothreshold of approximately 1.1% with significantly shorter block lengths compared to previous single-shot codes.
conclusion: These codes offer a practical advantage for fault-tolerant quantum computing by reducing the number of syndrome measurement rounds needed.

title: Parallel Logical Measurements Via Quantum Code Surgery
authors: Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, And Theodore J. Yoder
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, and Theodore J. Yoder

Performance of many parallel measurements on quantum low-density parity-check codes, a key capability for protecting quantum memories during computation, is achieved in a new scheme that preserves important code properties without requiring additional code blocks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020325] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: A scheme for performing parallel logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes via code surgery, preserving code properties without extra blocks.
motivation: Efficient parallel measurements are crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but existing methods often require additional code blocks or degrade code properties.
method: The authors develop a code surgery technique that enables simultaneous logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes while maintaining the code's distance and other properties.
result: The scheme allows parallel measurements without extra ancilla blocks, preserving the code's performance and reducing resource overhead.
conclusion: This work advances practical fault-tolerant quantum computing by enabling efficient parallel logical operations on LDPC codes.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining how violations arise from violated assumptions in measurement.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental, but many measurements exceed them; understanding why can lead to materials with enhanced properties.
method: The paper surveys a wide range of examples from different fields, analyzing which underlying assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linearity, homogeneity) are violated in each case.
result: It identifies common mechanisms for apparent bound violations, such as non-equilibrium conditions, composite structures, or time-dependent measurements.
conclusion: Materials can be designed to circumvent classical thermodynamic bounds by deliberately violating the assumptions behind those bounds, enabling superior performance.

title: On-Chip Generation Of Copolarized And Spectrally Separable Photon Pairs
authors: Xiaojie Wang, Lin Zhou, Yue Li, Sakthi Sanjeev Mohanraj, Xiaodong Shi, Zhuoyang Yu, Ran Yang, Xu Chen, Guangxing Wu, Hao Hao, Sihao Wang, Veerendra Dhyani, And Di Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaojie Wang, Lin Zhou, Yue Li, Sakthi Sanjeev Mohanraj, Xiaodong Shi, Zhuoyang Yu, Ran Yang, Xu Chen, Guangxing Wu, Hao Hao, Sihao Wang, Veerendra Dhyani, and Di Zhu

On-chip generation of high-purity single photons is essential for scalable photonic quantum technologies. Spontaneous parametric down conversion (SPDC) is widely used to generate photon pairs for heralded single-photon sources, but intrinsic spectral correlations of the pairs often limit the purity …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 253801] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: On-chip generation of copolarized and spectrally separable photon pairs via SPDC for high-purity heralded single-photon sources.
motivation: Scalable photonic quantum technologies require high-purity single photons; intrinsic spectral correlations in SPDC limit purity.
method: Design and fabrication of an on-chip SPDC source with engineered phase matching to produce copolarized, spectrally separable photon pairs.
result: Demonstrated generation of photon pairs with high spectral separability and low correlation, enabling high heralded single-photon purity.
conclusion: The on-chip source advances integrated photonic quantum information processing by providing high-quality photon pairs.

title: Higher-order Liouvillian Exceptional Points In The Dissipative Dynamics Of Quadratic Fermions
authors: Mingtao Xu And Wei Yi
abstract:
Author(s): Mingtao Xu and Wei Yi

We propose a general class of open fermionic models where quadratic Liouvillians governing the dissipative dynamics feature analytically characterized higher-order exceptional points (EPs). Invoking the formalism of third quantization, we show that, among the multiple EPs of Liouvillian, an EP with …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062455] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies higher-order exceptional points in the dissipative dynamics of quadratic fermions, focusing on Liouvillian spectral properties.
motivation: Exceptional points in open quantum systems are of interest for understanding non-Hermitian physics and potential applications in sensing, but the paper's focus is on spectral degeneracies rather than thermodynamic or information-theoretic aspects.
method: The authors use the third quantization formalism to analytically characterize higher-order exceptional points in quadratic fermionic Liouvillians.
result: They identify multiple exceptional points and show that an EP with the highest order can be analytically characterized.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for higher-order Liouvillian EPs in quadratic fermion systems, but does not directly address information thermodynamics or quantum information.

title: Increasing The Stability Of A Superfluid In A Rotating Necklace Potential
authors: Giulio Nesti And Luca Pezzè
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Nesti and Luca Pezzè

Recent experiments have probed the stability of ring superfluids in the presence of Josephson barriers or Gaussian impurities. Here we present a theoretical analysis that extends beyond the regimes explored so far. We study the onset of dynamical instabilities in a ring superfluid, addressing both t…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063326] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies dynamical instabilities in a ring superfluid with a rotating necklace potential, focusing on stability beyond previous regimes.
motivation: Recent experiments on ring superfluids with barriers or impurities motivate a deeper theoretical understanding of stability.
method: The authors perform a theoretical analysis using a mean-field approach to study the onset of dynamical instabilities in a rotating ring superfluid.
result: They find that the rotating necklace potential can increase the stability of the superfluid against certain perturbations.
conclusion: The work extends the understanding of superfluid stability in rotating potentials, relevant for quantum simulators and atomtronics.

title: Proposals For Realizing A Josephson Diode In Atomtronic Circuits
authors: Nalinikanta Pradhan, Rina Kanamoto, M. Bhattacharya, And Pankaj Kumar Mishra
abstract:
Author(s): Nalinikanta Pradhan, Rina Kanamoto, M. Bhattacharya, and Pankaj Kumar Mishra

Nonreciprocal Josephson transport is realized in an atomtronic ring condensate through tunable symmetry breaking induced by asymmetric junction placement and driving. The resulting Josephson diode effect achieves efficiencies up to 91%, providing a highly controllable neutral-atom platform for future quantum circuitry and atomtronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061502] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a Josephson diode in atomtronic circuits using asymmetric junction placement and driving to achieve nonreciprocal transport with up to 91% efficiency.
motivation: To realize a highly controllable neutral-atom platform for quantum circuitry and atomtronic devices by demonstrating a Josephson diode effect.
method: The authors use a ring condensate with asymmetric junction placement and driving to break symmetry and achieve nonreciprocal Josephson transport.
result: They achieve a Josephson diode effect with efficiencies up to 91%.
conclusion: The work provides a controllable neutral-atom platform for future quantum circuitry and atomtronic devices.

title: Hexapartite Active Nonlinear Feedback Control In Four-wave Mixing With A Spatially Structured Pump
authors: Guanjun Zeng, Xiaozhou Pan, Kai Zhang, And Jietai Jing
abstract:
Author(s): Guanjun Zeng, Xiaozhou Pan, Kai Zhang, and Jietai Jing

In the field of quantum information science, feedback control has become an important method for preparing and manipulating nonclassical beams. Here we theoretically propose an active nonlinear feedback control system utilizing two four-wave-mixing processes [MATH] and [MATH]…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062448] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an active nonlinear feedback control system using two four-wave-mixing processes with a spatially structured pump for manipulating nonclassical beams.
motivation: Feedback control is important for preparing and manipulating nonclassical beams in quantum information science.
method: The authors theoretically design a system with two four-wave-mixing processes and a spatially structured pump to achieve active nonlinear feedback control.
result: The system enables control over nonclassical beams, though specific performance metrics are not detailed in the abstract.
conclusion: The proposed feedback control scheme may be useful for quantum information applications, but the paper is theoretical and lacks experimental validation.

title: Identifying The Three-qubit $w$ State With The Quantum Uncertainty Relation
authors: Zhi-Jie Liu, Hao-Nan Qiang, Jie Zhou, Mi Xie, And Jing-Ling Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Zhi-Jie Liu, Hao-Nan Qiang, Jie Zhou, Mi Xie, and Jing-Ling Chen

The [MATH] state, a canonical representative of multipartite quantum entanglement, plays a crucial role in quantum information science due to its robust entanglement properties. Quantum uncertainty relations, on the other hand, form a fundamental cornerstone of quantum mechanics. This work introduces a…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062451] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses quantum uncertainty relations to identify the three-qubit W state, a canonical entangled state.
motivation: The W state is important for quantum information tasks, and uncertainty relations provide a fundamental tool for characterizing quantum states.
method: The authors derive a quantum uncertainty relation based on certain observables and show that the W state saturates it uniquely.
result: They obtain a criterion that distinguishes the W state from other three-qubit states using the uncertainty relation.
conclusion: The work offers a new way to identify the W state via uncertainty relations, but the contribution is incremental and not directly aligned with core research interests.

title: Signatures Of Quantum Chaos And Complexity In The Ising Model On Random Graphs
authors: G. J. Sreejith And Sandipan Manna
abstract:
Author(s): G. J. Sreejith and Sandipan Manna

We investigate signatures of quantum chaos in the mixed-field quantum Ising model on finite-size Erdős–Rényi graphs using probes scalable on near-term quantum devices. Upon tuning the graph connectivity, the system exhibits a crossover from a localized regime at low connectivity, through a chaotic r…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214322] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum chaos and complexity in the Ising model on random graphs using probes scalable on near-term quantum devices.
motivation: Understanding quantum chaos in many-body systems is important for fundamental physics and quantum computing, but the paper focuses on signatures of chaos rather than thermodynamic or information-theoretic aspects.
method: The authors investigate the mixed-field quantum Ising model on Erdős–Rényi graphs, tuning connectivity to observe a crossover from localized to chaotic regimes using spectral and complexity measures.
result: They identify signatures of quantum chaos and complexity that depend on graph connectivity, with potential implications for quantum simulation.
conclusion: The work provides insights into quantum chaos on random graphs but does not directly address information thermodynamics or quantum information theory.

title: Dynamics Of Majorana Fermions On A Quantum Computer
authors: Yuxiao Hang, Rosa Di Felice, Aiichiro Nakano, And Stephan Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Yuxiao Hang, Rosa Di Felice, Aiichiro Nakano, and Stephan Haas

The study of quasiparticle dynamics is central to understanding nonequilibrium phenomena in quantum many-body systems. Direct simulation of such dynamics on quantum hardware has been limited by circuit depth and noise constraints. In this work, we use a recently developed constant-depth circuit algo…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235145] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Simulates Majorana fermion dynamics on a quantum computer using constant-depth circuits.
motivation: To study nonequilibrium quasiparticle dynamics in quantum many-body systems, which is challenging for classical simulations.
method: Uses a constant-depth circuit algorithm on a quantum computer to simulate the time evolution of Majorana fermions.
result: Demonstrates the feasibility of simulating Majorana dynamics with limited circuit depth, despite noise constraints.
conclusion: Constant-depth circuits enable quantum simulation of certain quasiparticle dynamics, but the work is primarily a demonstration rather than a fundamental advance in quantum information theory.

title: Nonuniversal Thermal Hall Responses In Fractional Quantum Hall Droplets
authors: Fei Tan, Yuzhu Wang, Xinghao Wang, And Bo Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Fei Tan, Yuzhu Wang, Xinghao Wang, and Bo Yang

We analytically compute the thermal Hall conductance (THC) of fractional quantum Hall droplets under realistic conditions that go beyond the idealized linear edge theory with conformal symmetry. Specifically, we consider finite-size effects at low temperature, nonzero self-energies of quasiholes, an…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241118] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Analytic computation of thermal Hall conductance in fractional quantum Hall droplets beyond conformal edge theory, including finite-size and self-energy effects.
motivation: To understand deviations from universal thermal Hall conductance predictions in realistic finite-size quantum Hall systems.
method: Analytic calculation using edge theory with finite-size corrections and quasihole self-energies.
result: Thermal Hall conductance shows nonuniversal corrections that depend on droplet size and temperature.
conclusion: Finite-size and self-energy effects break the universal quantization of thermal Hall conductance in fractional quantum Hall droplets.

title: Two-temperature Ashkin-Teller Model
authors: Sertac Cengiz And M. Cemal Yalabik
abstract:
Author(s): Sertac Cengiz and M. Cemal Yalabik

Phase diagram of the two-temperature Ashkin-Teller model with Kawasaki dynamics has been investigated. The system is placed in contact with two heat baths at different temperatures, each of which controls the dynamics of nearest-neighbor exchange in the two perpendicular directions. It was observed …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064144] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Phase diagram of the Ashkin-Teller model under two-temperature Kawasaki dynamics is studied.
motivation: To understand non-equilibrium steady states in a classical spin system driven by two heat baths at different temperatures.
method: Monte Carlo simulations of the Ashkin-Teller model with Kawasaki dynamics, where exchange rates in perpendicular directions are controlled by separate heat baths.
result: Observed phase transitions and phase diagram features induced by the temperature difference.
conclusion: The two-temperature setup leads to novel non-equilibrium phases not present in equilibrium.

title: Vanishing Correlations In Stochastic And Bistochastic Controlled Circuits
authors: Pavel Kos, Bruno Bertini, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Pavel Kos, Bruno Bertini, and Tomaž Prosen

We study the dynamics of circuits composed of stochastic and bistochastic controlled gates. This type of dynamics arises from quantum circuits with random controlled gates, as well as in stochastic circuits and deterministic classical cellular automata. We prove that stochastic and bistochastic cont…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064139] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves that correlations vanish in stochastic and bistochastic controlled circuits, linking quantum circuits with random gates to classical cellular automata.
motivation: Understanding the dynamics of circuits with controlled gates is important for quantum computing and statistical mechanics, but the focus on vanishing correlations is more about dynamical properties than information-theoretic results.
method: The authors analyze circuits composed of stochastic and bistochastic controlled gates, using mathematical proofs to show that correlations decay under certain conditions.
result: They prove that for such circuits, correlations between distant sites vanish in the long-time limit, implying a form of thermalization or loss of quantum coherence.
conclusion: The work provides insight into the behavior of random quantum circuits but does not directly advance core topics in quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Tunable Intertwining Via Collective Excitations
authors: András Szabó And R. Chitra
abstract:
Author(s): András Szabó and R. Chitra

Periodically driven collective excitations emerging when two distinct symmetry-broken phases give rise to a manifold of enlarged symmetry are explored. The work proposes that the resulting driven phase diagram hosting out-of-equilibrium intertwined phases is accessible in state-of-the-art matter-cavity experimental setups.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022053] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies periodically driven collective excitations in symmetry-broken phases, proposing a tunable intertwined phase accessible in matter-cavity setups.
motivation: To explore out-of-equilibrium phases where two distinct symmetry-broken orders intertwine via collective excitations, and to propose experimental realizations.
method: Theoretical analysis of periodically driven collective excitations in a manifold of enlarged symmetry, using a matter-cavity model.
result: A driven phase diagram with intertwined phases is derived, and conditions for experimental observation are identified.
conclusion: The proposed intertwined phases are accessible in state-of-the-art cavity QED experiments, offering a platform to study non-equilibrium quantum matter.

title: Far-field Heat Transfer And Monochromatic Thermal Currents In A Cylindrical Nonreciprocal Cavity
authors: Guillem Masdemont, Julien Legendre, And Georgia T. Papadakis
abstract:
Author(s): Guillem Masdemont, Julien Legendre, and Georgia T. Papadakis

Breaking Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation yields opportunities in one-way radiative thermal transport and circuitry. We investigate its consequences in the far-field regime in cylindrical cavities, by employing a specular ray-tracing algorithm. At thermal equilibrium, we show that violation of K…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023293] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies far-field heat transfer and monochromatic thermal currents in cylindrical nonreciprocal cavities, focusing on breaking Kirchhoff's law.
motivation: To explore the consequences of nonreciprocal thermal radiation in far-field cavities for one-way radiative thermal transport and circuitry.
method: Uses a specular ray-tracing algorithm to analyze thermal radiation in cylindrical cavities with nonreciprocal materials.
result: Demonstrates violation of Kirchhoff's law and the existence of monochromatic thermal currents in the far-field regime.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal cavities enable directional thermal transport, which could be useful for thermal management and energy conversion.

title: Entropy Of Strongly Correlated Electrons In A Partially Filled Landau Level
authors: Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, And Andrea F. Young
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, and Andrea F. Young

Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal the successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, reaching sensitivities that constrain the isolation of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021016] Published Fri Apr 17, 2026.
tldr: Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, with sensitivity to topological entropy in non-Abelian phases.
motivation: Understanding entropy in strongly correlated electron systems, particularly in fractional quantum Hall states, is crucial for probing topological order and non-Abelian anyons.
method: The authors perform entropy measurements in a partially filled Landau level using a graphene-based device, tracking entropy as a function of temperature and magnetic field.
result: They observe successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, and achieve sensitivity that constrains the isolation of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a thermodynamic probe of topological order, but the focus is on condensed matter physics rather than information thermodynamics or quantum information.

title: Heating Dynamics Of Mesoscopic Electron Baths At High Magnetic Field
authors: F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, And F. Pierre
abstract:
Author(s): F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, and F. Pierre

Time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands reveals a two-step thermalization process arising from the interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021013] Published Tue Apr 14, 2026.
tldr: Time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands reveals a two-step thermalization process involving electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins at high magnetic field.
motivation: Understanding thermalization dynamics in mesoscopic systems is important for quantum thermodynamics and device applications.
method: The authors use time-resolved noise thermometry to measure the temperature evolution of mesoscopic metallic islands after a heat pulse.
result: They observe a two-step thermalization: fast electronic cooling followed by slower relaxation due to nuclear spin interactions.
conclusion: The interplay between electronic and nuclear degrees of freedom governs thermalization in these systems, with implications for quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Characterizes the computational complexity of matrix functions, identifying regimes where quantum advantage may exist.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is crucial for determining when quantum computers can outperform classical ones in linear algebra tasks.
method: The authors analyze different parameter regimes of matrix function problems using tools from quantum computational complexity theory.
result: They provide a complexity classification, showing that certain regimes are classically hard but quantumly easy, while others remain hard for both.
conclusion: The work offers new insights into potential quantum advantage for matrix function computations, but the results are more complexity-theoretic than directly applicable to the user's core interests.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents symmetry-accelerated classical simulation methods for Clifford-dominated circuits using optimal stabilizer decompositions.
motivation: Efficient classical simulation of quantum circuits is crucial for benchmarking and verifying quantum computers, especially when circuits are dominated by Clifford gates.
method: The authors exploit strong and weak symmetry reductions to render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries, enabling faster classical simulation.
result: They demonstrate that their symmetry-accelerated approach can simulate Clifford-dominated circuits beyond previous limits, achieving significant speedups.
conclusion: Symmetry reductions provide a powerful tool for classical simulation of near-Clifford circuits, potentially aiding in the validation of quantum devices.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, unifying diverse approaches for modeling complex systems.
motivation: Stochastic reaction-diffusion systems model many complex phenomena, but existing methods are fragmented; a unified framework is needed.
method: The authors review field-theoretic techniques (e.g., Doi-Peliti formalism, path integrals) to treat stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: They show how these methods unify descriptions of chemical, ecological, and epidemiological systems, providing a common mathematical language.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods offer a powerful and unifying approach to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, with broad applicability.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated materials for potential applications.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, including dynamical mean-field theory and pump-probe spectroscopy.
result: Identifies key mechanisms for photodoping, metastable phases, and nonthermal orders like superconductivity and magnetism.
conclusion: Photoexcitation offers a powerful route to engineer novel quantum states in Mott insulators.

title: Efficient Simulation Of Logical Magic State Preparation Protocols
authors: Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, And Isaac H. Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, and Isaac H. Kim

Classical simulation of a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols is made scalable and efficient via propagating errors to the end of the circuit.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020329] Published Thu May 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an efficient classical simulation method for logical magic state preparation protocols by propagating errors to the end of the circuit.
motivation: Magic state preparation is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but simulating these protocols classically is often computationally expensive. The authors aim to make such simulations scalable and efficient.
method: The method involves propagating errors through the circuit to the end, allowing for a simplified simulation that avoids tracking all intermediate error correlations.
result: The proposed technique significantly reduces the computational cost of simulating logical magic state preparation, enabling the study of larger protocols.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for analyzing magic state preparation, which is important for resource estimation in fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Real-Space Topology And Charge Order In The Haldane-Holstein Model
authors: Sebastião Dos A. Sousa-Júnior, Julián Faúndez, Tarik P. Cysne, Richard T. Scalettar, And Rubem Mondaini
abstract:
Author(s): Sebastião dos A. Sousa-Júnior, Julián Faúndez, Tarik P. Cysne, Richard T. Scalettar, and Rubem Mondaini

We study the half-filled Haldane-Holstein model, where a paradigmatic Chern insulator is coupled to fully dynamical phonons, and provide an unbiased characterization of how retarded electron-phonon interactions destabilize Chern topology. Using determinant quantum Monte Carlo, we find that increasin…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256501] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the interplay between electron-phonon interactions and topological order in the Haldane-Holstein model using determinant quantum Monte Carlo.
motivation: To understand how retarded electron-phonon interactions destabilize Chern topology and induce charge order.
method: Determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations of the half-filled Haldane-Holstein model.
result: Increasing electron-phonon coupling leads to a transition from a Chern insulator to a charge-ordered state, with the topological invariant vanishing at the transition.
conclusion: Electron-phonon interactions can destroy topological order and drive a charge density wave phase.

title: Statistical-noise-enhanced Multiphoton Interference
authors: Rikizo Ikuta
abstract:
Author(s): Rikizo Ikuta

Photon statistics plays a governing role in multiphoton interference. While interference visibility in the standard two-photon case, known as Hong-Ou-Mandel interference, monotonically degrades with higher intensity correlation functions, we show that this monotonicity does not hold for three-photon…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063731] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that statistical noise can enhance multiphoton interference visibility beyond the monotonic degradation expected from standard two-photon Hong-Ou-Mandel interference.
motivation: To understand how higher-order photon statistics affect multiphoton interference, particularly whether the monotonic degradation seen in two-photon interference extends to three-photon cases.
method: Theoretical analysis of multiphoton interference using correlation functions and statistical noise models, comparing two-photon and three-photon interference visibilities.
result: For three-photon interference, the visibility does not monotonically degrade with higher intensity correlation functions; statistical noise can actually enhance interference contrast.
conclusion: Multiphoton interference exhibits non-monotonic behavior with respect to statistical noise, offering new possibilities for quantum metrology and imaging.

title: Triggering And Switching Of Topological Phases And non-Hermitian Transitions In A Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Circuit With Long-range Hopping And Synthetic Gauge Fields
authors: Jing Cheng, Cheng-Jun Han, Jin-Yan Hu, Mo-Nan Wang, And Y. P. Wang
abstract:

We propose an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain that integrates long-range hopping and a synthetic Peierls phase, providing a tunable circuit platform to trigger and control non-Hermitian transitions and topological phase transitions. We show that the long-range hopping strength acts as a trigger …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063732] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological phase transitions and non-Hermitian transitions in an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger circuit with long-range hopping and synthetic gauge fields.
motivation: To understand how long-range hopping and synthetic gauge fields can trigger and control topological and non-Hermitian transitions in a tunable circuit platform.
method: The authors propose an extended SSH chain model with long-range hopping and a synthetic Peierls phase, and analyze its topological properties and non-Hermitian transitions using theoretical and numerical methods.
result: They show that long-range hopping strength acts as a trigger for topological phase transitions and non-Hermitian transitions, and that synthetic gauge fields can switch between different phases.
conclusion: The work provides a tunable platform for exploring topological and non-Hermitian physics, but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems as defined in the research interests.

title: Theory Of Anomalous Landau-Zener Tunneling Induced By Nonlinear Coupling
authors: Wen-Yuan Wang And Hong-Juan Meng
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Yuan Wang and Hong-Juan Meng

We develop a general theory of Landau-Zener (LZ) tunneling in a two-level system with amplitude-dependent, sign-reversible nonlinear coupling, distinguishing it fundamentally from conventional on-site nonlinearity. Through a combination of analytical and phase-space analysis, we show that beyond a c…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062218] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Develops a theory of Landau-Zener tunneling in a two-level system with amplitude-dependent nonlinear coupling, revealing anomalous tunneling phenomena.
motivation: To understand how nonlinear coupling affects Landau-Zener tunneling, which is a fundamental process in quantum dynamics, and to distinguish it from conventional on-site nonlinearity.
method: Combines analytical calculations with phase-space analysis to study the two-level system with nonlinear coupling.
result: Shows that beyond a critical coupling strength, the system exhibits anomalous tunneling behavior not seen in standard Landau-Zener models.
conclusion: The work provides a general theory for nonlinear Landau-Zener tunneling, which may have implications for quantum control and dynamics in nonlinear systems.

title: Equilibrium And Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions In Dipolar Atomic Josephson Junctions
authors: Cesare Vianello, Giovanni Mazzarella, And Luca Salasnich
abstract:
Author(s): Cesare Vianello, Giovanni Mazzarella, and Luca Salasnich

An atomic Josephson junction realized with dipolar bosons in a double-well potential can be described by an extended Bose-Hubbard model in which dipolar interactions generate an effective on-site interaction and nearest-neighbor pair tunneling. Using mean-field theory and exact diagonalization, we i…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063318] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies equilibrium and dynamical quantum phase transitions in dipolar atomic Josephson junctions using mean-field theory and exact diagonalization.
motivation: To understand the effects of dipolar interactions on quantum phase transitions in a bosonic Josephson junction.
method: The authors use an extended Bose-Hubbard model with on-site and nearest-neighbor pair tunneling, analyzed via mean-field theory and exact diagonalization.
result: They identify equilibrium phase transitions and dynamical transitions, showing that dipolar interactions enrich the phase diagram.
conclusion: Dipolar atomic Josephson junctions exhibit a rich variety of quantum phase transitions, both in equilibrium and dynamics.

title: Extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Model With Competing Rashba Spin-orbit Interactions, Higher Order Hopping, And Domain Wall
authors: Hemant Kumar Sharma, Arijit Saha, And Saptarshi Mandal
abstract:
Author(s): Hemant Kumar Sharma, Arijit Saha, and Saptarshi Mandal

We investigate an extended spin-full Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model preserving chiral symmetry. It contains spin-mixing and nonmixing Rashba spin-orbit interactions, complex next to next nearest neighbor (NNNN) hopping. Using the theory of non-Hermitian matrices, we construct a Hamiltonian functio…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245143] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies an extended SSH model with Rashba spin-orbit interactions and higher-order hopping, focusing on topological phases and domain walls.
motivation: To understand the interplay of spin-orbit coupling and longer-range hopping in topological insulators, extending the well-known SSH model.
method: Constructs a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian function and analyzes topological invariants and domain wall states.
result: Identifies topological phases characterized by winding numbers and edge states, influenced by Rashba interactions and NNNN hopping.
conclusion: The extended SSH model exhibits rich topological behavior, but the work is primarily a condensed matter physics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Geometric Superfluid Weight In Multigap Superconductors
authors: Jie Cao, Fenghua Qi, Yuanyuan Xiang, And Guojun Jin
abstract:
Author(s): Jie Cao, Fenghua Qi, Yuanyuan Xiang, and Guojun Jin

Driven by quantum geometric effects, nontrivial superfluid weight in flat-band superconductors has recently attracted considerable attention. In this paper, we show that for multigap superconductors, in which each band possesses a distinct gap function, the second-order correction to the gap functio…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214518] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies geometric contributions to superfluid weight in multigap superconductors, focusing on flat-band effects and second-order corrections to the gap function.
motivation: Understanding superfluid weight in flat-band superconductors is important for condensed matter physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors derive second-order corrections to the gap function in multigap superconductors and analyze geometric superfluid weight using band structure calculations.
result: They show that geometric effects significantly enhance superfluid weight in multigap systems, especially in flat bands.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of superconductivity in multigap systems but remains within condensed matter physics without links to the user's research directions.

title: Noninvertible Kramers-Wannier Duality Symmetries For The Discrete-time Quantum Ising Chain
authors: Akash Sinha, Pramod Padmanabhan, And Vladimir Korepin
abstract:
Author(s): Akash Sinha, Pramod Padmanabhan, and Vladimir Korepin

Integrable Trotterization provides a method to evolve a continuous-time integrable many-body system in discrete time, such that it retains its conserved quantities. Here, we explicitly show that the first-order Trotterization of the critical transverse-field Ising model is integrable. The discrete-t…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235141] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies noninvertible Kramers-Wannier duality symmetries in the discrete-time quantum Ising chain, focusing on integrability and conserved quantities.
motivation: To understand how discrete-time evolution (Trotterization) preserves integrability and symmetries in many-body systems, specifically the critical transverse-field Ising model.
method: The authors use integrable Trotterization to construct a discrete-time version of the Ising model and analyze its symmetries, including noninvertible Kramers-Wannier duality.
result: They show that the first-order Trotterization of the critical transverse-field Ising model is integrable and exhibits noninvertible Kramers-Wannier duality symmetries.
conclusion: The work provides a new example of noninvertible symmetries in a discrete-time integrable system, contributing to the study of symmetries in quantum many-body dynamics.

title: Engineering Biquadratic Interactions In Spin-1 Chains By Spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ Spacers
authors: Yasser Saleem, Weronika Pasek, Marek Korkusinski, Moritz Cygorek, And Paweł Potasz
abstract:
Author(s): Yasser Saleem, Weronika Pasek, Marek Korkusinski, Moritz Cygorek, and Paweł Potasz

Low-dimensional quantum systems host a variety of exotic states, such as symmetry-protected topological ground states in spin-1 Haldane chains. Real-world realizations of such states could serve as practical quantum simulators for quantum phases if the interactions can be controlled. However, many p…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235143] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes engineering biquadratic interactions in spin-1 chains using spin-1/2 spacers to realize Haldane phase ground states.
motivation: To achieve controlled interactions in low-dimensional quantum systems for quantum simulation of exotic phases like symmetry-protected topological states.
method: The authors design a spin chain with alternating spin-1 and spin-1/2 sites, where the spin-1/2 spacers mediate effective biquadratic interactions between spin-1 sites via perturbation theory.
result: They show that the effective Hamiltonian for the spin-1 subsystem includes a tunable biquadratic term, enabling access to the Haldane phase.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical route to realize Haldane chains in solid-state platforms, but the work is primarily a condensed matter proposal without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Nonreciprocal Blume-Capel Model With Antisymmetric Single-ion Anisotropies
authors: Arjun R, Pratyush Prakash Patra, And A. V. Anil Kumar
abstract:
Author(s): Arjun R, Pratyush Prakash Patra, and A. V. Anil Kumar

We investigate the interplay between nonreciprocal interactions and chemical-potential imbalance in a two-species nonreciprocal Blume-Capel model. Combining a systematic mean-field bifurcation analysis with large-scale Monte Carlo simulations in two and three dimensions, we map the model's dynamical…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064140] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a nonreciprocal Blume-Capel model with antisymmetric single-ion anisotropies using mean-field theory and Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: To understand the interplay between nonreciprocal interactions and chemical-potential imbalance in a two-species magnetic model.
method: Combines systematic mean-field bifurcation analysis with large-scale Monte Carlo simulations in two and three dimensions.
result: Maps the dynamical phase diagram and identifies novel phases driven by nonreciprocity.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal interactions lead to rich nonequilibrium behavior in the Blume-Capel model.

title: One-particle Density Matrix Framework For Mode-shell Correspondence: Characterizing Topology In Amorphous Higher-order Topological Insulators
authors: Miguel F. Martínez, Lucien Jezequel, Jens H. Bardarson, Thomas Klein Kvorning, And Julia D. Hannukainen
abstract:
Author(s): Miguel F. Martínez, Lucien Jezequel, Jens H. Bardarson, Thomas Klein Kvorning, and Julia D. Hannukainen

We present a framework for characterizing higher-order topological phases directly from the one-particle density matrix, without any reference to an underlying Hamiltonian. Our approach extends the mode-shell correspondence, originally formulated for single-particle Hamiltonians, to Gaussian states …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023320] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: A framework for characterizing higher-order topological phases in amorphous systems using the one-particle density matrix.
motivation: To extend topological characterization to amorphous materials where traditional band-structure methods fail.
method: Extends the mode-shell correspondence to Gaussian states via the one-particle density matrix, without reference to a Hamiltonian.
result: Demonstrates that higher-order topological invariants can be computed from the density matrix, applicable to amorphous higher-order topological insulators.
conclusion: Provides a practical tool for identifying topological phases in disordered systems, relevant for condensed matter physics.

title: Simulating Dynamics Of The Two-dimensional Transverse-field Ising Model: A Comparative Study Of Large-scale Classical Numerics
authors: Joseph Vovrosh, Sergi Julià-Farré, Wladislaw Krinitsin, Michael Kaicher, Fergus Hayes, Emmanuel Gottlob, Augustine Kshetrimayum, Kemal Bidzhiev, Simon B. Jäger, Markus Schmitt, Joseph Tindall, Constantin Dalyac, Tiago Mendes-Santos, And Alexandre Dauphin
abstract:

The quantum dynamics of many-qubit systems is an outstanding problem that has recently driven significant advances in both numerical methods and programmable quantum processing units (QPUs). In this work, we employ a comprehensive toolbox of state-of-the-art numerical approaches to classically simul…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023311] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: A comparative study of classical numerical methods for simulating the dynamics of the 2D transverse-field Ising model.
motivation: Quantum dynamics of many-qubit systems is computationally hard; this work benchmarks various classical numerical techniques to assess their accuracy and scalability.
method: The authors apply a suite of state-of-the-art numerical approaches (e.g., tensor networks, neural quantum states, exact diagonalization) to simulate the 2D transverse-field Ising model and compare their performance.
result: The study provides a detailed comparison of the methods' accuracy, computational cost, and scalability for different parameter regimes.
conclusion: No single method is universally optimal; the choice depends on the specific problem parameters and desired accuracy.

title: Disorder-induced Topological Phases In A Two-dimensional Chern Insulator With Strong Magnetic Disorder
authors: Devesh Vaish And Michael Potthoff
abstract:
Author(s): Devesh Vaish and Michael Potthoff

Strong directional disorder in local magnetic moments coupled to a Chern insulator gives rise to topological phases that cannot be realized in any clean system and are therefore genuinely disorder driven. We demonstrate this in a spinful Qi-Wu-Zhang model of a two-dimensional Chern insulator coupled…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023312] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies disorder-induced topological phases in a Chern insulator with strong magnetic disorder, which is a condensed matter physics topic without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To explore whether strong directional disorder in local magnetic moments can give rise to topological phases that are absent in clean systems.
method: The authors consider a spinful Qi-Wu-Zhang model of a two-dimensional Chern insulator coupled to disordered local magnetic moments and analyze the resulting topological phases.
result: They demonstrate that strong directional disorder can induce topological phases that are genuinely disorder-driven and cannot be realized in clean systems.
conclusion: Disorder can be a resource for engineering new topological phases in Chern insulators.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, and Michał Oszmaniec

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes complexity-theoretic foundations for BosonSampling in the saturated regime with a linear number of modes, proving hardness and anti-concentration results.
motivation: Previous BosonSampling complexity proofs assumed a dilute regime where the number of photons is much smaller than the number of modes, but experimental demonstrations operate in a saturated regime where the number of photons scales linearly with modes. The gap needed to be bridged to justify quantum advantage claims.
method: The authors develop new techniques to analyze the permanent of matrices with repeated rows/columns and prove that approximate BosonSampling remains hard in the saturated regime under standard complexity assumptions, using worst-case to average-case reductions and anti-concentration arguments.
result: They show that BosonSampling with a linear number of modes is classically hard to simulate approximately, and that the output distribution is anti-concentrated, enabling experimental verification.
conclusion: The results provide rigorous complexity-theoretic support for current photonic quantum advantage experiments operating in the saturated regime.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, and Jian-Wei Pan
