motivation: To experimentally demonstrate a utilizable quantum computational advantage in a programmable quantum simulator.
method: Uses an ultracold-atom processor to simulate the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system and benchmarks against classical simulations.
result: Achieves a quantum computational advantage by performing a task that is intractable for classical computers.
conclusion: The ultracold-atom processor can serve as a platform for demonstrating practical quantum advantage in simulating many-body physics.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, and Akira Furusawa

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021034] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: Introduces control parameters for scalable generation of non-Gaussian quantum states in optical systems.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum information processing but their generation is inefficient; the paper aims to improve success rates.
method: The authors propose new non-Gaussian control parameters and a systematic optimization framework for quantum light sources.
result: The approach increases the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.
conclusion: The work provides a practical method to scale up non-Gaussian state generation, advancing optical quantum computing.

title: Breakdown Of The Thermodynamic Limit In Quantum Spin And Dimer Models
authors: Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, And Victor Galitski
abstract:
Author(s): Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, and Victor Galitski

Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models demonstrates that domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states, challenging traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021020] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models challenges the thermodynamic limit.
motivation: To understand how domain shape can alter macroscopic ground states in quantum spin and dimer models.
method: Analytical and numerical study of quantum dimer models with geometry-induced phase separation.
result: Domain shape fundamentally changes the ground state, breaking the thermodynamic limit assumption.
conclusion: Traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit may fail in certain quantum spin systems.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; space-time duality offers a unified framework.
method: The review explains how discretizing time evolution on a lattice and treating space and time symmetrically leads to solvable models, particularly brickwork quantum circuits.
result: The paper provides a pedagogical overview of exactly solvable dynamics via space-time duality, linking to quantum computation.
conclusion: Space-time duality is a powerful tool for understanding and solving quantum many-body dynamics, with deep connections to quantum circuits.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on material candidates and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a type of quantum spin liquid with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in candidate materials, discussing their magnetic and topological properties.
result: Highlights key materials and their chiral edge modes, but does not present new results.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids remain an active area of research with many open questions, and the review serves as a guide for future work.

title: Trion Formation And Ordering In The Attractive Su(3) Fermi-Hubbard Model
authors: Jonathan Stepp, Eduardo Ibarra-García-Padilla, Richard T. Scalettar, And Kaden R. A. Hazzard
abstract:

Recent advances in microwave shielding have increased the stability and control of large numbers of polar molecules, allowing for the first realization of a molecular Bose-Einstein condensate. Remarkably, it was also recently realized that shielded polar molecules exhibit an [MATH] symmetr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250402] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies trion formation and ordering in the attractive SU(3) Fermi-Hubbard model, a strongly correlated fermionic system.
motivation: Understanding emergent phases in multi-component Fermi gases with attractive interactions, motivated by recent experiments with ultracold polar molecules.
method: The authors use determinant quantum Monte Carlo (DQMC) simulations to compute the phase diagram and correlation functions of the SU(3) Hubbard model with attractive interactions.
result: They find a trion phase (three-body bound states) and evidence of trion ordering at low temperatures, with a crossover to a trion superfluid phase.
conclusion: The SU(3) attractive Hubbard model supports trion formation and ordering, providing a platform for studying novel quantum phases in ultracold matter.

title: Nonperturbative $S$-Matrix Renormalization
authors: Laurent Freidel, José Padua-Argüelles, Susanne Schander, And Marc Schiffer
abstract:
Author(s): Laurent Freidel, José Padua-Argüelles, Susanne Schander, and Marc Schiffer

We propose a renormalization group flow equation for a functional that generates [MATH]-matrix elements and which captures similarities to the well-known Wetterich and Polchinski equations. While the latter ones, respectively, involve the effective action and Schwinger functional, which are genuine off…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251602] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a nonperturbative renormalization group flow equation for generating S-matrix elements, drawing analogies to Wetterich and Polchinski equations.
motivation: To develop a renormalization group approach directly for on-shell S-matrix elements, avoiding off-shell quantities like effective actions.
method: The authors derive a functional flow equation for an S-matrix generating functional, using techniques similar to functional renormalization group methods.
result: They obtain a nonperturbative equation that governs the flow of S-matrix elements under changes of the cutoff scale.
conclusion: This approach provides a new tool for studying nonperturbative aspects of quantum field theories directly from on-shell data.

title: Fluid Flow And Spatiotemporal Chaos In Chemically Active Emulsions
authors: Charu Datt, Jonathan Bauermann, Nazmi Burak Budanur, And Frank Jülicher

We study phase-separating fluid mixtures as they demix in the presence of chemical reactions that maintain them away from thermodynamic equilibrium. tldr: This paper studies spatiotemporal chaos in chemically active emulsions, focusing on non-equilibrium fluid dynamics and phase separation.
motivation: To understand how chemical reactions and phase separation interact with hydrodynamics to produce complex self-organization in active emulsions.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and numerical simulations of phase-separating fluid mixtures with chemical reactions.
result: They demonstrate that the interplay of reactions, phase separation, and hydrodynamics leads to spatiotemporal chaos and complex flow patterns.
conclusion: Chemically active emulsions exhibit rich non-equilibrium dynamics that could inform the design of active materials.

title: Geometric Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory

A geometric reformulation of time-dependent density-functional theory better describes nonequilibrium systems.

motivation: To improve the description of nonequilibrium systems within time-dependent density functional theory.
method: The authors propose a geometric reformulation of the theory.
result: The reformulation provides a better description of nonequilibrium systems.

While experimental evidence for spacetime supersymmetry (SUSY) in particle physics remains elusive, condensed matter systems offer a promising arena for its emergence at quantum critical points (QCPs). result: They show that spacetime supersymmetry can emerge at a fractionalized quantum critical point, providing a concrete condensed matter realization.
conclusion: This work offers a new platform for studying supersymmetry in condensed matter, but it is not aligned with the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Dynamics Of Superconducting Pairs In The Two-Dimensional Hubbard Model
authors: G. Sordi, E. M. O’callaghan, C. Walsh, M. Charlebois, P. Sémon, And A.-M. S. Tremblay

The frequency structure of the superconducting correlations in cuprates gives insights on the pairing mechanism. Here we present an exhaustive study of this problem in the two-dimensional Hubbard model with cellular dynamical mean-field theory. To this end, we systematically quantify the dependence …

tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of superconducting pairs in the two-dimensional Hubbard model using cellular dynamical mean-field theory.
motivation: Understanding the frequency structure of superconducting correlations in cuprates provides insights into the pairing mechanism.

title: Edge Reconstruction In A Quantum Spin Hall Insulator
authors: Rahul Soni, Matthias Thamm, Gonzalo Alvarez, Bernd Rosenow, And Adrian Del Maestro
abstract:

We study interaction-driven edge reconstruction in a quantum spin Hall insulator described by the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang model with Kanamori-Hubbard interactions using the real-space density matrix renormalization group method in both the grand-canonical and canonical ensembles. result: They find that isotope substitution induces collective phonon mixing and eigenvector transport, altering vibrational properties beyond simple frequency shifts.
conclusion: Isotopic substitution in solids with dense phonon manifolds leads to nontrivial modifications of phonon dynamics, which must be accounted for in interpreting experimental data.

result: Identifies general conditions for stacking-induced ferromagnetism, antiferromagnetism, and more exotic magnetic states.

conclusion: The framework enables more accurate first-principles calculations of electronic structure with electron-phonon coupling, relevant for condensed matter physics.

authors: João P. Mendonça, S. Biswas, M. Dziurawiec, U. Bhattacharya, K. Jachymski, M. Aidelsburger, M. Lewenstein, M. M. Maśka, And T. Grass

result: They find that diagonal hopping and loop exchange independently suppress metallic behavior but stabilize completely different spatial patterns of electron pairing.

method: The authors perform a systematic exploration of the phase diagram as a function of twist angle, filling, and interlayer tunneling strength using a microscopic model.

method: Using first-principles calculations, the authors design materials by stacking and intercalating van der Waals layers to achieve the desired band structure.
result: They identify specific material candidates that exhibit ideal type-II nodal line semimetal behavior with strongly tilted Dirac cones.
conclusion: The proposed strategy provides a rational route to engineer type-II nodal line semimetals in two-dimensional materials.

title: Steady-state Equilibrium And Nonequilibrium Noisy Network Dynamics
authors: Pik-Yin Lai
abstract:
Author(s): Pik-Yin Lai (黎璧賢)

The fluctuating dynamics of a network about its stable, noise-free steady state are theoretically investigated. Various causes of nonequilibrium dynamics are identified in terms of the properties and symmetry of the network connections and the noise covariance matrices. Several equivalent conditions…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064148] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies steady-state fluctuations in noisy networks, focusing on equilibrium and nonequilibrium dynamics from a classical stochastic perspective.
motivation: To understand how network connectivity and noise properties drive nonequilibrium dynamics in complex systems.
method: Theoretical analysis using Langevin equations and covariance matrices to characterize fluctuations around stable steady states.
result: Identifies conditions for equilibrium and nonequilibrium dynamics based on network symmetry and noise correlations.
conclusion: The framework provides a general classification of network dynamics but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Collective Decision Making With Higher-order Interactions On $d$-uniform Hypergraphs
authors: Thierry Njougouo, Timoteo Carletti, And Elio Tuci
abstract:
Author(s): Thierry Njougouo, Timoteo Carletti, and Elio Tuci

Understanding how group interactions influence opinion dynamics is fundamental to the study of collective behavior. In this work, we propose and study a model of opinion dynamics on [MATH]-uniform hypergraphs, where individuals interact through group-based (higher-order) structures rather than simple p…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064311] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies opinion dynamics on d-uniform hypergraphs, focusing on collective decision making with higher-order interactions.
motivation: Understanding how group interactions influence opinion dynamics is fundamental to collective behavior.
method: The authors propose and analyze a model of opinion dynamics on d-uniform hypergraphs, where interactions occur through group-based structures.
result: The model reveals how higher-order interactions affect consensus and polarization.
conclusion: Higher-order interactions significantly shape collective decision-making processes.

title: Hydrodynamic Theory Of Wetting By Active Particles
authors: Noah Grodzinski, Michael E. Cates, And Robert L. Jack
abstract:
Author(s): Noah Grodzinski, Michael E. Cates, and Robert L. Jack

The accumulation of self-propelled particles on repulsive barriers is a widely observed feature in active matter. Despite being implicated in a broad range of biological processes, from biofilm formation to cytoskeletal movement, wetting of surfaces by active particles remains poorly understood. In …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065423] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a hydrodynamic theory for the wetting of repulsive barriers by active particles, focusing on the accumulation and collective behavior of self-propelled particles.
motivation: Active particle wetting is observed in biological processes like biofilm formation and cytoskeletal movement, but a theoretical understanding is lacking.
method: The authors derive a hydrodynamic model based on continuum equations for density and polarization, incorporating activity and steric interactions.
result: The theory predicts wetting transitions and contact angles that depend on activity, and shows that active particles can wet surfaces even when passive particles cannot.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for understanding active wetting, with implications for biological and soft matter systems.

title: Collective Coordinate Descriptions Of A Kink In A Driven-damped ${ϕ}^{4}$ Model
authors: Jacek Gatlik, Tomasz Dobrowolski, Jean-Guy Caputo, And Panayotis G. Kevrekidis
abstract:
Author(s): Jacek Gatlik, Tomasz Dobrowolski, Jean-Guy Caputo, and Panayotis G. Kevrekidis

Extending a recent effective theory formulation for the dynamics of kinks in the sine-Gordon model [T. Dobrowolski et al.,
tldr: This paper develops effective collective coordinate models for kink dynamics in a driven-damped φ^4 model, extending a previous sine-Gordon approach.
motivation: To provide a reduced description of kink motion in the φ^4 model under driving and damping, which is important for understanding nonlinear wave propagation in classical field theories.
method: The authors propose three reduced models based on collective coordinates (position, width, internal mode) and compare their predictions with full partial differential equation simulations.
result: The reduced models capture key features of kink dynamics, including resonance phenomena and energy transfer, with varying accuracy depending on the driving and damping parameters.
conclusion: Collective coordinate descriptions offer a computationally efficient way to model kink dynamics, but their validity is limited to specific parameter regimes.

title: Relationship Between Heider Links And Ising Spins
authors: Zdzislaw Burda, Maciej Wołoszyn, Krzysztof Malarz, And Krzysztof Kułakowski
abstract:
Author(s): Zdzislaw Burda, Maciej Wołoszyn, Krzysztof Malarz, and Krzysztof Kułakowski

We show that the Heider model with an external field is equivalent, in the limit of structural balance, to the Ising model with nearest-neighbor interactions without an external field. More precisely, we claim that the signs of the Heider relations that maintain structural equilibrium in the system …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062104] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes an equivalence between the Heider model of social balance and the Ising model in the limit of structural balance.
motivation: To connect sociological balance theory with statistical physics models, potentially enabling new insights into social dynamics.
method: The authors show analytically that the Heider model with an external field reduces to the Ising model without an external field under the condition of structural balance.
result: The signs of Heider relations maintaining structural equilibrium correspond to Ising spin configurations with nearest-neighbor interactions.
conclusion: The equivalence provides a bridge between social network theory and condensed matter physics, but the paper is primarily a theoretical mapping without direct relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Discontinuous Wealth-gradient Transition Driving Cooperation
authors: Hyun Gyu Lee, Hyeong-Chai Jeong, And Deok-Sun Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Hyun Gyu Lee, Hyeong-Chai Jeong, and Deok-Sun Lee

The universal prevalence of cooperation is puzzling, as defection typically yields higher payoffs than cooperation, motivating searches for hidden pathways to cooperation. Here we study a game-theoretic model on a lattice structured population in which interaction payoffs are scaled by the minimum o…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064306] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies cooperation in a game-theoretic model on a lattice, focusing on wealth gradients and phase transitions.
motivation: Understanding the emergence of cooperation despite the payoff advantage of defection is a classic puzzle in evolutionary game theory.
method: The authors analyze a spatial game where interaction payoffs are scaled by the minimum of players' wealth, leading to a wealth-gradient driven transition.
result: They find a discontinuous transition in cooperation levels as a function of the wealth gradient parameter.
conclusion: Wealth inequality can promote cooperation through a gradient-induced phase transition, offering a new mechanism for cooperation.

title: Universality And Ambiguity In Extremes Of Anomalous Diffusion
authors: Sean D. Lawley
abstract:
Author(s): Sean D. Lawley

Many biophysical processes begin when the fastest searcher finds a target out of many random searchers, which is called an extreme or fastest first passage time (fFPT). In some models (i) the fFPT vanishes logarithmically as the number of searchers grows and (ii) the fFPT can be faster for subdiffus…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064135] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the scaling of fastest first-passage times in anomalous diffusion processes, focusing on universality and ambiguity in extreme statistics.
motivation: Many biophysical processes depend on the fastest searcher among many; understanding how extreme first-passage times scale with the number of searchers is important for modeling such processes.
method: The author analyzes mathematical models of subdiffusion and superdiffusion, deriving asymptotic expressions for the fastest first-passage time as the number of searchers grows.
result: The fastest first-passage time vanishes logarithmically for some models but can be faster for subdiffusion, and the scaling exhibits ambiguity depending on the model details.
conclusion: Extreme statistics of anomalous diffusion show universal logarithmic scaling in some cases but also model-dependent ambiguities, highlighting the need for careful modeling in biophysical applications.

title: Tiling By Near Coincidence
authors: Meshy Ochana And Ron Lifshitz
abstract:
Author(s): Meshy Ochana and Ron Lifshitz

Moiré patterns of twisted and scaled bilayers have recently emerged as a fertile source of quasiperiodic order in two-dimensional materials. Inspired by these systems, we introduce the near-coincidence method for generating quasiperiodic tilings of the plane. The method is intuitive—admitting pairs …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023330] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a near-coincidence method for generating quasiperiodic tilings inspired by moiré patterns in twisted bilayers.
motivation: To provide an intuitive method for generating quasiperiodic tilings that mimics the formation of moiré patterns in twisted and scaled bilayers.
method: The near-coincidence method generates tilings by overlaying two periodic lattices with a slight mismatch in scale or rotation, producing quasiperiodic patterns.
result: The method yields a variety of quasiperiodic tilings, including those with 12-fold symmetry, and can be extended to other symmetries.
conclusion: The near-coincidence method offers a simple and intuitive way to generate quasiperiodic tilings, with potential applications in modeling moiré materials.

title: Phase-space Topology And Spectral Flow In Screened Magnetized Plasmas
authors: Xianhao Rao, Adil Yolbarsop, Hong Li, And Wandong Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Xianhao Rao, Adil Yolbarsop, Hong Li, and Wandong Liu

Topological wave phenomena in continuous media are fundamentally challenged by unbounded spectra and the absence of a compact Brillouin zone, which obstruct conventional bulk-interface formulations. We develop a unified phase-space framework for screened magnetized plasma based on a pseudo-Hermitian…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023334] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a phase-space framework for topological wave phenomena in screened magnetized plasmas, focusing on spectral flow and bulk-interface correspondence in continuous media.
motivation: Topological wave phenomena in continuous media are challenged by unbounded spectra and lack of a compact Brillouin zone, which obstruct conventional bulk-interface formulations.
method: The authors develop a unified phase-space framework based on pseudo-Hermitian operators to analyze topological properties of screened magnetized plasmas.
result: They demonstrate spectral flow and establish a bulk-interface correspondence within this framework.
conclusion: The phase-space approach provides a way to study topological phenomena in continuous media with unbounded spectra.

title: Excited Eigenstates From A Two-species Random Walk
authors: Paul-Henry Glinel, Normand Beaudoin, And Alexandre Melanson
abstract:
Author(s): Paul-Henry Glinel, Normand Beaudoin, and Alexandre Melanson

Macroscopically, the population density function of random walk models can satisfy self-contained dynamics and exhibit unexpected order. Here, we show how a two-species random walk model that includes diffusion, probabilistic absorption of walkers mediated by a potential function, cross-species anni…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023324] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: A two-species random walk model with diffusion, absorption, and cross-species annihilation is studied, showing emergent order in population density.
motivation: To understand how macroscopic order can arise from simple stochastic microscopic rules in a two-species system.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of a random walk model with diffusion, potential-mediated absorption, and cross-species annihilation.
result: The population density function satisfies self-contained dynamics and exhibits unexpected order.
conclusion: The model demonstrates that complex emergent behavior can occur in simple random walk systems.

title: Theory Of High-harmonic Generation With Quantum Light
authors: Haoyu Liu, Hanxu Zhang, Xu Wang, And Jianmin Yuan
abstract:
Author(s): Haoyu Liu, Hanxu Zhang, Xu Wang, and Jianmin Yuan

High-harmonic generation (HHG) driven by intense quantum light has recently emerged as a new frontier in strong-field physics. Yet, the mechanism underlying HHG with nonclassical fields such as bright squeezed vacuum (BSV) light—characterized by a vanishing mean electric field—remains elusive. In th…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023326] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theory of high-harmonic generation driven by bright squeezed vacuum light, focusing on the quantum optical properties of the driving field.
motivation: High-harmonic generation (HHG) with nonclassical light, such as bright squeezed vacuum, is a new frontier in strong-field physics, but the underlying mechanism remains unclear.
method: The authors extend the standard three-step model of HHG to incorporate quantum light, using a fully quantum treatment of the driving field and the electron dynamics.
result: They show that HHG with bright squeezed vacuum exhibits unique features, such as photon-number correlations and nonclassical statistics in the harmonic emission.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for HHG with quantum light, opening up possibilities for generating nonclassical states of light at high frequencies.

title: Formation Of Bosonic $^{23}\mathrm{Na}^{41}\mathrm{K}$ Feshbach Molecules
authors: Sungjun Lee, Younghoon Lim, Jongyeol Kim, Jaeryeong Chang, And Jee Woo Park
abstract:
Author(s): Sungjun Lee, Younghoon Lim, Jongyeol Kim, Jaeryeong Chang, and Jee Woo Park

Ultracold Feshbach molecules are a crucial intermediate step for the creation of quantum degenerate gases of strongly dipolar molecules. After coherent transfer to the rovibrational ground state, these dimers can realize stable dipolar gases with strong, tunable long-range interactions. Here, we rep…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023307] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the formation of ultracold 23Na41K Feshbach molecules, a step toward creating dipolar quantum gases.
motivation: Ultracold Feshbach molecules are precursors to strongly dipolar gases with tunable long-range interactions, enabling studies of quantum many-body physics.
method: The authors use magnetoassociation across a Feshbach resonance in a mixture of 23Na and 41K atoms, followed by characterization of the molecules via radio-frequency spectroscopy.
result: They successfully create Feshbach molecules and measure their binding energies and lifetimes, demonstrating efficient conversion.
conclusion: This work provides a pathway to produce ground-state dipolar molecules for exploring quantum phases and quantum simulation.

title: Observation Of Surface Ferromagnons In The Axion-insulating Phase Of The Antiferromagnetic Topological Insulator ${\mathrm{EuSn}}_{2}{\mathrm{As}}_{2}$
authors: Mamoun Hemmida, Santanu Pakhira, David C. Johnston, And Hans-Albrecht Krug von Nidda
abstract:
Author(s): Mamoun Hemmida, Santanu Pakhira, David C. Johnston, and Hans-Albrecht Krug von Nidda

We report the study of spin dynamics of [MATH] in the antiferromagnetic axion topological insulator [MATH] by means of antiferromagnetic resonance at 9.34 GHz. Below the Néel temperature ([MATH]), two types of resonance modes, the conventiona…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023309] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports antiferromagnetic resonance measurements in the topological insulator EuSn2As2, observing surface ferromagnons in the axion-insulating phase.
motivation: To study spin dynamics and surface magnetic excitations in a topological insulator with antiferromagnetic order, which is relevant to axion electrodynamics.
method: Electron spin resonance (ESR) at 9.34 GHz was used to measure antiferromagnetic resonance modes below the Néel temperature.
result: Two resonance modes were observed: conventional antiferromagnetic resonance and a surface ferromagnon mode, indicating surface magnetic order.
conclusion: The surface ferromagnon mode is a signature of the axion-insulating phase, providing insight into the interplay between magnetism and topology.

title: Most Probable Path And Invariant Sets In Noise-induced Transition To Turbulence
authors: Yoshiki Hiruta, Kento Yasuda, And Kenta Ishimoto
abstract:
Author(s): Yoshiki Hiruta, Kento Yasuda, and Kenta Ishimoto

Turbulence transition often arises from a subcritical transition between bistable states characterized by invariant sets of deterministic dynamical systems, and such transitions can be triggered by system noise as rare events. In this study, we employ the Onsager-Machlup (OM) formulation of stochast…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023303] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies noise-induced transitions to turbulence using the Onsager-Machlup formulation to find most probable paths and invariant sets.
motivation: Understanding turbulence transition from bistable states triggered by noise is important for predicting and controlling turbulent flows.
method: The authors apply the Onsager-Machlup functional to a stochastic dynamical system to compute most probable transition paths and identify invariant sets.
result: They characterize the most probable paths and invariant sets governing the noise-induced transition to turbulence.
conclusion: The work provides insight into the role of noise in triggering turbulence, but is focused on classical fluid dynamics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Macroscopic Localization And Collective Memory In Poisson Renewal Resetting
authors: Ohad Vilk
abstract:
Author(s): Ohad Vilk

Stochastic renewal processes are ubiquitous across physics, biology, and the social sciences. Here, we show that continuous-time renewal dynamics can naturally produce a mixed discrete-continuous structure, with a macroscopic fraction of particles occupying a discrete state. For ensembles of continu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023305] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies macroscopic localization and collective memory in Poisson renewal resetting processes.
motivation: Stochastic renewal processes are common in many fields, and understanding their emergent structure is important.
method: The authors analyze continuous-time renewal dynamics and show that they can produce a mixed discrete-continuous structure with a macroscopic fraction of particles in a discrete state.
result: They demonstrate that such dynamics exhibit macroscopic localization and collective memory effects.
conclusion: The findings reveal new features of renewal processes that may have implications for various complex systems.

title: Manifold-based Transformation Of Probability Distributions: Application To The Inverse Problem Of Reconstructing Distributions From Experimental Data
authors: Tomotaka Oroguchi, Rintaro Inoue, And Masaaki Sugiyama
abstract:
Author(s): Tomotaka Oroguchi, Rintaro Inoue, and Masaaki Sugiyama

Information geometry is a mathematical framework that elucidates the manifold structure of the probability distribution space (p space), providing a systematic approach to transforming probability distributions (PDs). In this study, we utilized information geometry to address the inverse problems as…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023291] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses information geometry to transform probability distributions for solving inverse problems in experimental data reconstruction.
motivation: The authors aim to address the inverse problem of reconstructing probability distributions from experimental data, which is common in fields like structural biology.
method: They apply information geometry, specifically the manifold structure of probability distribution spaces, to systematically transform distributions and solve the inverse problem.
result: The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of the manifold-based transformation approach for reconstructing distributions from limited or noisy experimental data.
conclusion: Information geometry provides a powerful framework for inverse problems involving probability distributions, with potential applications in various experimental sciences.

title: Dynamical Phase Transitions Across Slow And Fast Regimes In A Two-tone Driven Duffing Resonator
authors: Soumya S. Kumar, Javier Del Pino, Letizia Catalini, Alexander Eichler, And Oded Zilberberg
abstract:
Author(s): Soumya S. Kumar, Javier del Pino, Letizia Catalini, Alexander Eichler, and Oded Zilberberg

The dynamical phase transitions of a Duffing resonator subjected to a bichromatic drive across the slow- and fast-beating regimes are mapped. An analytical threshold to observe these transitions based on an effective nonlinear response theory is provided, explaining the mechanism behind these processes. Complementary analytical treatments for the slow and fast regimes are supplied.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023298] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical phase transitions in a driven Duffing resonator, focusing on classical nonlinear dynamics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the transition between slow and fast beating regimes in a classical nonlinear resonator under bichromatic drive.
method: Analytical effective nonlinear response theory combined with complementary treatments for slow and fast regimes.
result: An analytical threshold for dynamical phase transitions is derived and mapped across the two regimes.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for predicting and explaining dynamical phase transitions in driven nonlinear resonators.

title: Complete Inelastic Transparency Of Time-modulated Resonant Photonic Circuits
authors: M. Sumetsky
abstract:
Author(s): M. Sumetsky

Photonic circuits modulated in time can convert the input light frequency [MATH], shifting it by multiples of the modulation frequency [MATH] and, in certain cases, amplify the total input light power. Of special interest are photonic circuits employing microwave capacitors, which instantaneou…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023299] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies time-modulated resonant photonic circuits that achieve complete inelastic transparency, converting input light frequency with potential amplification.
motivation: To understand and exploit frequency conversion and amplification in time-modulated photonic circuits, which could have applications in optical communication and signal processing.
method: Theoretical analysis of photonic circuits with time-dependent modulation, using coupled-mode theory and scattering matrix formalism to derive conditions for complete inelastic transparency.
result: Complete inelastic transparency is achieved when the modulation frequency matches the resonant frequency spacing, leading to perfect frequency conversion without reflection.
conclusion: Time-modulated resonant photonic circuits can act as efficient frequency converters and amplifiers, with potential for integrated photonic devices.

title: General Spin Models From Noncollinear Spin Density Functional Theory And Spin-cluster Expansion
authors: Tomonori Tanaka And Yoshihiro Gohda
abstract:
Author(s): Tomonori Tanaka and Yoshihiro Gohda

We present a data-efficient framework for constructing general classical spin Hamiltonians by combining the spin-cluster expansion (SCE) with fully self-consistent noncollinear spin density functional theory (DFT). The key idea is to fit the SCE model to magnetic torques rather than to total energie…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023300] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A data-efficient framework for constructing classical spin Hamiltonians from noncollinear spin DFT using spin-cluster expansion fitted to magnetic torques.
motivation: To enable accurate and efficient modeling of complex magnetic systems beyond simple Heisenberg models.
method: Combines noncollinear spin DFT with spin-cluster expansion, fitting the model to magnetic torques instead of total energies.
result: Demonstrates that the torque-based fitting yields accurate spin Hamiltonians with fewer DFT calculations.
conclusion: The proposed framework is a practical tool for studying magnetic materials with complex spin textures.

title: Dynamics Of Quantum Chiral Solitons
authors: Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, And Cristian D. Batista
abstract:
Author(s): Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, and Cristian D. Batista

A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains demonstrates that they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, appearing as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and becoming detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021056] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains, showing they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and are detectable via neutron scattering.
motivation: To understand the quantum dynamics of chiral solitons in spin chains, which are topological excitations with potential relevance to low-dimensional magnetism.
method: A nonperturbative quantization approach is applied to chiral solitons in a spin chain model, analyzing their condensation into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid.
result: Chiral solitons appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and their signature can be observed via inelastic neutron scattering.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for chiral soliton dynamics and suggests experimental detection is feasible.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, And Yin-Chen He
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, and Yin-Chen He

Researchers use noncommutative “fuzzy” spheres to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study free and interacting fermionic conformal field theories in three dimensions, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To develop a non-perturbative method for studying strongly coupled conformal field theories using the fuzzy sphere as a regularization scheme.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative geometry, to discretize the sphere and simulate fermionic CFTs, analyzing spectra and correlation functions.
result: They find evidence of emergent supersymmetry in the interacting theory and compute scaling dimensions of operators.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere provides a viable numerical approach to study fermionic CFTs, with potential applications to more complex theories.

title: General Approach To Solving Spin Moiré Superstructures
authors: Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. Debeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, And Joseph G. Checkelsky
abstract:
Author(s): Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. DeBeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, and Joseph G. Checkelsky

Mapping of spin textures in EuAg
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021054] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general approach to solving spin moiré superstructures in EuAg4Sb2, revealing three distinct magnetic phases and establishing a design framework for spin-based vortex lattices.
motivation: To understand and control complex spin textures in moiré superlattices, which are of interest for information manipulation via spin-based vortex lattices.
method: The authors combine neutron scattering, magnetization measurements, and theoretical modeling to map the magnetic phase diagram of EuAg4Sb2 under varying temperature and magnetic field.
result: Three distinct, tunable magnetic phases are identified, including a skyrmion lattice phase, and a general framework for designing spin moiré superstructures is proposed.
conclusion: The work provides a blueprint for engineering spin textures in moiré materials, potentially enabling new approaches to information storage and processing.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature
authors: Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, and Alexander Mook

Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures demonstrates that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point, providing a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021053] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: Theoretical study of topological magnon gaps in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature.
motivation: To understand the stability of topological magnon gaps near the Curie point for spintronic applications.
method: Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures.
result: Topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point.
conclusion: Provides a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.

title: Are Neural Networks Collision Resistant?
authors: Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, And Riccardo Zecchina
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, and Riccardo Zecchina

A study of the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network shows that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, a result of direct relevance for the definition of new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021051] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of finding collisions in a one-layer neural network, showing that efficient algorithms fail, which is relevant for cryptography based on machine learning.
motivation: To understand whether neural networks can serve as collision-resistant hash functions for cryptographic protocols.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network using theoretical and algorithmic approaches.
result: Efficient algorithms are shown to fail in finding collisions, suggesting that such neural networks may be collision resistant.
conclusion: The findings are relevant for designing new cryptographic protocols based on machine learning models.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks
authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Li, Wei Chen, and Jan Nagler

A physics-informed framework allows for inferring general causal links across a wide range of networked dynamics systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021048] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A physics-informed framework for inferring causal links in networked dynamical systems.
motivation: Understanding causal relationships in complex networks is crucial for predicting system behavior, but existing methods often lack a physical basis.
method: The authors develop a framework that incorporates physical principles to infer causal links from time-series data of network dynamics.
result: The framework accurately predicts physical links across various networked dynamical systems, outperforming standard causal inference methods.
conclusion: Physics-informed causal inference can significantly improve link prediction in networks, with potential applications in many fields.

title: Anyon Superfluidity Of Excitons In Quantum Hall Bilayers
authors: Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, And Ashvin Vishwanath
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, and Ashvin Vishwanath

Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers reveals that topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids, offering a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021044] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies anyon superfluidity of excitons in quantum Hall bilayers, focusing on topological criticality and exotic collective states.
motivation: To understand and engineer exotic quantum states in fractional quantum Hall systems, specifically anyonic exciton superfluids.
method: Theoretical analysis using topological field theory and mean-field approaches for quantum Hall bilayers.
result: Topological criticality enables the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids with robust properties.
conclusion: Quantum Hall bilayers provide a platform for realizing anyonic superfluidity, which may have implications for topological quantum matter.

title: Liquid-Gas Criticality Of Hyperuniform Fluids
authors: Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, And Qun-Li Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, and Qun-Li Lei

Where ordinary fluids show wild fluctuations and critical opalescence, hyperuniform fluids of spinning particles stay unusually calm yet highly susceptible at the liquid–vapor critical point.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021032] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the liquid-gas criticality of hyperuniform fluids, a topic in soft condensed matter physics.
motivation: To understand the unusual critical behavior of hyperuniform fluids, which exhibit suppressed density fluctuations yet high susceptibility at the critical point.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and possibly simulations to characterize the critical properties of hyperuniform fluids composed of spinning particles.
result: Hyperuniform fluids show suppressed fluctuations but enhanced susceptibility at the liquid-vapor critical point, contrasting with ordinary fluids.
conclusion: The work reveals a new class of critical behavior in hyperuniform fluids, relevant to soft matter and statistical physics.

title: Stealthy-Hyperuniform Wave Dynamics In Two-Dimensional Photonic Crystals
authors: Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, And Mikael C. Rechtsman
abstract:
Author(s): Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, and Mikael C. Rechtsman

While disordered stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be largely transparent within a particular range of wavelengths, new experiments on large-scale silicon photonic crystals reveal unexpected residual scattering driven by radiative loss.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021028] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wave dynamics in disordered stealthy hyperuniform photonic crystals, revealing unexpected residual scattering due to radiative loss.
motivation: Stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be transparent in certain wavelength ranges, but experiments show residual scattering that needs explanation.
method: Large-scale experiments on silicon photonic crystals combined with theoretical analysis of radiative loss mechanisms.
result: Unexpected residual scattering is driven by radiative loss, contradicting the expectation of near-perfect transparency.
conclusion: The findings highlight limitations of stealthy hyperuniformity for photonic applications and suggest design modifications.

title: Dipolar Nematic State In Relaxor Ferroelectrics
authors: Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, And Shi Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, and Shi Liu

A nematic ordering underpins the behavior of relaxor ferroelectrics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021022] Published Wed Apr 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a dipolar nematic state in relaxor ferroelectrics, focusing on condensed matter physics without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Relaxor ferroelectrics exhibit complex ordering; understanding the nematic state may clarify their behavior.
method: The authors likely use theoretical modeling or experimental characterization to identify the dipolar nematic phase.
result: A dipolar nematic state is identified as underpinning relaxor ferroelectric behavior.
conclusion: The nematic ordering is key to relaxor properties, but the work is purely in condensed matter physics.

title: Excitations Across The Equilibrium And Photoinduced “Hidden” States Of Magnetoresistive Manganites
authors: Shiyu Fan, Feng Jin, Taehun Kim, Umesh Kumar, Zixun Zhang, Vivek Bhartiya, Jiemin Li, Brandon Yalin, Yanhong Gu, Mingqiang Gu, Wen Hu, Claudio Mazzoli, G. Lawrence Carr, Osor S. Barišić, Andrey S. Mishchenko, Valentina Bisogni, Sobhit Singh, Wenbin Wu, And Jonathan Pelliciari
abstract:
Author(s): Shiyu Fan, Feng Jin, Taehun Kim, Umesh Kumar, Zixun Zhang, Vivek Bhartiya, Jiemin Li, Brandon Yalin, Yanhong Gu, Mingqiang Gu, Wen Hu, Claudio Mazzoli, G. Lawrence Carr, Osor S. Barišić, Andrey S. Mishchenko, Valentina Bisogni, Sobhit Singh, Wenbin Wu, and Jonathan Pelliciari

Ultrafast photoexcitation in /3Ca1/3MnO3 generates a long-lived hidden phase with unique polaronic and phononic excitations that do not exist under standard equilibrium conditions.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021018] Published Thu Apr 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies photoinduced hidden phases and excitations in magnetoresistive manganites using ultrafast spectroscopy.
motivation: To understand the nature of photoinduced hidden phases in strongly correlated electron systems, which may have implications for controlling material properties.
method: Combines resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) and time-resolved optical spectroscopy to probe excitations across equilibrium and hidden states.
result: Identifies unique polaronic and phononic excitations in the hidden phase that are absent in equilibrium.
conclusion: Photoexcitation can create long-lived metastable phases with distinct lattice and electronic excitations, offering a route to manipulate material functionality.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a quantum algorithm for computing persistence in topological data analysis, claiming exponential speedup.
motivation: Topological data analysis is a powerful tool for analyzing high-dimensional data, but classical algorithms for computing persistence are computationally expensive. Quantum computing may offer a speedup.
method: The authors design a quantum algorithm that leverages quantum linear algebra and sampling techniques to compute persistence diagrams more efficiently than classical methods.
result: They prove a provable exponential quantum speedup for certain instances of the persistence computation problem.
conclusion: The work suggests that quantum computers could significantly accelerate topological data analysis, potentially enabling new applications.

title: Grand Challenge Of Quantum Applications
authors: Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. Mcclean, Thomas O’brien, And Nicholas C. Rubin
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. McClean, Thomas O’Brien, and Nicholas C. Rubin

A proposed five-stage framework outlines the path to useful quantum computing, detailing the scientific milestones required to bridge the gap between theory and real-world utility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020101] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A high-level perspective piece proposing a five-stage framework for achieving useful quantum computing, focusing on scientific milestones rather than technical results.
motivation: To outline a roadmap for bridging the gap between theoretical quantum computing and practical applications.
method: Conceptual framework based on expert opinion and analysis of current quantum computing progress.
result: A five-stage framework detailing milestones for quantum utility.
conclusion: The framework provides a structured path for the quantum computing community to focus efforts on achieving real-world impact.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, serving as a benchmark for quantum computers.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a topological invariant that is hard to compute classically, making it a candidate for quantum advantage. The authors aim to provide an end-to-end implementation on current quantum hardware.
method: The authors design a complete quantum algorithm pipeline including state preparation, unitary evolution, and measurement, and implement it on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
result: They successfully compute the Jones polynomial for several knots and links, demonstrating the feasibility of the algorithm and observing signatures of quantum advantage.
conclusion: The work establishes a practical benchmark for quantum computers and suggests that topological invariants like the Jones polynomial are promising for demonstrating quantum advantage.

title: Photon Catalysis For General Multimode Multi-Photon Quantum State Preparation
authors: Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, And Massimo Frigerio
abstract:
Author(s): Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, and Massimo Frigerio

Using a procedure based on symmetric tensor decomposition, every photonic state can be prepared with realistic experimental tools and a predictable number of steps.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020323] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: A method for preparing arbitrary photonic states using symmetric tensor decomposition and photon catalysis.
motivation: Efficient preparation of complex photonic states is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are often limited to specific states or require many resources.
method: The authors propose a procedure based on symmetric tensor decomposition to decompose any photonic state into a sequence of elementary operations, including photon catalysis and linear optics.
result: They show that any multimode multi-photon state can be prepared with a predictable number of steps using realistic experimental tools.
conclusion: The work provides a general and resource-efficient framework for photonic state preparation, potentially advancing photonic quantum computing and quantum networks.

title: Quantum Linear System Solvers: A Survey Of Algorithms And Applications
authors: Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, And Dominic W. Berry
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, and Dominic W. Berry

Given vector b and matrix
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025005] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive survey of quantum algorithms for solving linear systems, focusing on HHL and post-HHL developments.
motivation: Linear system solving is central to many computational tasks, and quantum algorithms promise exponential speedups. This survey aims to organize the rapidly growing body of work on the quantum linear system problem.
method: The paper reviews algorithmic techniques including HHL, variable-time amplitude amplification, adiabatic approaches, and block-encoding methods, with a focus on query complexity and resource requirements.
result: It provides a taxonomy of algorithms, compares their complexities, and discusses applications in machine learning, differential equations, and data fitting.
conclusion: Quantum linear system solvers have matured significantly, but practical implementation remains challenging due to resource overheads; the survey highlights open problems and future directions.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge in 2D magnetism, which has revealed new phenomena and challenged established theories.
method: The paper is a review that surveys experimental and theoretical progress in 2D van der Waals magnetic materials.
result: The review covers ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, topology, quantum dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, spintronics, and magneto-optical phenomena.
conclusion: The field is rapidly evolving, with potential for new applications and deeper understanding of low-dimensional magnetism.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from geometric frustration and interference effects.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, synthesizing findings from condensed matter physics.
result: Kagome metals exhibit a wealth of exotic states including topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, unconventional superconductivity, and orbital antiferromagnetism.
conclusion: The kagome lattice provides a rich platform for exploring correlated electron physics and may lead to new quantum states.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes

Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation, with broad applications to physical systems.
motivation: Spin glasses are a classic model for disordered systems, and understanding their dynamics is relevant to many fields, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The review synthesizes experimental results, theoretical models, and large-scale simulations of spin-glass dynamics.
result: The paper tracks progress in the field and highlights the synergy between experiment, theory, and simulation.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain an active area with future research opportunities, but the paper is not aligned with the user's research interests.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to neural network data, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding coordinated activity in large neural networks is a central challenge in neuroscience.
method: The authors review recent progress in using maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques to analyze recordings from thousands of neurons.
result: These methods uncover reproducible collective behaviors in neural populations.
conclusion: Statistical physics provides a powerful framework for predicting neural activity, with predictive power comparable to other areas of physics.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on nonradiative transitions and their applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: To understand and model the photophysical process of internal conversion, which is important for applications like photonics and energy harvesting.
method: Review of theoretical models describing nonradiative decay mechanisms, including various quantum dynamical approaches.
result: Summarizes the current theoretical understanding of internal conversion and identifies areas for future research.
conclusion: Theoretical methods for internal conversion are advancing, but further development is needed for accurate predictions in complex systems.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review of quantum aspects of magnetic skyrmions, covering their formation and quantum features.
motivation: To survey quantum-mechanical properties of skyrmions, which are topological spin textures with potential applications in spintronics.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion quantum mechanics, including interactions and quantum features.
result: Summarizes current understanding of quantum effects in skyrmions, such as quantum tunneling and entanglement.
conclusion: Skyrmions exhibit rich quantum behavior that may enable future quantum technologies, but the field is still developing.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium reviewing synthetic quantum matter in fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions, focusing on simulation of topological and gravitational phenomena.
motivation: To explore quantum many-body physics in nonstandard geometries that enable simulation of exotic phenomena like topology and gravity.
method: Reviews experimental and theoretical implementations in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems for fractal, curved, and higher-dimensional geometries.
result: Summarizes progress in realizing synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries and their potential for simulating condensed matter and gravitational models.
conclusion: These synthetic systems offer new platforms for studying quantum many-body physics beyond conventional geometries, with implications for topology and quantum gravity.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of using massive quantum systems to probe gravity, including tests of quantum gravity effects and entanglement mediation.
motivation: To understand the interplay between quantum mechanics and gravity, which is poorly understood, by using massive quantum systems as probes.
method: Review of theoretical proposals and experimental efforts, including matter-wave interferometry and tests of gravity-induced entanglement.
result: Summarizes current theoretical models and experimental progress, highlighting that no definitive evidence of quantum gravity has been found yet.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems offer a promising avenue to test quantum gravity, but further theoretical and experimental work is needed.

One-dimensional (1D) structures provide a unique platform to study the correlated quantum interactions and phase transitions such as unconventional magnetism and superconducting states. Here, we report that iron chalcogenide [MATH] exhibits an unusual bl…

tldr: This paper reports an unusual block-type antiferromagnetic order in a quasi-one-dimensional iron chalcogenide, studied via neutron scattering and first-principles calculations.

result: Discovery of a block-type antiferromagnetic structure with alternating ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic couplings along the chain.

authors: Li Li, Ze Sun, And Fu-Guo Yang

We study the nonlinear interior dynamics of spontaneously scalarized black holes in Einstein-Maxwell-scalar theory with zero cosmological constant, revealing novel critical phenomena. title: Intrinsic Generation Of Angular Momenta And Entanglement In Fission

method: Time-dependent density functional theory with axial and nonaxial deformations is applied to simulate spontaneous fission of 252Cf.
result: The study reveals how constraints from axial symmetry affect spin and entanglement of fission fragments.
conclusion: The work provides insights into nuclear fission dynamics but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Topological Slot In Phononic Crystals
authors: Qing Wang, Yinfei Zhang, Gangqiao Shao, Han Liu, Weiyin Deng, Hailong He, Liping Ye, Jiuyang Lu, Manzhu Ke, And Zhengyou Liu

tldr: This paper proposes a method to pause or spatially confine chiral edge states in phononic Chern insulators by introducing a topological slot that breaks translational symmetry.

method: They design a phononic crystal with a topological slot—a defect that locally breaks the Chern topology—and use numerical simulations and experiments to demonstrate that edge states can be trapped or released by controlling the slot's properties.
result: The topological slot successfully pins the chiral edge state, allowing spatial confinement and controlled release, as verified by transmission measurements and field distributions.
conclusion: The work introduces a new mechanism for manipulating topological edge states, with potential applications in acoustic information processing and topological waveguides.

title: Direct Observation Of Sublattice-Dependent Magnetic Ordering And Strong Electron-Magnon Coupling In ${\mathrm{Fe}}_{5}{\mathrm{GeTe}}_{2}$
authors: R. Xu, X. H. Chen, X. L. Li, Y. Z. Wang, J. H. Yao, Z. S. Zhao, S. Liao, S. W. Su, P. Li, Z. T. Liu, D. W. Shen, F. M. Li, Y. L. Wang, D. L. Feng, And J. Jiang

result: Observed sublattice-dependent magnetic ordering and strong electron-magnon coupling.

tldr: This paper studies scattering symmetries in diffraction gratings and metagratings, focusing on electromagnetic wave control.
motivation: To understand and exploit symmetries in diffraction gratings for enhanced control of electromagnetic waves.
method: Theoretical analysis of scattering symmetries using group theory and electromagnetic theory.

Chromium thiophosphate ([MATH]) is a long-known material: A layered semiconducting antiferromagnet. Its recently discovered gate-tunable metamagnetic phase transitions, the remarkable positive and oscillating magnetoresistance as a tunnel barrier, and its Fano-resonance luminescence, …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023323] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ligand-mediated magnetic coupling and metamagnetic transitions in CrPS4, a layered antiferromagnetic semiconductor.
motivation: To understand the microscopic mechanism of metamagnetic transitions and magnetoresistance in CrPS4, which is of interest for spintronics.
method: X-ray absorption spectroscopy and X-ray magnetic circular dichroism at the Cr L2,3 and S K edges, combined with first-principles calculations.
result: Identified that magnetic coupling is mediated by sulfur ligands and changes across metamagnetic transitions, explaining the observed magnetoresistance.
conclusion: The study provides insight into the electronic and magnetic structure of CrPS4, relevant for its application in spintronic devices.

title: Before The Cycle Is Over: Subcycle Time Refraction At Optical Frequencies
authors: Ohad Segal, Noa Konforty, Oded Schiller, Maxwell J. Tolchin, Tony Yasniger, Soham Saha, Ryan W. Spangler, Jon-Paul Maria, Yonatan Plotnik, And Mordechai Segev
abstract:

This work demonstrates subcycle order-unity variations in the refractive index at optical frequencies and measures the time-refraction of a probe wave propagating in the modulated medium.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022054] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates subcycle order-unity refractive index variations at optical frequencies and measures time-refraction of a probe wave.
motivation: To achieve ultrafast modulation of refractive index at optical frequencies, enabling new regimes of light-matter interaction.
method: Experimental demonstration using a modulated medium to induce subcycle refractive index changes and probe wave time-refraction.
result: Order-unity refractive index variations on subcycle timescales were observed, with time-refraction of the probe wave.
conclusion: Subcycle time refraction is feasible at optical frequencies, opening possibilities for ultrafast optical control.
