Andrew MacFarlane, Robert F. Kiefl, Geetha Balakrishnan, Evgueni V. Chulkov, Stuart S. P. Parkin, and Zaher Salman

We investigate the behavior of interstitial [MATH] implanted near the surface of [MATH] using [MATH]-detected nuclear magnetic resonance. We find that, unlike the muon, [MATH] does not show any signature of induced magnetism. This result is consist…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023316] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies impurity-induced magnetism and dynamics in 2H-MoTe2 using β-NMR, finding no induced magnetism for Li8, contrasting with muon behavior.
motivation: To understand the magnetic properties of transition metal dichalcogenides and the role of interstitial impurities, which is relevant for spintronics and materials science.
method: β-detected nuclear magnetic resonance (β-NMR) is used to probe Li8 implanted near the surface of 2H-MoTe2, comparing with muon spin rotation results.
result: Li8 shows no signature of induced magnetism, unlike muons, indicating different interactions with the host material.
conclusion: The absence of induced magnetism for Li8 suggests that the magnetic response depends on the specific impurity, which has implications for understanding magnetism in TMDs.

title: Machine-learning-guided Discovery Of Kagome Superconductors ${\mathrm{YRu}}_{3}{\mathrm{B}}_{2}$ And ${\mathrm{LuRu}}_{3}{\mathrm{B}}_{2}$
authors: Rose Albu Mustaf, Sajilesh K. P., Sanu Mishra, Junze Deng, Yi Jiang, Kaja H. Hiorth, Eeli O. Lamponen, Martin Gutierrez-Amigo, Päivi Törmä, Miguel A. L. Marques, B. Andrei Bernevig, And Emilia Morosan

Author(s): Rose Albu Mustaf, Sajilesh K. P., Sanu Mishra, Junze Deng, Yi Jiang, Kaja H. Hiorth, Eeli O. Lamponen, Martin Gutierrez-Amigo, Päivi Törmä, Miguel A. L. Marques, B. Andrei Bernevig, and Emilia Morosan

We report the experimental discovery of bulk superconductivity in two kagome lattice compounds, [MATH] and [MATH], which were predicted through machine-learning-accelerated high-throughput screening combined with first-principles calculati…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023308] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Machine learning and first-principles calculations predict and experimentally discover two new kagome superconductors.
motivation: To discover new kagome superconductors using machine-learning-accelerated high-throughput screening.
method: Machine learning models combined with first-principles calculations to screen candidate materials, followed by experimental synthesis and characterization.
result: Discovery of bulk superconductivity in YRu3B2 and LuRu3B2 with kagome lattice structure.
conclusion: The approach successfully identifies new kagome superconductors, demonstrating the power of machine learning in materials discovery.

title: Confinement And Finite-range Effects In A Quasi-two-dimensional Gas Of Fermionic Dimers
authors: Giovanni Midei, Jordi Boronat, And Grigory E. Astrakharchik
abstract:
Author(s): Giovanni Midei, Jordi Boronat, and Grigory E. Astrakharchik

A study of a gas of fermionic dimers in a quasi-two-dimensional geometry induced by strong harmonic confinement in one direction is presented. Fixed-node diffusion Monte Carlo calculations are used to quantify the effects of confinement and finite interaction range on the equation of state and density profiles, with the results benchmarked against analytical theories.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022051] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: A Monte Carlo study of fermionic dimers in a quasi-2D geometry, focusing on confinement and finite-range effects on the equation of state.
motivation: To understand how strong confinement and finite interaction range affect the properties of a gas of fermionic dimers, relevant to ultracold atomic systems.
method: Fixed-node diffusion Monte Carlo simulations are used to compute the equation of state and density profiles, benchmarked against analytical theories.
result: Quantifies the effects of confinement and finite range, showing deviations from simple analytical models.
conclusion: The study provides benchmarks for quasi-2D fermionic dimer gases, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Revealing Charge Anisotropies In Metal Compounds Via High-purity X-ray Polarimetry
authors: Lena Scherthan, Juliusz A. Wolny, Isabelle Faus, Olaf Leupold, Kai S. Schulze, Sebastian Höfer, Robert Loetzsch, Berit Marx-Glowna, Christopher E. Anson, Annie K. Powell, Ingo Uschmann, Hans-Christian Wille, Gerhard G. Paulus, Volker Schünemann, And Ralf Röhlsberger

Linear polarization analysis of hard x-rays is employed to probe electronic anisotropies in metal-containing complexes with high selectivity. We use polarization-resolved nuclear forward scattering (PR-NFS) of synchrotron radiation at the 14.4 keV nuclear resonance of [MATH] to determine…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023297] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses high-purity X-ray polarimetry to probe charge anisotropies in metal compounds via nuclear forward scattering.
motivation: Understanding electronic anisotropies in metal complexes is important for materials science and chemistry, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors employ polarization-resolved nuclear forward scattering (PR-NFS) of synchrotron radiation at the 14.4 keV nuclear resonance of 57Fe to measure linear polarization of hard X-rays.
result: The technique reveals charge anisotropies with high selectivity in metal-containing complexes.
conclusion: High-purity X-ray polarimetry is a powerful tool for probing electronic structure, but the work is purely experimental and unrelated to the user's research directions.

title: Current-induced Successive Structural Phase Transitions Beyond Thermal Equilibrium In Single-crystal ${\mathrm{VO}}_{2}$
authors: Shunsuke Kitou, Akitoshi Nakano, Masato Imaizumi, Yuiga Nakamura, Yuto Nakamura, Hideo Kishida, Taka-Hisa Arima, And Ichiro Terasaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shunsuke Kitou, Akitoshi Nakano, Masato Imaizumi, Yuiga Nakamura, Yuto Nakamura, Hideo Kishida, Taka-hisa Arima, and Ichiro Terasaki

Using synchrotron x-ray diffraction, optical microscopy, and Raman spectroscopy, current-induced structural phase transitions in single-crystal vanadium dioxide are investigated. Successive transitions to two distinct metallic tetragonal phases are observed, including a nonequilibrium structure with isotropic lattice expansion inaccessible under thermal equilibrium.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022050] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports current-induced structural phase transitions in VO2 single crystals, revealing nonequilibrium metallic phases not accessible under thermal equilibrium.
motivation: To understand how electric current can drive structural phase transitions beyond thermal equilibrium, potentially enabling new pathways to control material properties.
method: Synchrotron x-ray diffraction, optical microscopy, and Raman spectroscopy were used to characterize structural changes in single-crystal VO2 under applied current.
result: Successive transitions to two distinct metallic tetragonal phases were observed, including a nonequilibrium structure with isotropic lattice expansion.
conclusion: Current can induce structural phase transitions that are inaccessible by heating alone, demonstrating a non-thermal control mechanism.

title: Ghost Mechanism: An Analytical Model Of Abrupt Learning In Recurrent Networks
authors: Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, And Hidenori Tanaka
abstract:
Author(s): Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, and Hidenori Tanaka

This study establishes the ghost mechanism as an underlying mechanism for abrupt learning, whereby the recurrent neural network develops ghost points—transient dynamical bottlenecks—and identifies ways to overcome the training instabilities.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021058] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a ghost mechanism to explain abrupt learning in recurrent neural networks, focusing on dynamical bottlenecks and training instabilities.
motivation: Understanding abrupt learning phenomena in neural networks is important for improving training stability and performance.
method: The authors develop an analytical model of ghost points—transient dynamical bottlenecks—in recurrent networks and analyze their role in abrupt learning.
result: The ghost mechanism is identified as a key underlying cause of abrupt learning, and methods to overcome training instabilities are proposed.
conclusion: The ghost mechanism provides a theoretical framework for abrupt learning, with implications for designing more stable recurrent networks.

title: General Framework Enabling Polarity-Tunable Time-Reversal Symmetric Superconducting Diode Effects In Gate-Defined Homojunctions
authors: Hongwei Zhang, Chunsheng Wang, Ran Wang, Senyang Pan, Hengning Wang, Jiaqiang Cai, Yonglai Liu, Zhe Qu, Xiangde Zhu, Wei Ning, Chuanying Xi, Jinglei Zhang, Ning Hao, Guolin Zheng, And Mingliang Tian

Local protonic gating in
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021046] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a time-reversal symmetric superconducting diode effect in gate-defined homojunctions using local protonic gating.
motivation: To achieve magnetic-field-free control of nonreciprocal critical currents in superconducting devices.
method: Local protonic gating is applied to homojunctions to induce a polarity-tunable superconducting diode effect.
result: A time-reversal symmetric superconducting diode effect is observed, enabling control of nonreciprocal critical currents without magnetic fields.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for polarity-tunable superconducting diodes, relevant for superconducting electronics.

title: Three-Dimensional Xy Universality And Nonlinear Magnetic Susceptibility In A Kagome Ice Compound
authors: Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, And Philipp Gegenwart

Author(s): Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, and Philipp Gegenwart

Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, reached via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021043] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in a kagome spin ice compound, revealing hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.
motivation: To investigate the nature of the ground state and phase transition in the kagome ice compound HoAgGe, which may host exotic magnetic order.
method: Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements were performed on single crystals of HoAgGe, combined with neutron scattering and other techniques to characterize the phase transition.
result: The measurements reveal a three-dimensional XY universality class transition and hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground state.
conclusion: The study provides evidence for a novel magnetic ground state in a kagome ice system, relevant to frustrated magnetism and topological phases.

title: Robust Orbital-Selective Flat Bands In Layered Transition-Metal Oxyhalides At Room Temperature
authors: Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Riccardo Comin
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, and Riccardo Comin

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of layered transition-metal oxyhalides reveals intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021041] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of robust orbital-selective flat bands in layered transition-metal oxyhalides at room temperature using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: Flat bands in strongly correlated materials can host exotic quantum phases, but many are only stable at low temperatures. The authors aim to find a room-temperature platform for studying such phenomena.
method: The authors synthesize layered transition-metal oxyhalides and characterize their electronic structure using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and density functional theory (DFT) calculations.
result: They observe intrinsic flat bands that are orbital-selective and remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for strongly correlated electron states.
conclusion: These materials offer a promising system for investigating flat-band physics and potentially correlated phases at accessible temperatures.

title: Probing Quantum Anomalous Hall States In Twisted Bilayer ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$ Via Attractive Polaron Spectroscopy
authors: Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, And Mohammad Hafezi
abstract:
Author(s): Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, and Mohammad Hafezi

Magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted WSe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021037] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses magneto-optical spectroscopy to probe quantum anomalous Hall states in twisted bilayer WSe2, demonstrating electric-field control of magnetic order.
motivation: Understanding and controlling topological phases in moiré materials is important for fundamental physics and potential applications.
method: The authors perform magneto-optical spectroscopy on twisted bilayer WSe2, measuring attractive polaron resonances to probe the electronic structure and magnetic ordering.
result: They observe a spontaneous quantum anomalous Hall phase and demonstrate electric-field-induced switching between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic orders.
conclusion: The work establishes attractive polaron spectroscopy as a powerful tool for studying quantum anomalous Hall states and highlights the tunability of magnetic order in moiré systems.

title: Intertwined Polar, Chiral, And Ferro-Rotational Orders In A Homo-Ferro-Rotational Insulator
authors: Weizhe Zhang, June Ho Yeo, Xiaoyu Guo, Tony Chiang, Nishkarsh Agarwal, John T. Heron, Kai Sun, Junjie Yang, Sang-Wook Cheong, Youngjun Ahn, And Liuyan Zhao
abstract:

Multimodal optical characterization of Ni
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021030] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of intertwined polar, chiral, and ferro-rotational orders in a homo-ferro-rotational insulator using multimodal optical characterization.
motivation: To understand the coupling between different ferroic orders and the formation of complex domain walls in materials with ferro-rotational order.
method: Multimodal optical characterization techniques including second harmonic generation and optical anisotropy measurements on Ni2Mo3O8.
result: Identified a uniform ferro-rotational state that couples polarity and chirality, leading to complex mixed-type domain walls.
conclusion: The findings reveal a new type of multiferroic order with intertwined polar, chiral, and ferro-rotational degrees of freedom.

title: Ballistic Spin Valve In Graphene Realized Via Electron Optics
authors: Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, And Ivan J. Vera-Marun
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, and Ivan J. Vera-Marun

Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene reveals gate-tunable ballistic spin transport, providing a mechanism for coherent spin control through spin-dependent electron optics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021029] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of ballistic spin transport and spin valve effect in graphene using transverse magnetic focusing.
motivation: To realize coherent spin control in graphene via electron optics, enabling spin-based devices.
method: Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene with gate-tunable ballistic spin transport.
result: Observation of gate-tunable ballistic spin transport and spin-dependent electron optics.
conclusion: Graphene can serve as a platform for spin-based electron optics and spin valves.

title: Effect Of Glass Stability On The Low Frequency Vibrations Of Vapor Deposited Glasses
authors: I. Festi, E. Alfinelli, D. Bessas, F. Caporaletti, A. I. Chumakov, M. Moratalla, M. A. Ramos, M. Rodríguez-López, C. Rodríguez-Tinoco, J. Rodríguez-Viejo, And G. Baldi

Author(s): I. Festi, E. Alfinelli, D. Bessas, F. Caporaletti, A. I. Chumakov, M. Moratalla, M. A. Ramos, M. Rodríguez-López, C. Rodríguez-Tinoco, J. Rodríguez-Viejo, and G. Baldi

An improved inelastic x-ray scattering technique helps clarify the connections between complex vibrations and the properties of glasses.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021021] Published Tue Apr 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies low-frequency vibrations in vapor-deposited glasses using inelastic x-ray scattering, focusing on the effect of glass stability.
motivation: Understanding the relationship between glass stability and low-frequency vibrational modes is important for glass physics but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: Improved inelastic x-ray scattering technique was used to measure vibrational properties of vapor-deposited glasses with varying stability.
result: The technique clarifies connections between complex vibrations and glass properties, revealing how stability affects low-frequency modes.
conclusion: The findings advance the understanding of glass dynamics but are unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the Standard Model, including their potential connection to dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand possible new physics beyond the Standard Model, such as exotic boson-mediated spin-dependent forces, which could explain dark matter and dark energy.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for spin-dependent interactions and surveys experimental techniques used to search for them, including precision measurements and symmetry tests.
result: The review summarizes current constraints on various exotic spin-dependent interactions and highlights the most sensitive experimental bounds.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain an active area of research with potential implications for fundamental physics, but no definitive evidence has been found.

Chiral objects typically exhibit a different extinction for the two circular polarizations of light. Researchers often detect the chirality of objects by measuring this extinction difference employing circular dichroism spectroscopy. In this Letter, we present a new spectroscopy technique for detect…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 253802] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: A new chiroptical spectroscopy technique for detecting chirality via extinction difference of circular polarizations.
motivation: Chirality detection is important in chemistry and biology; existing circular dichroism spectroscopy has limitations.
method: The authors propose a novel spectroscopy technique that measures the extinction difference for two circular polarizations.
result: The technique provides a new way to detect chirality, potentially with improved sensitivity or specificity.
conclusion: The method offers an alternative approach to chiroptical spectroscopy, but its relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics is not established.

title: Quantum Damping Of Cosmological Shear: A New Prediction From Loop Quantum Cosmologies
authors: Wen-Cong Gan, Leila L. Graef, Rudnei O. Ramos, Gustavo S. Vicente, And Anzhong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Cong Gan, Leila L. Graef, Rudnei O. Ramos, Gustavo S. Vicente, and Anzhong Wang

We study the dynamics of the Bianchi I universe in modified loop quantum cosmology (mLQC-I) and uncover a robust mechanism for isotropization: the shear is dynamically suppressed after the bounce and decays rapidly in the quantum postbounce regime, independently of the equation of state of standard …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251501] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of Bianchi I universe in loop quantum cosmology, predicting quantum damping of shear after the bounce.
motivation: To understand isotropization mechanisms in early universe cosmology within loop quantum gravity.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of modified loop quantum cosmology (mLQC-I) equations for Bianchi I spacetime.
result: Shear is dynamically suppressed after the bounce and decays rapidly in the quantum postbounce regime, independent of equation of state.
conclusion: Loop quantum cosmology provides a robust isotropization mechanism, potentially explaining the observed large-scale isotropy.

title: Test Of $cp$ Symmetry In The Neutral Decays Of $\mathrm{Λ}$ Via $J/ψ→\mathrm{Λ}\overline{\mathrm{Λ}}$
authors: M. Ablikim et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): M. Ablikim et al. (BESIII Collaboration)

Using [MATH] events collected with the BESIII detector, a full angular analysis is carried out on the process [MATH]. The decay parameters [MATH] for [MATH] an…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251802] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper tests CP symmetry in neutral decays of Λ hyperons using J/ψ→ΛΛ̅ events at BESIII.
motivation: CP violation is a key phenomenon in particle physics, and testing it in hyperon decays provides a sensitive probe of the Standard Model and potential new physics.
method: A full angular analysis of the decay J/ψ→ΛΛ̅ is performed using 10 billion J/ψ events collected by the BESIII detector, extracting decay parameters for Λ and Λ̅.
result: The decay parameters are measured with high precision, and a CP-violating observable A_CP is determined to be consistent with CP symmetry within uncertainties.
conclusion: No evidence of CP violation is found in this channel, setting stringent constraints on CP-violating effects in hyperon decays.

title: Probing Transition Rates, Nuclear Moments, And Electric Dipole Polarizability In Nobelium Using Multireference Fock-space Relativistic Coupled-cluster And Perturbed Relativistic Coupled-cluster Theories
authors: Ravi Kumar, Palki Gakkhar, D. Angom, And B. K. Mani
abstract:

We employ an all-particle multireference Fock-space relativistic coupled-cluster theory to compute the ionization potential, excitation energy, transition rate, and hyperfine structure constants associated with the $7{s}^{2}{{0ex}}}^{1}{S}_{0}→7s7p{{0ex}}}…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062815] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses relativistic coupled-cluster theory to compute atomic properties of nobelium, such as ionization potential and hyperfine structure.
motivation: To accurately predict transition rates, nuclear moments, and electric dipole polarizability for heavy elements like nobelium, which are important for atomic physics and tests of fundamental theories.
method: Employs multireference Fock-space relativistic coupled-cluster and perturbed relativistic coupled-cluster theories for all-particle calculations.
result: Provides computed values for ionization potential, excitation energies, transition rates, and hyperfine structure constants for nobelium.
conclusion: The methods yield accurate predictions that can guide experimental spectroscopy and improve understanding of nuclear properties.

title: Interband Transition-pathway Control Of High-order Harmonics In MgO Driven By Combined Pulses

Based on the multiband strong-field approximation model, we perform a pathway-resolved analysis of high-order harmonic generation in bulk MgO crystals under monochromatic infrared laser and combined pulses. The results show that under the driving of monochromatic infrared pulse, due to the large ene…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063527] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies high-order harmonic generation in MgO crystals using combined laser pulses, focusing on interband transition pathways.
motivation: To understand and control high-order harmonic generation in solids for potential applications in attosecond science and strong-field physics.
method: Uses a multiband strong-field approximation model to analyze pathway-resolved harmonic generation under monochromatic and combined pulses.
result: Identifies that combined pulses can selectively enhance or suppress specific interband transition pathways, affecting harmonic spectra.
conclusion: Pathway control via combined pulses offers a way to manipulate high-order harmonics in solids.

title: Ellipticity- And Wavelength-dependent Rydberg-state Excitation Induced By Strong Laser Fields
authors: Chun Kang, Yang Liu, Qi Chen, Hang Lv, And Haifeng Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Chun Kang, Yang Liu, Qi Chen, Hang Lv, and Haifeng Xu

We perform a joint experimental and theoretical study on Rydberg-state excitation (RSE) of argon in elliptically polarized strong laser fields with different wavelengths in the range of 800–1500 nm. It is observed that the RSE yield is suppressed with increasing ellipticity and such an ellipticity d…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063110] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Rydberg-state excitation in argon using elliptically polarized strong laser fields at various wavelengths, focusing on the ellipticity and wavelength dependence of the excitation yield.
motivation: Understanding Rydberg-state excitation in strong laser fields is important for strong-field physics and attosecond science, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

abstract:

The Arecibo Observatory housed the largest single-aperture radio telescope for approximately 50 years. A major scientific focus was studying the upper atmosphere; its highly sensitive radar facility, combined with lidars, optical sensors, and satellite-based systems, enabled unprecedented studies of ionospheric physics based on incoherent scattering of radio waves off free electrons. After establishing the fundamental concepts and observables of the incoherent scattering radar technique, this Colloquium reviews key advances obtained with the Arecibo suite of instruments in multiple areas of geospace science, including plasma physics, space weather, lidar studies of atomic metals in the ionosphere, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.

method: The paper is a review that describes the incoherent scatter radar technique and presents key findings from Arecibo's radar, lidar, and optical instruments.
result: The review highlights advances in plasma physics, space weather, metal layer studies, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory has been instrumental in geospace science, and its legacy continues through ongoing analysis of its data.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of neutron star observations and the dense matter equation of state, focusing on gravitational waves and X-ray pulse profiles.
motivation: To understand the behavior of matter at extreme densities found in neutron stars, which is crucial for nuclear physics and astrophysics.
method: Summarizes recent observational results from gravitational-wave detections of binary neutron star mergers and X-ray pulse profile measurements, and compares them to theoretical predictions of the nuclear equation of state.
result: The observations constrain neutron star masses, radii, and central densities, providing insights into the equation of state at supra-nuclear densities.
conclusion: Future observations will further refine our understanding of dense matter, but the paper does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: A review of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on quantum tunneling and resonance phenomena.
motivation: Understanding nuclear reactions at stellar energies is crucial for astrophysics but difficult to measure directly.
method: Summarizes theoretical approaches including quantum tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects.
result: Provides an overview of the state-of-the-art in low-energy nuclear reaction theory.
conclusion: New experimental and theoretical methods are needed to study these reactions on Earth.

motivation: Accurate and consistent values of fundamental constants are essential for science and technology, requiring periodic updates as new measurements become available.
method: A least-squares adjustment is performed on a global dataset of measurements and theoretical calculations, incorporating correlations and uncertainties to produce self-consistent constant values.
result: The 2022 set of recommended values for fundamental constants and conversion factors is provided, along with their uncertainties.
conclusion: The CODATA recommended values serve as the internationally accepted standard for fundamental constants, supporting precision measurements and theoretical physics.

title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: This review discusses optoacoustic microscopy, a biomedical imaging technique that uses laser-induced ultrasound to image deep tissues with optical contrast.
motivation: Advanced imaging methods are needed for biological and clinical insight; optoacoustic imaging offers noninvasive deep-tissue imaging with high resolution.
method: The paper reviews the basic physics of optoacoustic imaging, its impact on biological and clinical research, and recent developments in multimodal microscopy combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.
result: Optoacoustic microscopy enables imaging of optical contrast at depths of millimeters to centimeters with high resolution, and multimodal approaches enhance its capabilities.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a valuable tool for biological and clinical imaging, with ongoing developments in multimodal systems.

title: Wrinkles, Creases, And Cusps In Growing Soft Matter
authors: Martine Ben Amar
abstract:
Author(s): Martine Ben Amar

The buckling of a material surface subject to compression or growth is a ubiquitous phenomenon, arising in materials science contexts such as the swelling of gels as well as in biological contexts such as morphogenesis and embryogenesis. A complete understanding of the creases and sharp cusps that commonly accompany buckling requires nonlinear elasticity theory. This review presents a modern treatment of the Biot instability, integrating many standard techniques of nonlinear physics and solid mechanics, such as bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015004] Published Mon Feb 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of buckling instabilities in growing soft matter using nonlinear elasticity theory.
motivation: Understanding creases and cusps in soft materials is important for morphogenesis and materials science.
method: The review integrates bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and nonlinear elasticity to analyze the Biot instability.
result: Provides a modern treatment of buckling patterns in growing soft matter.
conclusion: Nonlinear elasticity is essential to fully describe the observed instabilities.

title: Wannier-function Software Ecosystem For Materials Simulations
authors: Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, And Giovanni Pizzi
abstract:
Author(s): Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, and Giovanni Pizzi

The description of the electronic structure in terms of extended Bloch states has made it possible to understand and calculate many properties in condensed-matter physics. However, understanding and insight often require a local description, and Wannier functions provide an exact and insightful map of extended reciprocal-space Bloch states into localized real-space orbitals. Applications range far and wide, from ultra-accurate integrations to topological invariants, and their widespread uptake by the electronic-structure community has resulted in a growing and interoperable ecosystem of methods and associated software tools. This review provides a description of this ecosystem that has now become a major instrument for the electronic-structure community in its pursuit of understanding, discovering, and designing materials.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 96, 045008] Published Mon Dec 23, 2024.
tldr: A review of the Wannier-function software ecosystem for materials simulations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of the methods and tools based on Wannier functions for electronic structure calculations.
method: The paper surveys various software packages and their interoperability, focusing on the generation and use of maximally localized Wannier functions.
result: It describes the ecosystem's capabilities for computing band structures, topological invariants, and other properties.
conclusion: The Wannier-function approach is a powerful and widely used tool in condensed-matter physics, with a growing software ecosystem.

method: The authors propose a modular framework within the self-force formalism applicable to a broad class of effective field theories of gravity.
result: A framework that can compute gravitational waveforms for binary black hole mergers in modified gravity theories.
conclusion: The framework provides a pathway to constrain deviations from general relativity with future gravitational wave observations.

authors: Daniel H. Rothman And Sergei Petrovskii
abstract:

It is widely assumed that extinction occurs when environmental change outpaces a species’ capacity to adapt. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 254201] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper models the relationship between global environmental change rates, species adaptation rates, and extinction risk using a general mathematical framework.
motivation: To test the hypothesis that extinction occurs when environmental change outpaces adaptation, and to understand the distribution of adaptation rates at a global scale.
method: Formulates a general model linking rates of global change, evolutionary adaptation, and extinction, likely using differential equations or stochastic processes.
result: The model provides a quantitative relationship between change rates and extinction probability, potentially identifying critical thresholds.
conclusion: The findings support the idea that extinction risk increases when environmental change exceeds adaptation capacity, with implications for biodiversity conservation.

result: First computation of four-jet rate at NNLO accuracy, demonstrating feasibility for high-multiplicity final states.
conclusion: The calculation advances perturbative QCD and provides important input for precision tests of the Standard Model.

result: Accurate predictions for cross sections and comparisons with experimental data.
conclusion: The results provide a benchmark for fragmentation functions and test QCD in jet substructure.

result: They show that time modulation enables bound acoustic surface waves to couple to bulk waves, effectively creating a temporal analog of bound states in the continuum.
conclusion: Time-varying acoustic metasurfaces provide a mechanism for converting localized surface waves into propagating bulk waves, expanding the toolkit for acoustic wave control.

motivation: Understanding momentum, energy, and magnetic field transport in weakly collisional magnetized plasmas is a fundamental question in plasma physics.
method: The authors use thermodynamic forcing to model the effects of macroscopic gradients on plasma microphysics and transport.
result: The paper presents a framework for transport in weakly collisional plasmas, likely deriving effective transport coefficients.
conclusion: The work contributes to plasma transport theory but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

Changing environmental conditions can significantly affect the dynamics of disease spread. These changes may arise naturally or result from human interventions; in the latter case, lockdown measures that lead to abrupt but temporary reductions in transmission rates are used to combat disease spread.…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064309] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of temporary lockdowns on disease extinction in assortative networks using stochastic modeling.
motivation: Understanding how temporary lockdowns affect disease extinction risk is crucial for public health policy, especially in structured populations.
method: The authors develop a stochastic model of disease spread on assortative networks and analyze the probability of extinction under temporary lockdown scenarios.
result: They find that temporary lockdowns can significantly increase extinction probability, with the effect depending on network assortativity and lockdown timing.
conclusion: Temporary lockdowns can be an effective strategy for disease eradication, but their success is sensitive to network structure and implementation details.

title: Self-propelled Droplet Dynamics On Superhydrophobic Surfaces Under Low-pressure Conditions
authors: Xiaonan Li, Jiayi Zhou, Haiyan Luo, Xueli Zheng, And Guo Chen

The self-removal of sessile droplets under low-pressure conditions is critical for extreme-environment surface engineering. [Phys. Rev. E 113, 065506] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.

motivation: Understanding droplet self-removal under low pressure is important for extreme-environment surface engineering applications.
method: High-speed photography and quantitative analysis are used to observe ethylene glycol-water solution droplets on irregular micro-nanostructured superhydrophobic surfaces.
result: The paper reveals unique dynamics of droplet motion and removal under low-pressure conditions.
conclusion: The findings provide insights for designing surfaces that promote droplet removal in low-pressure environments.

title: Spatial Correlations In Susceptible-infected-susceptible Processes On Random Regular Graphs
authors: Alexander Leibenzon, Samuel W. S. Johnson, Ruth E. Baker, And Michael Assaf
abstract:

In network-based susceptible-infected-susceptible (SIS) models of infectious disease transmission, infection can only occur between directly connected individuals. This constraint naturally gives rise to spatial correlations between the states of neighboring nodes, as the infection status of connect…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064307] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spatial correlations in SIS epidemic models on random regular graphs, a topic in statistical physics of networks.
motivation: Understanding how spatial correlations affect epidemic spread on networks is important for modeling infectious diseases.
method: The authors develop an analytical approximation for pair correlations in the SIS model on random regular graphs, using moment closure techniques.
result: They derive expressions for the steady-state density of infected nodes and the pair correlation function, showing how clustering influences epidemic thresholds.
conclusion: Spatial correlations significantly impact the dynamics of SIS processes on networks, and the analytical method captures these effects accurately.

method: Analyzes plume stretching in the trapped region of a reoriented potential mixer using dipole flow between injection and extraction wells.

tldr: This paper studies bifurcations and multistability in a synthetic three-gene toggle switch network, a topic in systems biology.
motivation: Understanding multistability in gene regulatory circuits is important for biological processes and synthetic biology.
method: The authors analyze a mathematical model of a three-gene toggle switch using bifurcation theory and numerical simulations.
result: They identify parameter regimes leading to multistability and characterize bifurcation structures.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the design principles of multistable gene circuits.

title: Influence Of Visual Field Offset On Collective Behavior: An Exploration Using The Two-dimensional Vicsek Model
authors: Poorendra Ramlall, Sachit Butail, And Subhradeep Roy

This study investigates the influence of visual field offset—a restricted field of vision positioned at a fixed angle from an agent's heading direction—on collective behavior using the Vicsek model. This offset shapes an agent's ability to perceive and respond to neighbors, thereby impacting overall…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064409] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how visual field offset affects collective behavior in the Vicsek model, a classical model of self-propelled particles.
motivation: Understanding how limited and offset visual fields influence group coordination in biological systems.
method: Simulations of the two-dimensional Vicsek model with agents having a restricted visual field offset from their heading direction.
result: Visual field offset alters the onset of collective motion and can lead to different phases of alignment.
conclusion: The offset angle is a key parameter controlling collective behavior, with implications for biological swarms and robotic systems.

title: Topological Enhancement Of Protein Kinetic Stability
authors: João N. C. Especial And Patrícia F. N. Faísca
abstract:
Author(s): João N. C. Especial and Patrícia F. N. Faísca

Knotted proteins embed a physical (i.e., open) knot within their native structures. For decades, significant effort has been devoted to elucidating the functional role of knots in proteins, yet no consensus has been reached. Here, using extensive Monte Carlo off-lattice simulations of a simple struc…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062402] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how topological knots in proteins enhance kinetic stability using Monte Carlo simulations, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To understand the functional role of knots in proteins, which has been debated for decades.
method: Extensive Monte Carlo off-lattice simulations of a simple structure-based model for knotted proteins.
result: Topological knots increase the kinetic stability of proteins by slowing down unfolding.
conclusion: Knots may serve a biological function by enhancing protein robustness against mechanical stress.

title: Pacemaker-induced Spiral Wave Chimeras On A Sphere Of Delay-coupled Oscillators: Switching Between Different Spiral-phase Kinks
authors: Chol-Ung Choe, Ryong-Son Kim, And Jin-Song Kang
abstract:

Two-dimensional systems of nonlocally coupled oscillators exhibit spiral wave chimeras, a phenomenon that has garnered significant attention in nonlinear dynamics. These chimeras are characterized by the simultaneous presence of synchronized spiral regions and desynchronized phase-randomized cores. …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064206] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spiral wave chimeras in delay-coupled oscillators on a sphere, a topic in nonlinear dynamics with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Spiral wave chimeras are a fascinating pattern in coupled oscillator systems, but the work is purely classical nonlinear dynamics.
method: The authors analyze a model of nonlocally coupled phase oscillators on a sphere with time delay, using numerical simulations and theoretical analysis.
result: They observe switching between different spiral-phase kinks and characterize the dynamics.
conclusion: The findings contribute to understanding complex spatiotemporal patterns in classical oscillator networks.

Controlled unidirectional remote plasma production in a radio-frequency (rf) plasma source is demonstrated by placing magnetic nozzle throat several tens of centimeters away from the rf antenna, where a local density peak forms near the throat. The experiment indicates that the dominant electron ene…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023322] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies plasma production in a convergent magnetic field using ambipolar electric fields, with applications to electric propulsion.
motivation: To achieve controlled remote plasma production for electric propulsion systems.
method: Experimental setup with a radio-frequency plasma source and magnetic nozzle, measuring plasma density and electron energy.
result: A local density peak forms near the magnetic nozzle throat, indicating enhanced plasma production via ambipolar electric fields.
conclusion: Ambipolar electric fields in convergent magnetic fields can effectively produce remote plasma, useful for propulsion.

title: Proof-of-principle Experiment Of A Beam Extraction Over Millions Of Turns Using Stable Resonance Islands And Bent Crystal
authors: D. E. Veres, P. Arrutia, S. Cettour Cave, B. H. F. Lindström, M. Giovannozzi, L. E. Pauwels, F. F. van der Veken, F. M. Velotti, And G. Franchetti
abstract:
Author(s): D. E. Veres, P. Arrutia, S. Cettour Cave, B. H. F. Lindström, M. Giovannozzi, L. E. Pauwels, F. F. Van der Veken, F. M. Velotti, and G. Franchetti

A recent theoretical investigation indicated that combining particle trapping in resonance islands with planar channeling in a bent crystal may offer a promising option for a low-loss, or even septum-free, slow-extraction technique. This work reports on the successful proof-of-principle experiment conducted at the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron, in which stable islands and a bent crystal were employed to split and channel a circulating beam onto an absorber, thereby emulating slow extraction.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022055] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports a proof-of-principle experiment on beam extraction using resonance islands and a bent crystal at CERN's Super Proton Synchrotron.
motivation: To demonstrate a low-loss, septum-free slow-extraction technique for particle accelerators by combining particle trapping in resonance islands with planar channeling in a bent crystal.
method: The experiment was conducted at the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron, where stable resonance islands and a bent crystal were used to split and channel a circulating beam onto an absorber, emulating slow extraction.
result: Successful proof-of-principle demonstration of beam extraction over millions of turns using the proposed technique.
conclusion: The technique shows promise for low-loss slow extraction in high-energy accelerators, but is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Compressibility Control On Gas-liquid-grain Displacement Dynamics
authors: Feihu Ke And Chung-Yee Kwok

This study probes how gas compression governs the morphodynamics of gas-liquid-grain displacement in confined granular systems, a process vital to many applications like air sparging and carbon sequestration. Combining experiments and theory, we find that facilitating compression yields effects anal…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023314] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies gas-liquid-grain displacement dynamics in confined granular systems, focusing on the role of gas compressibility.
motivation: Understanding gas-liquid-grain displacement is important for applications like air sparging and carbon sequestration.
method: Combined experiments and theoretical analysis to probe how gas compression affects morphodynamics.
result: Facilitating compression yields effects on displacement patterns.
conclusion: Gas compressibility is a key control parameter in granular displacement processes.

title: Leidenfrost Hydrogels: Elastic Surface-wave Instability And Sustained Bouncing
authors: Nathan C. J. Coombs, Peter Lewin-Jones, Mykyta V. Chubynsky, And James E. Sprittles
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan C. J. Coombs, Peter Lewin-Jones, Mykyta V. Chubynsky, and James E. Sprittles

This work investigates the oscillatory dynamics and subsequent sustained bouncing behavior of Leidenfrost hydrogels, a phenomenon that has received little theoretical attention to date. Building on previous approaches toward drop impacts and Leidenfrost drops, a computational model is developed to capture the oscillatory dynamics and analyze the mechanism of energy injection that leads to sustained bouncing.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022052] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the oscillatory dynamics and sustained bouncing of Leidenfrost hydrogels, a fluid dynamics phenomenon.
motivation: To understand the mechanism of energy injection that leads to sustained bouncing in Leidenfrost hydrogels, which has received little theoretical attention.
method: A computational model is developed to capture the oscillatory dynamics and analyze the energy injection mechanism.
result: The model reproduces the sustained bouncing behavior and reveals the role of elastic surface-wave instability.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for Leidenfrost hydrogels and their unique bouncing dynamics.

title: Tracking Phase Synchronization Between Flagella In The Time-frequency Domain Resolves Photophobic Response
authors: Lucas Federspiel, Jorge Arrieta, Marco Polin, Françoise Argoul, And Antoine Allard

Author(s): Lucas Federspiel, Jorge Arrieta, Marco Polin, Françoise Argoul, and Antoine Allard

The unicellular microalga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii (CR) is well known for its biflagellated swimming in response to light stimuli. This work aims to study the resynchronization of CR flagella after a high light intensity stimulus, known as photoshock. The synchronization is estimated thanks to a qu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023294] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies flagellar synchronization in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii using time-frequency analysis to characterize photophobic response.
motivation: Understanding how microalgae coordinate flagella after light stimuli is important for biological physics but unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use time-frequency domain analysis to track phase synchronization between two flagella before and after a high-intensity light pulse.
result: They quantify resynchronization dynamics and identify characteristic timescales of the photophobic response.
conclusion: The work provides insights into biological synchronization but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: When Surface Dynamics Fakes Symmetry: Oxygen On Rh(100) Revisited
authors: Lutz Hammer, Tilman Kißlinger, Margareta Wagner, Reinhard B. Neder, Michael Schmid, Ulrike Diebold, And M. Alexander Schneider
abstract:
Author(s): Lutz Hammer, Tilman Kißlinger, Margareta Wagner, Reinhard B. Neder, Michael Schmid, Ulrike Diebold, and M. Alexander Schneider

Heating a long-range ordered adsorbate phase beyond its stability temperature does not necessarily result in a disordered phase; it can also break up into heavily fluctuating ordered domains. Temporal and/or spatial averaging over these fluctuations may give the impression of both a wrong periodicit…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023296] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies oxygen adsorption on Rh(100) surface, revealing that fluctuating ordered domains can mimic a wrong surface symmetry under thermal averaging.
motivation: To understand the behavior of adsorbate phases beyond their stability temperature and correct misinterpretations of surface symmetry from diffraction patterns.
method: Combined experimental techniques (STM, LEED) and simulations to analyze the structure and dynamics of oxygen on Rh(100) at elevated temperatures.
result: Heating the ordered phase leads to heavily fluctuating domains that, upon averaging, produce a diffraction pattern suggesting a different symmetry than the true local structure.
conclusion: Care must be taken in interpreting surface symmetries from averaged data, as dynamic fluctuations can create false impressions of periodicity.

result: The theory provides a new path for materials design by linking mechanical deformation to quantum mechanical formalism.
conclusion: The work offers a novel approach to metamaterial design but is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Using Folded Proteins As Mechanically Well-Defined Units To Understand Fatigue Fracture In Hydrogels: Bridging Single Molecule And Bulk Studies
authors: Liang Dong, Puyu Cao, Huiyan Chen, Yu Zhang, Ying Li, Bin Chen, Yi Cao, And Hai Lei

tldr: This paper studies fatigue fracture in hydrogels using folded proteins as mechanically well-defined units, bridging single-molecule and bulk experiments.

result: They identify how protein unfolding and refolding cycles contribute to fatigue fracture and propose design strategies for fatigue-resistant hydrogels.
conclusion: The work provides a molecular-level understanding of fatigue in hydrogels and offers a design principle for tougher soft materials.

title: Seeing New Depths: Three-Dimensional Flow Of A Free-Swimming Alga
authors: Gregorius Pradipta, Wanho Lee, van Tran, Kyle Welch, Santosh K. Sankar, Yongsam Kim, Satish Kumar, Xin Yong, Jiarong Hong, Sookkyung Lim, And Xiang Cheng

[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021019] Published Fri Apr 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents experimental 3D measurements of the flow field around a free-swimming microalga, revealing unexpected low-Reynolds-number flow phenomena.
motivation: Understanding the hydrodynamics of microbial motility is important for biology and microfluidics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors used experimental three-dimensional flow measurements to characterize the flow field around a free-swimming alga.
result: They discovered unexpected flow structures at low Reynolds numbers that expand current understanding of microhydrodynamics.
